articles.title: Après les ventilateurs, Dreo passe au chauffage et prépare une IA pour aider à réduire la facture d’électricité
articles.text:
À la sortie d'un été marqué par le succès de ses ventilateurs, Dreo veut désormais s’installer dans nos maisons toute l’année. La marque lance deux chauffages connectés et un purificateur d’air, avant l’arrivée d’une IA capable de coordonner ses appareils pour améliorer le confort et maîtriser la consommation électrique.
Dreo ne compte pas quitter nos salons avec la fin de l’été. Le fabricant, qui s’est fait connaître en France grâce à ses ventilateurs, présentait ce 23 septembre trois nouveaux appareils pour affronter les mois les plus froids de l'année : les chauffages 720S et 711S, ainsi que le purificateur d’air 530S, déjà aperçu à l’IFA. Tous peuvent être commandés dès maintenant, à des tarifs compris entre 120 et 150 euros, mais les expéditions du 711S ne commenceront que le 28 septembre.
La marque a de bonnes raisons de vouloir prolonger l’aventure. Officiellement arrivée en France en avril, après une phase de test en 2025, elle revendique 180 000 ventilateurs vendus sur Amazon France au 21 septembre, dont 45% au seul mois de juin selon Hugo Esquenet, directeur marketing de la marque en France. Lors de sa présentation à la presse, Dreo a également mis en avant ses premières places dans plusieurs catégories sur Amazon, notamment les ventilateurs aux États-Unis et les chauffages d’appoint au Royaume-Uni.
Deux chauffages pour réchauffer une pièce ou simplement son occupant
Le 720S, proposé à 120 euros, possède une particularité intéressante : sa partie supérieure peut changer de position pour modifier la diffusion de la chaleur. Abaissée, elle dirige le souffle vers une zone précise, par exemple lorsqu’on travaille à son bureau. Relevée, elle répartit l’air chaud à 360° pour couvrir une pièce de 15 à 25 m², selon Dreo.
Le fabricant promet également un fonctionnement pouvant descendre à 25 dB, ainsi qu’un arrêt automatique en cas de basculement accidentel et une protection contre la surchauffe.
Le 711S prend le problème autrement. Vendu 150 euros, il utilise la convection naturelle. L’air froid entre par le bas, se réchauffe puis ressort par le haut, sans ventilateur. De quoi éviter le bruit de soufflerie dans une chambre ou un bureau. Sa façade en verre trempé soigne la présentation et l’appareil peut être fixé au mur pour libérer de la place au sol.
Les deux modèles développent jusqu’à 2 000 watts et disposent d’un mode économique qui module leur puissance à l’approche de la température demandée. Dreo revendique ainsi jusqu’à 40% de consommation en moins par rapport à un fonctionnement continu à pleine puissance. L’économie éventuelle vient donc de la régulation et du temps de fonctionnement réduit, pas d’un meilleur rendement de la résistance électrique.
Ces deux chauffages retrouvent surtout l’application Dreo, dont nous avions apprécié la simplicité et la clarté lors de nos tests de ventilateurs au printemps, les TurboCool 516S et 765S. Avec plusieurs chauffages installés, on peut régler indépendamment la température de chaque pièce, pour garder le bureau au chaud pendant le télétravail tout en chauffant moins la chambre, par exemple.
Les utilisateurs déjà équipés retrouvent ainsi leurs appareils dans une interface familière, sans multiplier les applications. Un confort d’usage qui compte au quotidien et donne davantage d’intérêt à la partie connectée qu’une simple télécommande supplémentaire.
Un purificateur qui ajuste son fonctionnement à la qualité de l’air
Le troisième appareil, le 530S, s’attaque aux poussières, aux particules fines et aux odeurs. Ce purificateur à 140 euros associe un préfiltre, un filtre à particules et du charbon actif, avec un capteur PM2,5 chargé d’adapter automatiquement la ventilation.
Un voyant coloré donne une indication immédiate de la qualité de l’air tandis que l’application permet de programmer l’appareil et de suivre l’usure de son filtre principal. Selon Dreo, ce dernier capture 99,97% des particules en suspension de 0,3 µm, conformément au protocole IEST, dont les particules fines PM2,5.
Le fabricant annonce un débit d’air purifié de 221 m³/h, soit l’équivalent de 4,8 volumes d’air filtrés par heure dans une pièce de 19 m². Cela peut compléter l’aération du logement, mais certainement pas la remplacer.
En 2027, une IA pour faire travailler tous ces appareils ensemble
La nouveauté la plus intéressante pourrait toutefois arriver un peu plus tard. Dreo prépare Air Intelligence, un système destiné à coordonner ses chauffages, ventilateurs, purificateurs et autres appareils compatibles. L’équipe française vise un lancement au minimum en 2027.
Plutôt que de régler chaque produit séparément, l’utilisateur pourrait ainsi laisser l’IA croiser leurs mesures avec la météo, la pollution extérieure ou, encore, les niveaux de pollen. Température, humidité et circulation de l’air serviraient notamment à évaluer le confort ressenti dans le logement, résumé par un score sur 100.
L’autre promesse concerne le portefeuille. L’application doit suivre la consommation des appareils et estimer les économies possibles, en kilowattheures comme en euros. Elle pourrait, par exemple, indiquer combien vous économiseriez en baissant le chauffage d’un degré. Vous choisiriez ensuite d’appliquer ce réglage ou de conserver votre température habituelle.
Toujours côté domotique, Dreo travaille également à rendre ses nouveaux chauffages compatibles avec Matter. Air Intelligence doit ainsi pouvoir dialoguer avec certains équipements d’autres marques, mais le calendrier et la liste des produits pris en charge restent à préciser.

articles.title: Instinct aún no factura ni un dólar pero está a punto de valer 10.000 millones. Lo que vende es la pereza que nos dará dejarlo
articles.text:
Planet Fitness se ha dejado un 19% en bolsa esta semana y The New York Times, un 16%. Ninguno ha presentado malos resultados que expliquen una caída tan grande en tan poco tiempo. Lo que ha pasado es que Meta ha lanzado una aplicación.
Los inversores temen que Muse se convierta en un comparador gigante que facilite a los usuarios encontrar alternativas más baratas y debilite la lealtad que los retiene con sus proveedores. Grandes bancos americanos como JPMorgan y Wells Fargo han caído más de un 3%, Charles Schwab casi un 5%, y Booking y TripAdvisor más de un 6%.
Que el gimnasio sea el gran damnificado tiene todo el sentido. Es el ejemplo de manual de un negocio que se sostiene sobre cuotas que la gente sigue pagando porque el proceso de darse de baja da pereza y lo vamos postergando.
El mercado ha entendido la mitad de la historia. La otra mitad se llama Instinct.
Un agente sin pintas de agente
Instinct es obra de Noah Shinn, de 23 años. Antes fue investigador en Sierra, la empresa que construye agentes de atención al cliente para otras empresas. Es decir, pasó de programar al agente que te atiende a programar al que envías a discutir con él.
Su valoración ha pasado de 50 millones de dólares a 2.500 millones en cuatro meses, y ya está en conversaciones para buscar otra ronda de financiación a una valoración de 10.000 millones. Recordemos que todavía es gratis. No tiene forma de monetizarse aún. Está en la fase de crecimiento y en cuanto lo pruebas es evidente por qué.
Una parte de la explicación de ese entusiasmo es su forma: Instinct no tiene interfaz propia. Le escribes o le llamas por iMessage, WhatsApp, SMS o teléfono, y detrás hay un ordenador en la nube que sigue trabajando entre mensaje y mensaje. Es un OpenClaw ultrasimplificado.
Hasta hace nada, tener un agente personal exigía montarse ese OpenClaw o un Hermes, configurar las credenciales y aceptar que aquello era también un hobby para usuarios avanzados. Instinct ha convertido todo eso en un contacto más de WhatsApp al que le pides cualquier cosa y ya vais viendo. Por eso creo que es el primer agente de este tipo que escala de verdad. Muse lo ha hecho también, pero solo está disponible en Estados Unidos. A mi alrededor, en España, estoy viendo a bastante gente sin un perfil técnico avanzado empezar a usar Instinct. No es un fenómeno estadístico, pero sí una señal: cuando el agente vive donde ya hablas con familia y amigos, no hay que aprender nada nuevo.
Y un agente sin pereza
Todos tenemos un umbral a partir del cual preferimos palmar pasta antes que perder la tarde. Ese trámite burocrático infernal cuya recompensa "tampoco es tan grande". El agente no tiene ese umbral. Instinct sí puede pasarse una semana reclamando quince euros que no está claro por qué nos los cobraron, comparando seguros hasta encontrar el que nos cubre lo que nos interesa al mejor precio o persiguiendo un reembolso, sin cansarse y sin ofenderse.
Ahí está la amenaza para las telecos, las aseguradoras, las suscripciones y cualquier negocio cuyo margen dependa de que el cliente no revise la factura o sienta que no le compensa el esfuerzo. Esa desidia ha sido un activo contable al margen de cualquier balance. Y el siguiente paso ya se intuye: las empresas usando IA para atender, y los usuarios mandando a su propio agente a hablar con ella. Quien tenga el agente más capaz, y previsiblemente más caro, saldrá ganando.
Instinct es a su vez una paradoja: el agente que te ayuda a cambiar de aseguradora sin esfuerzo es, al mismo tiempo, el producto más difícil de abandonar que hayamos usado. Su valor no está en el modelo, sino en lo que acumula: tus preferencias, tus cuentas, tus tareas a medias, a quién respondes rápido y a quién no.
Cambiar de móvil no es demasiado incómodo porque la mayoría de datos migran del viejo al nuevo. Cambiar de agente obliga a enseñarle otra vez tu vida entera a otro. Por eso tiene sentido que hoy sea gratis: el precio se paga después, en forma de coste de salida.
No sé si los agentes matarán la economía de la inercia, pero desde luego pueden concentrarla. Vamos a pasar de estar atados a decenas de proveedores a estarlo a uno solo, que además es quien elige por nosotros entre todos los demás.

articles.title: Meta Connect 2026, des lunettes pour tous les usages et même un modèle sans caméra
articles.text:
Meta Connect 2026, des lunettes pour tous les usages et même un modèle sans caméra
C'est un véritable déluge d'annonces auquel s'est livrée Meta lors de sa conférence Connect annuelle, avec toute une gamme de nouvelles lunettes connectées et un appareil VR d'à peine 100 g, les Meta VR Glasses.
Cela fait presque deux ans que Meta n'avait plus sorti de matériel de réalité virtuelles. Le paradoxe vaut d'être souligné, tant l'entreprise écrase le secteur, avec plus de 50 % de parts de marché sur les casques. Le Meta Connect 2026 a mis fin à cette disette de façon assez spectaculaire, avec les Meta VR Glasses.
Des Meta VR Glasses cinq fois plus légères qu'un Quest 3
La vedette de la soirée tient dans une centaine de grammes. Les Meta VR Glasses ressemblent d'ailleurs davantage à de grosses lunettes qu'à un casque, avec un poids d'environ 100 g, soit un cinquième de celui d'un Quest 3. Le secret de cette cure d'amaigrissement se glisse dans la poche, sous la forme d'un puck de calcul filaire qui déporte l'essentiel de l'électronique.
Pas de manettes dans la boîte. Le pilotage repose sur le suivi des mains et du regard, avec l'agent Muse intégré directement au système d'exploitation. Un clavier virtuel complète l'ensemble et Mark Zuckerberg assure que son directeur technique y dépasse les 100 mots par minute, une performance évidemment invérifiable en l'état. Nous n'allons pas nous étendre ici sur ce produit dans la mesure où il a droit à son article dédié, qui contient aussi nos premières impressions.
Ray-Ban et Meta Glasses, la gamme se réorganise
Passons maintenant au cœur de l'offre actuelle de Meta, à savoir les lunettes intelligentes. Sur ce front, ce sont les Ray-Ban Meta Audio qui nous ont le plus étonnés. Elles inaugurent en effet une approche plus minimaliste. Jugez plutôt : pas de caméra, seulement du son, pour 43 g sur le nez et 12 heures d'autonomie (la meilleure de toutes les lunettes Meta), de quoi tenir une journée complète selon la marque. Deux styles distincts arriveront au lancement, déclinés en plusieurs coloris et au prix de départ de 349 €.
Les Ray-Ban Meta passent par ailleurs en troisième génération, avec des montures Wayfarer affinées, de nouveaux styles dont des aviateurs et un enregistrement audio en Dolby Atmos. Le tout à partir de 449 €.
Les Meta Glasses accueillent quant à elles le style Capri et une collaboration avec Lisa, du groupe BlackPink. Cerise sur le gâteau (pour les amateurs), chaque paire de cette édition sera vendue avec un charm différent en lien avec la chanteuse. La version Adventurer profite pour sa part d'une baisse de prix, à partir de 259 €.
Les Meta Display arrivent en France
De leur côté, les Meta Display s'exportent enfin. Désormais vendues en ligne et lancées à l'international, elles débarquent en France le 13 octobre, avec des précommandes ouvertes dès aujourd'hui. Au menu des nouveautés, deux fonctions photo, Dynamic Photo et Landscape Mode, ainsi qu'une capture audio en Dolby Atmos. Les hologrammes en pied y font également leur apparition. Comptez tout de même 899 € si vous souhaitez vous les procurer.
L'annonce la plus inattendue concerne l'audition. Hearing Enhancement transforme les lunettes en aide auditive en vente libre validée par la FDA, l'autorité sanitaire américaine, à destination des personnes malentendantes. La fonction se débloque moyennant un paiement unique de 149 dollars.
Muse s'invite partout
Mais s'il y a un mot-clé qui a irrigué toute la conférence, c'est bien "Muse". L'agent IA maison veut désormais agir dans le monde réel. Avec la permission de l'utilisateur, il peut acheter un article repéré à travers les lunettes en passant par Shopify, PayPal, Walmart, Best Buy, Instacart ou DoorDash. Il sait aussi piloter un Mac et dispose de sa propre adresse e-mail. Côté modèle économique, Meta prélève une commission sur les transactions traitées par l'agent, tout en offrant un volume conséquent de tokens. Pour rassurer sur la confidentialité, l'entreprise met en avant une Muse Security VM, une machine virtuelle privée qui stockerait les informations hors de portée de Meta, selon ses propres dires.
Un accessoire viendra compléter le dispositif pour les fêtes de fin d'année. Le Muse Charm, petit appareil de poche animé par un modèle vocal en temps réel, servira à converser avec l'agent et Meta promet d'en dire davantage d'ici décembre.

articles.title: Rayman Legends Retold's PC specs range from a GTX 1660 to an RTX 4080 – with upscaling throughout
articles.text:
In a nutshell: Do any developers release their games' PC system requirements without upscaling enabled these days? Based on the new Rayman Legends Retold reveal, it's become very rare. Once again, the game can run on a potato-like PC, and once again, the caveat is that upscaling is required at every level.
The good news for fans of the long-running platforming franchise is that the latest entry will play at 1080p@60FPS on an Intel Core i3-8100 or Ryzen 3 3100 paired with a GTX 1060, RX 5500 XT, or Intel Arc A580 and 8GB of RAM. However, graphics need to be set to the lowest preset and you still need upscaling (quality).
That quality upscaling setting is present in all four levels. Interestingly, the required hardware for the Recommended (1080p@60FPS with high graphics preset) and 2K (1440p@60FPS high preset) levels is pretty much identical. Only the AMD GPU (RX 5700 to an RX 6750 XT) and Intel GPU (Arc A750 to Arc B580) change.
Finally, the 4K ultra preset level is still quite demanding, considering this is a platformer (an admittedly pretty one) and upscaling is enabled. It asks for an RTX 4080 or Radeon RX 7900 XTX. The CPU requirements are more forgiving: a Core i5-9400 or Ryzen 5 3600.
The modest storage requirement is nice to see: 33GB of SSD space. That's around half of what's needed for The Blood of Dawnwalker, and almost 100GB less than Gears of War: E-Day.
Back in 2023, Remnant II set what was then considered a worrying precedent: it was the first PC game "designed with upscaling in mind."
While developers have avoided that kind of language since then, more games are adopting this thinking. Monster Hunter Wilds, Assassin's Creed Shadows, Rise of the Ronin, F1 25, DOOM: The Dark Ages, FBC: Firebreak, Mafia: The Old Country, Silent Hill f, Resident Evil Requiem, and Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced are just some that explicitly included upscaling in their published PC hardware requirements. Upcoming releases Gears of War: E-Day and Phantom Blade Zero have also included upscaling. Some titles, like The Blood of Dawnwalker, go out of their way to emphasize that upscaling is not part of the requirements.
Rayman Legends Retold is scheduled to release on PC and consoles on December 3, 2026. It had been set to launch on October 1, but Ubisoft delayed it to allow extra time for polish. It also allows the game to land after big releases like Gears of War, Call of Duty, and, of course, GTA 6.

articles.title: Micron discontinues 2GB GDDR7 chips for gaming GPUs as it pivots toward higher-density memory for AI — chipmaker reportedly pivots to high-margin 3GB silicon for AI GPUs
articles.text:
Micron discontinues 2GB GDDR7 chips for gaming GPUs as it pivots toward higher-density memory for AI — chipmaker reportedly pivots to high-margin 3GB silicon for AI GPUs
Samsung and SK Hynix already lead the 2GB GDDR7 market
Micron is reportedly pulling the plug on its 2 GB (16Gb) GDDR7 memory chips, ending production and sales of both the 28 Gbps and 32 Gbps variants. According to an X post by UNIKO’s Hardware, the chips — some of which shipped on some GeForce RTX 50 graphics cards — are now designated as “End of Life” on Micron's site. Tom’s Hardware can confirm that the pages for module norms return “No results found.”
Micron just began supplying its 2GB GDDR7 to Nvidia earlier this year, with Samsung and SK Hynix being the main GDDR7 suppliers. As a result, Micron's 2GB module only shipped on a few Nvidia models, such as retail variants of the GeForce RTX 5060. Samsung and SK Hynix cover the vast bulk of 2 GB GDDR7 modules for the standard RTX 50 retail lineup, so the risk of immediate shortages is minimal. Micron’s uncompetitive position in the 2 GB segment also appears to have made a fast exit logical to free up fabrication capacity.
The company is reportedly shifting its focus toward higher-density 3 GB (24 Gb) GDDR7 chips. These larger packages are considered impractical for Nvidia's RTX 50 lineup because they are more expensive and result in less conventional consumer memory capacities. However, they yield higher profit margins and are actively utilized in Nvidia's high-end RTX PRO Blackwell GPUs tailored for generative and agentic AI workloads.
Micron’s decision follows the ongoing trend of memory suppliers prioritizing AI-facing technologies over their consumer and retail counterparts. The company exited its Crucial consumer memory and SSD business earlier, explicitly saying that surging AI data-center demand had prompted it to prioritize larger strategic customers in faster-growing segments.

articles.title: Rachat de SFR : 5 000 emplois menacés d'ici 2029, les salariés en grève ce jeudi
articles.text:
Alors que le rachat de SFR pour quelque 20 milliards d’euros est acté depuis juin 2026, les conséquences sociales de l’opération commencent à se dessiner. Plusieurs actions se dessinent.
D’un côté, le CSE de l’entreprise, autrement dit les délégués du personnel, attaque les futurs propriétaires, à savoir les trois autres grands opérateurs historiques : Orange, Bouygues et Iliad (Free). De l’autre, on apprend dans Ouest France qu’une grève aura lieu ce jeudi 24 septembre 2026 dans l’après-midi à l’appel de l’intersyndicale regroupant l’Unsa, la CFDT et la CFTC.
« Colère et détermination »
Le motif de la grève est simple : il doit s’agir d’un « coup de semonce » d’après Olivier Lelong, délégué syndical central CFDT auprès de l’AFP et « faire entendre l’inquiétude » des salariés « leur colère et leur détermination ». « On va continuer le combat jusqu’à ce qu’ils reconsidèrent la situation », prévient Abdelkader Chourkane, élu du CSE et de l’UNsa.
Les futurs patrons ont assurés qu’ils garantiraient l’emploi des 8000 salariés de SFR jusqu’en 2029. Passée cette date, seuls environ 3000 d’entres eux conserveront leurs postes, dont une majorité chez Bouygues Telecom (2300 salariés), autour des 300 chez Orange et seulement 54 pour Free, qui récupère RED by SFR, la marque low cost de l’opérateur. Les délégués syndicaux affirment avoir déjà répertorié les boutiques qui devront fermer.
La grève intervient donc dans un contexte de négociation toujours en cours entre l’intersyndicale et les trois repreneurs. D’après Ouest France, une offre de reprise par salarié aurait été offerte, mais les syndicats souhaiteraient monter à trois offres par personne.
Une audience en référé doit avoir lieu ce matin au tribunal judiciaire de Paris juste avant la grève. Les syndicats tentent d’y obtenir davantage de documents sur la vente.

articles.title: UiPath introduces new workflow automation, software testing features - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
UiPath introduces new workflow automation, software testing features
UiPath Inc. is updating its namesake automation platform with more than a dozen new features designed to save time for knowledge workers.
The company debuted the enhancements today at its FUSION conference in Las Vegas. Many of the features are either available today or will launch next month.
The company’s platform uses artificial intelligence agents, scripts and third party applications to automate repetitive business work. It can also speed up technical tasks such as software testing. The company says more than 3 million developers use its platform to create automation workflows.
UiPath’s new feature lineup is headlined by a tool called Cartographer. It eases the first step of automation initiatives, which is determining how employees perform the manual task that a company wishes to speed up. The process can involve weeks of work. The reason is that companies must not only determine the typical manner in which employees perform a given task, but also how they respond to unusual developments and errors.
Cartographer automatically collects the necessary data. It then provides a ready-to-use automation workflow complete with features for measuring its effectiveness. Once the workflow is deployed in production, a feature called the Decision Ledger logs the actions that it performs. Enterprises can use that information to make accuracy enhancements.
“A process map tells you how work is designed to run,” said UiPath founder and Chief Executive Officer Daniel Dines. “UiPath Cartographer is the key to uncovering the operational knowledge of how that work actually runs, with every exception and every judgment call included. It’s the first product built to capture both and keep them in sync.”
Cartographer is available today. Next month, it will be joined by a set of enhancements to Test Cloud, a component of UiPath’s platform that speeds up software testing initiatives.
Engineers scan applications for bugs using scripts that simulate user activity. Writing those scripts, collecting their findings and extracting key data points can be highly labor-intensive. Test Cloud is receiving a feature called Autonomous Exploration that promises to speed up the task. It enables engineers to test an application by defining high-level bug detection goals.
Test Cloud can also mix manual and automated testing approaches. According to UiPath, engineers now can have the platform run their manually-developed tests on their applications. A new AI agent called UiPath Delegate automates administrative tasks such as preparing interface test summaries.
The third major focus of today’s product is the UiPath Integration Service. It provides connectors that enable automation workflows to interact with third party applications.
UiPath is adding features that make it possible to integrate workflows with databases and MCP-based AI agent tools. Another new capability, Relay, connects to on-premises workloads. Customers can store the login credentials their workflows use to access external applications in their existing secrets vaults. That removes the need to keep a separate copy of the credentials in UiPath, which eases administrators’ work.
The company is also rolling out several other platform enhancements. New governance controls will help enterprises ensure that the AI components of their automation workflows operate reliably. Plus, a feature called UiPath Coding Agents that made its original debut in March has moved to general availability. It enables developers to create automation workflows using AI tools such as Claude Code.

articles.title: Logitech G Unveils New Sim Racing Lineup Including the RS50 McLaren Racing Bundle
articles.text:
Wednesday, September 23rd 2026
	
									
	
	
	
Logitech G Unveils New Sim Racing Lineup Including the RS50 McLaren Racing Bundle
At Logitech G PLAY 2026, Logitech G unveiled a new sim racing lineup built around a breakthrough in awareness and accessibility: the Logitech G RS50 McLaren Racing Bundle, PC-only versions of the RS50 System and G923, and the RS Pedals SE. Together, these launches make sim racing more accessible to motorsport fans, more attainable for aspiring racers, and more flexible for PC players who want to pay only for what they need and upgrade at their own pace.
First introduced by Bruce McLaren in the 1960s, the iconic papaya color has become synonymous with six decades of racing heritage, innovation, and peak performance. Champions like McLaren Mastercard Formula 1 Team Drivers Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri spend hours each week in simulators, refining braking points and testing setup changes through force feedback systems that replicate every kerb strike and tire slip.That is why the Logitech G RS50 McLaren Racing Bundle matters. It brings the look, energy, and spirit of McLaren Racing into the home for motorsport fans and aspiring racers who want to feel closer to the track.
Richard Neville, Head of Simulation at Logitech G"Sim racing isn't just about replicating physics; it's about capturing the emotional connection between driver and machine. The RS50 McLaren Racing Bundle represents years of work translating what professional teams demand into something accessible."
As an all-in-one setup, this bundle provides everything you need for an unparalleled PC or console racing experience. It includes the RS50 Wheel Base, an 8 Nm Direct Drive system with TRUEFORCE technology for lifelike feedback; the RS Formula Wheel; the RS Wheel Hub with magnetic paddle shifters and fully integrated controls; the RS Pedals with a 75 kg load-cell brake; and all necessary accessories for quick assembly on a rig or table. This complete solution is designed to immerse racing enthusiasts in the thrill of precision driving, offering the tactile satisfaction of mastering each curve, the responsiveness of advanced braking, and the exhilaration of driving a high-performance machine, all from the comfort of your home.The excitement of motorsport has never been more accessible. Sim racing offers fans and enthusiasts an exhilarating way to experience the precision, energy, and competitive spirit of racing. It brings the excitement of driving legendary cars on iconic circuits directly into your hands, empowering you to refine your skills, test your limits, and immerse yourself in the challenges of the track. Whether you're a newcomer or a seasoned driver, the expanded Logitech G PC-only lineup provides the flexibility to create a setup tailored to your needs and grow alongside your ambitions.Sim racing delivers the most authentic connection to motorsport outside of being on the track, transforming every session and lap into a deeply rewarding journey. Designed with choice and simplicity at its core, the new Logitech G PC-only lineup empowers drivers to invest only in what they need, when they need it. This streamlined approach makes the lineup more adaptable, focused, and accessible, so you can stop imagining and start racing.
The lineup also creates a clear path for upgrading at your own pace. Newer drivers can begin with the G923 PC-only, while racers seeking greater power and precision can elevate their setup with the RS50 PC-only System. For those who want the full papaya experience, the RS50 McLaren Racing Bundle delivers a complete setup from day one.
Found in both the RS50 and the G923, TRUEFORCE uniquely connects with in-game physics to deliver a direct, deeper layer of feedback than traditional systems alone. Instead of only feeling broad steering forces, TRUEFORCE improves performance by allowing racers to experience the rumble of the engine, the texture of the asphalt beneath, and the exact moment you accidentally clip a curb, along with every detail in between.
The same pay-for-what-you-need philosophy extends to the new RS Pedals SE. Out of the box, they come with Hall-effect gas and brake pedals, giving drivers a durable, precise two-pedal setup for GT and Formula-style racing. For those who want more advanced braking later, the load-cell brake is available as an optional add-on rather than a required upfront cost. The hall-effect brake can then be repurposed as a clutch for manual shifting.
Logitech G is making sim racing more accessible, easier to grow into, and increasingly rewarding over time. If you have been waiting for the right moment, there's never been a better time to start racing.
		
		Sources:
				Logitech RS50 McLaren Racing Bundle, 				RS50 System, 				RS Pedals SE			
	
	
	
		
	
		
First introduced by Bruce McLaren in the 1960s, the iconic papaya color has become synonymous with six decades of racing heritage, innovation, and peak performance. Champions like McLaren Mastercard Formula 1 Team Drivers Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri spend hours each week in simulators, refining braking points and testing setup changes through force feedback systems that replicate every kerb strike and tire slip.That is why the Logitech G RS50 McLaren Racing Bundle matters. It brings the look, energy, and spirit of McLaren Racing into the home for motorsport fans and aspiring racers who want to feel closer to the track.
Richard Neville, Head of Simulation at Logitech G"Sim racing isn't just about replicating physics; it's about capturing the emotional connection between driver and machine. The RS50 McLaren Racing Bundle represents years of work translating what professional teams demand into something accessible."
The lineup also creates a clear path for upgrading at your own pace. Newer drivers can begin with the G923 PC-only, while racers seeking greater power and precision can elevate their setup with the RS50 PC-only System. For those who want the full papaya experience, the RS50 McLaren Racing Bundle delivers a complete setup from day one.
Found in both the RS50 and the G923, TRUEFORCE uniquely connects with in-game physics to deliver a direct, deeper layer of feedback than traditional systems alone. Instead of only feeling broad steering forces, TRUEFORCE improves performance by allowing racers to experience the rumble of the engine, the texture of the asphalt beneath, and the exact moment you accidentally clip a curb, along with every detail in between.
The same pay-for-what-you-need philosophy extends to the new RS Pedals SE. Out of the box, they come with Hall-effect gas and brake pedals, giving drivers a durable, precise two-pedal setup for GT and Formula-style racing. For those who want more advanced braking later, the load-cell brake is available as an optional add-on rather than a required upfront cost. The hall-effect brake can then be repurposed as a clutch for manual shifting.
Logitech G is making sim racing more accessible, easier to grow into, and increasingly rewarding over time. If you have been waiting for the right moment, there's never been a better time to start racing.

articles.title: ‘Glasses is the ideal form factor’ — Why Meta is bringing hearing enhancement to its smart glasses
articles.text:
‘Glasses is the ideal form factor’ — Why Meta is bringing hearing enhancement to its smart glasses
They're set to launch in the US later in 2026
Meta Connect 2026 is busy. Alongside the next-generation Meta Glasses, a camera-free version of the Ray-Ban Meta Glasses, and a new collaboration with Korean pop star Lisa, Meta is adding a significant new capability to its glasses: hearing enhancement.
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has cleared the feature, which turns a pair of Meta Glasses into a hearing aid for people with mild to moderate hearing loss. It amplifies sound based on your hearing profile and uses machine learning to boost voices and suppress background noise.
Meta isn't the first here, though. Apple's AirPods Pro 2 are already cleared as over-the-counter hearing aids and Nuance offers a pair of smart shades with a similar function. Meta, though, is betting on its form factor: glasses sit outside the ear, and many people already wear them all day.
It's not free, though. The feature launches with a free 30-day trial, after which it costs a one-time payment of $149.99, or comes as part of a Meta One subscription. In the US, it's also FSA/HSA eligible, with Meta saying it will share more details closer to the launch, which in the US is set for later in 2026. Even including the price of compatible glasses, Meta says it's significantly cheaper than traditional hearing aids.
The feature is launching in the US first, with Meta planning to expand to other countries as it works through each region's medical device regulations.
I spoke with Ravish Mehra, Director of Research Science at Meta, about why Meta thinks glasses are the right home for hearing enhancement. Mehra, who has spent nearly 12 years at the company, says the work started more than five years ago.
"We have a very unique audio platform that has microphone arrays, that has glasses, is socially acceptable in terms of people wearing glasses, and we have onboard compute," he says.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
According to Mehra, one in six Americans have mild to moderate hearing loss, yet only around 15% of them do anything about it. He notes that hearing aids are expensive, uncomfortable to wear all day, and signal to others that you have a hearing impairment. So people "put the issue under the rug," Mehra says, telling themselves, "Okay, it's just people are mumbling, and that's why I'm not able to hear."
Glasses sidestep the stigma in his view: "Nobody else can tell just by looking at your glasses that you have hearing impairment.”
A hearing test at home
"Every person's hearing loss is slightly different," Mehra says. Instead of a clinic visit and multiple fittings, Meta's hearing test takes around one to two minutes with your phone, through the Meta AI app, and your glasses. You listen to sounds at different frequencies, indicate when you can barely hear them, and the system builds a hearing profile showing where you need amplification.
"You don't have to go anywhere to get these glasses fit for your hearing profile," Mehra says. "You just do a very simple test at home, and whenever your hearing needs change, you just redo the test."
That test was central to the FDA clearance. Meta tested the feature with a group of people with mild to moderate hearing loss, and its results showed the phone-based test was equivalent in performance to a professional fitting, within an acceptable margin.
"We are actually the first self-fitting hearing aid on glasses in the market," Mehra says.
How it works
The glasses' six microphones capture sound around you — currently being used on Meta Glasses — which is then amplified where your profile shows a deficit. That also amplifies noise, so a machine learning model trained to recognize voices brings the background down. It all runs on-device, and speed is critical. "All of this has to happen in a very short latency, because otherwise you start hearing echoes or start hearing distortions," Mehra says.
There are two modes: 360 mode amplifies sound all around you, while Focus mode suits environments like a restaurant, where you want to hear the person across the table.
"We actually use the microphones to first do beamforming, which is like focusing in the forward direction more," Mehra explains. "And then […] we train the system to enhance the voices while not enhancing or suppressing the noise."
The frame helps, too. "Because the glasses have a much wider baseline, you can put the microphones much farther away," says Mehra. This makes it easier to isolate speech from noise than with microphones placed millimeters apart in the ear.
I got a brief demo: Meta had us put in earplugs to simulate hearing loss, then wear the glasses. They did properly amplify the people directly around me, and even those a bit farther away. Focus mode noticeably singles out the person in front of you, but it wasn't perfect, and of course earplugs are no substitute for real hearing loss.
The feedback problem
Amplifying sound isn't the hardest part, though. "One of the issues that any kind of real-time amplification feature faces is called feedback," Mehra says. "When you amplify something through the speakers, they feed back into the microphones."
On glasses, with their open-ear design, nothing separates the speakers from the microphones. Meta's system has to detect feedback before it builds, suppress it, and still deliver enough amplification. "If you're not able to cancel that feedback, then you hear these very sharp noises," Mehra says.
Then there's processing, which is added on top of a broader feature set the glasses offer, so Meta had to squeeze the feature into what Mehra calls "a very small envelope" of onboard compute power.
Meta hasn't confirmed which glasses will support it, only that they must meet a minimum performance bar, or confirmed a rollout schedule other than late 2026. Given the processing involved, I'd be surprised to see it on older models like the first-gen Ray-Ban Meta glasses; all of the demos at Meta Connect have been on the more recently released Meta Glasses.
Meta isn't just trying to make its glasses hear for you; it's trying to help you hear, too. It's a new category for the company, but Mehra is in no doubt about the bet, telling me: "We strongly feel like glasses is the ideal form factor."

Jacob Krol is the US Managing Editor, News for TechRadar. He’s been writing about technology since he was 14 when he started his own tech blog. Since then Jacob has worked for a plethora of publications including CNN Underscored, TheStreet, Parade, Men’s Journal, Mashable, CNET, and CNBC among others.
He specializes in covering companies like Apple, Samsung, and Google and going hands-on with mobile devices, smart home gadgets, TVs, and wearables. In his spare time, you can find Jacob listening to Bruce Springsteen, building a Lego set, or binge-watching the latest from Disney, Marvel, or Star Wars.

articles.title: En 1923, un vaquero instaló un molino para tener electricidad. Un siglo después, convirtió el viento en una mina de oro que vende electricidad a miles de hogares
articles.text:
La historia comienza hace 103 años, cuando la electricidad todavía no llegaba a un remoto rancho de las praderas de Kansas. Entonces, la familia Ferrell levantó un pequeño molino para fabricársela por su cuenta. Un siglo después, el escenario parece una versión gigantesca de aquella misma idea: donde entonces giraba un modesto Windjammer conectado a unas baterías, hoy se levantan 50 enormes aerogeneradores entre las vacas. La diferencia es que ahora el rancho ya no necesita el viento para encender sus propias luces. Lo ha convertido en una de sus principales fuentes de ingresos y en parte de un parque monumental.
Un rancho desde 1888. El relato arranca con el bisabuelo de Pete Ferrell, que estableció el rancho familiar en Beaumont, Kansas, en 1888. Hablamos de unas 7.000 acres (alrededor de 2.800 hectáreas) en las Flint Hills, una inmensa extensión de pradera de hierba alta donde la familia lleva cuatro generaciones criando ganado.
El lugar tiene además una peculiaridad clave: está situado en una de las zonas elevadas de la región y recibe abundante viento. Ferrell, de hecho, bromea con que su bisabuelo eligió por pura casualidad un lugar extraordinario para construir un parque eólico más de un siglo después.
Encender las luces. Cuando la familia construyó su casa en 1923, la red eléctrica todavía no llegaba hasta allí. La solución fue instalar un Jacobs Windjammer, un pequeño generador eólico de corriente continua conectado a una batería Delco que proporcionaba electricidad para las luces y algunos aparatos domésticos.
Aquel sistema mantuvo parcialmente electrificada la vivienda hasta que la red alcanzó finalmente el rancho durante la década de 1940. Así que cien años antes de que las grandes turbinas se convirtieran en parte del paisaje de Kansas, los Ferrell ya estaban cosechando viento porque no tenían otra manera de conseguir electricidad.
El salvavidas debajo de la tierra. La ganadería tenía un problema que ninguna generación podía eliminar: dependía demasiado del clima y de los mercados. Así, durante la década de 1920, la familia comenzó a arrendar derechos para extraer petróleo de sus terrenos, creando una segunda fuente de ingresos capaz de sostener el rancho cuando la sequía castigaba los pastos y el ganado.
Décadas después, Pete Ferrell terminaría aplicando prácticamente la misma lógica a otro recurso natural de su propiedad. Solo que esta vez no había que perforar el suelo: bastaba con aprovechar lo que llevaba toda la vida soplando sobre él.
Primero dijo que no. A mediados de los años noventa, una empresa propuso a Ferrell instalar un parque eólico en sus tierras. Su primera respuesta fue negativa. Temía alterar la pradera, perjudicar a especies como el gallo de las praderas y descubrir demasiado tarde que las enormes máquinas eran incompatibles con el ganado.
El punto de inflexión llegó poco después, durante un viaje al Altamont Pass de California, donde pudo hablar con ganaderos que llevaban años trabajando entre aerogeneradores. Regresó a Kansas convencido de que ambas actividades podían convivir, aunque el primer proyecto terminó fracasando y él mismo tuvo después que buscar otro promotor hasta alcanzar un acuerdo con Greenlight Energy Resources.
De pequeño molino a 50 gigantes. El Elk River Wind Project comenzó a funcionar en 2005 con 100 aerogeneradores GE de 1,5 MW y una potencia conjunta de 150 MW. Exactamente la mitad de esas máquinas se encuentran dentro del rancho de Ferrell, y las otras 50 están repartidas por tres propiedades vecinas.
Las estimaciones originales situaban su producción en unos 550.000 MWh anuales, equivalente entonces al consumo de aproximadamente 42.000 hogares, aunque estimaciones posteriores han elevado esa equivalencia hasta unas 60.000 viviendas. Ferrell no vende personalmente esa electricidad, sino algo todavía más sencillo para él y su familia: cobra por alquilar sus terrenos mientras la energía generada por el parque entra en la red.
Las vacas perdieron tierra, el rancho se multiplicó. La transformación parece enorme cuando se observan las turbinas desde lejos, pero sobre el terreno resulta mucho más pequeña. Ferrell midió posteriormente todo el espacio ocupado por las bases, carreteras e instalaciones del parque y calculó que había perdido aproximadamente 50 acres (20 hectáreas) de superficie agrícola: apenas un acre (0,4 hectáreas) por aerogenerador.
Eso significa que alrededor del 99% de la propiedad continúa disponible y las vacas siguen pastando alrededor de las turbinas prácticamente como antes. La comparación favorita de Ferrell es con los antiguos pozos petrolíferos del rancho: considera los molinos una especie de bombas de petróleo suspendidas en el aire, con una diferencia importante, porque no pueden derramar agua salada sobre el terreno y su combustible no se agota.
La mejor cosecha: el viento. La verdadera transformación del rancho no está en el paisaje, sino en sus cuentas. Desde que comenzó el proyecto, los royalties eólicos han llegado a representar aproximadamente la mitad de los ingresos de Ferrell, proporcionando algo excepcionalmente valioso para cualquier ganadero: dinero que no depende directamente del precio del ganado, de cuánto crezca la hierba o de que llueva.
Una sequía puede obligarle a reducir animales, comprar alimento y asumir pérdidas, pero no impide necesariamente que las turbinas continúen girando. Por eso Ferrell define el viento como su mejor cash crop: una cosecha que puede seguir produciendo precisamente cuando las demás están fallando.
Un siglo después, la historia dio la vuelta. Los ingresos han permitido a Ferrell mantener el rancho, reducir su dependencia de la ganadería y preparar la transmisión de una propiedad familiar desde 1888 a sus hijos y nietos sin cargarles con una montaña de deuda. Si se quiere también, hay algo especialmente circular en todo ello.
En 1923, sus antepasados levantaron un pequeño molino porque vivían tan lejos que nadie podía llevarles electricidad. Un siglo después, 50 gigantes ocupan apenas una fracción de aquellas mismas tierras mientras las vacas continúan pastando debajo tranquilamente.
El rancho que tuvo que recurrir al viento para encender unas cuantas bombillas terminó descubriendo que llevaba generaciones sentado sobre otra fuente de riqueza: una que no estaba enterrada bajo sus pies, sino soplando sobre sus cabezas.

articles.title: The GPU Madness Has Come to This: 9070 XT vs. 5060 Ti 16GB
articles.text:
Good news, guys. I've saved up my dollarydoos and I'm finally ready to buy a new graphics card for playing all my favorite video games. So let's go shopping, shall we?
I've got around $1,200 to spend here in Australia, roughly $850 USD, though ideally we'd like to spend a little less. Let's aim for a mid-range GeForce GPU because we've heard over on Reddit that GeForce is better than Radeon, so that's probably correct. Clearly, we're off to a very sensible start.
The GeForce RTX 5060 Ti seems like what we're after, the 16GB model of course, because we might eventually play something other than Fortnite. You never know.
Wow, what's going on here? The last time we checked, admittedly earlier in the year, the 5060 Ti 16GB was priced around $750. Now they're starting at $1,050 and are mostly out of stock.
In fact, PC Case Gear has just a single model available, a PNY card for $1,049. Yikes. Bugger that, let's try Mwave. Here we go, $769. Nice. Wait, it's out of stock. Okay, $1,000, also out of stock. $1,049, finally one that's available, and it's another PNY model. Then there's the Asus Dual at $1,129. Man, it's rough out here.
Okay, so we know those Radeon GPUs aren't meant to be as good, but we're getting desperate, so let's take a look. Based on what we're seeing at local retailers, a GPU called the Radeon RX 9070 XT appears to be the direct competitor to the 5060 Ti 16GB. They're a little more expensive, but pricing is surprisingly similar, starting at $1,149 with plenty of models around $1,249. Hopefully it's not much slower than the GeForce GPU.
Just to make sure this isn't some bizarre Australian pricing anomaly, we also checked Newegg. There, the 5060 Ti 16GB starts at around $780, which means the 9070 XT is actually cheaper, with Radeon models starting at roughly $740. Both GPUs come with 16GB of VRAM, so we clearly need to see how they compare.
For that, we've benchmarked the Radeon RX 9070 XT and GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 16GB across 52 games to see what gamers are actually getting for roughly an $800 budget overseas or around $1,200 in Australia. Rather than walk through all 52 games individually, we'll highlight some of the more interesting results before getting to the full performance summary and cost-per-frame analysis. Let's do it...
Test System Specs
| CPU | AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D | 
| Motherboard | MSI MPG X870E Carbon WiFi [BIOS 7E49v1A4] Resizable BAR Enabled | 
| Memory | G.Skill Trident Z5 RGB DDR5-6000 CL30 [CL30-38-38-96] | 
| Graphics Card | Sapphire Radeon RX 9070 XT Pure Asus Prime GeForce RTX 5070 Ti 16GB | 
| ATX Case | MSI Prospect 700R | 
| Power Supply | Kolink Regulator Gold ATX 3.0 1200W | 
| Storage | TeamGroup T-Force Cardea A440 M.2 PCIe Gen4 NVMe SSD 4TB | 
| Operating System | Windows 11 25H2 | 
| Display Driver | AMD Radeon Adrenalin 26.8.1 GeForce Game Ready Driver 610.88 | 
Benchmarks
007 First Light
Starting with 007 First Light, we see the 9070 XT is 81% faster at 1440p using the Medium preset, with frame rates jumping from 67 fps on the RTX 5060 Ti to 121 fps on the Radeon GPU. That seems like quite a lot.
The 4K results are even worse for the GeForce GPU. Again using the Medium preset, the 9070 XT was 106% faster, taking performance from a measly 34 fps to a highly playable 70 fps.
Switching to the Ultra preset didn't help the RTX 5060 Ti all that much. The margins did come down, but even so, the 9070 XT was still 62% faster at 1440p and 78% faster at 4K. At native resolutions, the 5060 Ti is effectively limited to 1440p here, while 4K is a realistic option with the 9070 XT.
Spider-Man 2
Swinging into Spider-Man 2, the 9070 XT continues to flex on the 5060 Ti. At 1440p using the Very High preset, it averaged 130 fps compared with 81 fps on the 5060 Ti, a massive 60% performance advantage.
Even at 4K, the Radeon GPU remained rock-solid at 80 fps, making it 70% faster than the 5060 Ti, which managed just 47 fps.
Enabling the demanding Ray Tracing Ultimate mode brings frame rates down, but the hierarchy stays firmly in place. At 1440p, the 9070 XT delivered a playable 67 fps, making it 60% faster than the 5060 Ti's 42 fps. Then at 4K, the 9070 XT averaged 36 fps, giving it a 50% advantage over the 5060 Ti's cinematic 24 fps.
Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight
Moving over to Lego Batman, we see the bloodbath continue. At 1440p using the Medium preset, the 9070 XT pumps out 234 fps compared with 149 fps for the 5060 Ti, making the Radeon card a cool 57% faster. Bumping the resolution to 4K makes the Nvidia card's value proposition look even more embarrassing. The 9070 XT crushes it by an 88% margin, delivering a buttery-smooth 147 fps while the 5060 Ti trails far behind at just 78 fps.
Cranking the visuals up to the Epic preset gives the RTX 5060 Ti a slight breather in terms of the performance gap, but it still gets thoroughly outclassed. At 1440p, the Radeon GPU maintains a comfortable 40% lead, hitting 102 fps versus 73 fps for the GeForce GPU.
Pushing the resolution to 4K, the 9070 XT manages to scrape by with an almost 60 fps experience, making it 51% faster than the 5060 Ti's rather pathetic 39 fps. Ultimately, while 1440p is doable on both GPUs, anyone hoping for a decent native 4K experience here will be severely disappointed by the GeForce card.
Fortnite
Fortnite gives the RTX 5060 Ti its closest showing yet, at least in lightweight competitive settings. At 1440p using Performance Mode, the 9070 XT was just 14% faster, though that gap stretched to 30% at 4K.
However, once Unreal Engine 5's full graphical suite is unleashed using Epic Quality settings with ray tracing enabled, normal service resumes. At 1440p, the 9070 XT rendered 120 fps, making it 54% faster than the 5060 Ti's 78 fps. Then at 4K, AMD held a flat 50% lead at 66 fps versus 44 fps.
Forza Horizon 6
In Forza Horizon 6, the rasterized and ray-traced results tell an identical story of AMD dominance. Using the Extreme preset at 1440p, the 9070 XT was 65% faster, rendering 140 fps compared with the 5060 Ti's 85 fps.
Moving to 4K, the 9070 XT breezed past the 100 fps mark, while the 5060 Ti failed to maintain 60 fps, giving the Radeon GPU a 76% advantage.
Tossing ray tracing into the mix highlights the hardware gap even further. At 1440p, the 9070 XT remained 79% ahead with 75 fps versus 42 fps. At 4K, both GPUs struggled, but the 9070 XT's 43 fps was still 79% faster than the unplayable 24 fps produced by the RTX 5060 Ti. With some upscaling support, the Radeon GPU would at least be usable here.
Crimson Desert
Next up is Crimson Desert, where the 9070 XT maintains a commanding lead. Using the Medium preset at 1440p, the Radeon GPU averaged 103 fps compared with 67 fps for the 5060 Ti, a 54% performance advantage.
At 4K, the disparity widened considerably. The Radeon GPU cruised along at 66 fps for a 69% advantage, while the GeForce card stumbled into sub-40 fps territory at just 39 fps.
Enabling the Cinematic quality preset doesn't do Team Green any favors either. At 1440p, the 9070 XT remained 54% faster, rendering 86 fps against the 5060 Ti's 56 fps. Meanwhile, at 4K, the 9070 XT averaged a respectable 53 fps, beating the 5060 Ti's 32 fps by 66%. For a smooth visual showcase at maximum settings, the 5060 Ti clearly punches well below its inflated price point.
Ark: Survival Ascended
Unreal Engine 5 continues to take no prisoners, but the RTX 5060 Ti suffers a particularly grim fate here. At 1440p using the Medium preset, the 9070 XT delivered 70% greater performance, managing 51 fps while Nvidia's offering crawled along at just 30 fps.
Stepping up to 4K effectively turned the RTX 5060 Ti into a slideshow at 18 fps, whereas the Radeon GPU was 72% faster at 31 fps. That's not exactly lightning quick, but it is substantially better.
Things get downright comical with the Epic preset. At 1440p, the 9070 XT was 81% faster, and at 4K the gap widened to 83%, leaving the 5060 Ti choking at a miserable 12 fps average with single-digit 1% lows. Simply put, native rendering on the 5060 Ti is essentially unplayable across the board in this title. It's so bad, in fact, that most of these results wouldn't be made workable even with Ultra Performance DLSS thrown into the mix.
Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty
In Night City, traditionally a stronghold for Nvidia hardware, particularly with ray tracing enabled, the raw tier mismatch makes for some brutal viewing. At 1440p using the Ultra preset, the 9070 XT sat comfortably at 131 fps, giving it a massive 90% lead over the 5060 Ti's 69 fps. Stepping up to 4K widened the gap further to 103%, with the Radeon GPU maintaining a playable 63 fps average while the 5060 Ti stumbled along at just 31 fps.
Even with Ray Tracing Ultra engaged, the 5060 Ti simply lacks the horsepower to compete. At 1440p, the 9070 XT was nearly twice as fast, with a 96% performance advantage.
Native 4K proved punishing for both, but the 9070 XT's 26 fps still placed it 86% ahead of the 5060 Ti's slideshow-like 14 fps average.
Stalker 2: Heart of Chornobyl
Venturing into the Zone at native resolution yields another heavy round of defeats for the GeForce GPU. At 1440p using the Medium preset, the 9070 XT clocked in at 122 fps, 54% faster than the 5060 Ti's 79 fps, with the Radeon GPU's 1% lows even surpassing the GeForce card's average frame rate. At 4K, the Radeon GPU delivered a 63% uplift, managing 70 fps while the 5060 Ti fell flat at 43 fps.
Dialing the visuals up to Epic tightens things slightly, but the hierarchy remains unchanged. At 1440p, the 9070 XT stayed 52% ahead with 70 fps versus 46 fps.
At 4K, neither GPU is delivering a high-refresh experience, but the 9070 XT's 40 fps still outpaced the 5060 Ti's 26 fps by 54%.
Pragmata
Rounding out this portion of the testing with Pragmata, the Radeon GPU continues its dominant sweep. At 1440p using the Max Quality settings, the 9070 XT rendered 138 fps, outpacing the 5060 Ti's 89 fps by 55%. Moving to 4K pushed that lead to 63%, with AMD hitting a smooth 78 fps while Nvidia struggled to break 50 fps at 48 fps.
Enabling ray tracing barely slowed down the 9070 XT. At 1440p with full ray tracing, the Radeon GPU averaged 135 fps, enjoying a 63% advantage over the 5060 Ti's 83 fps.
Then at 4K, the 9070 XT averaged a solid 76 fps for a 69% margin over the 5060 Ti's 45 fps. With both GPUs selling for equivalent money, giving up more than 60% of your frame rate for the GeForce badge is a tough pill to swallow.
Arc Raiders
Finally, in Arc Raiders, we see some of the narrowest margins of the test suite, though the 9070 XT still wins in every configuration. Using Epic Quality with RT Static at 1440p, the Radeon GPU was 30% faster, extending that margin to 38% at 4K.
Stepping up to RT Epic at 1440p compressed the margin to its narrowest point at 24%. At 4K, the gap settled at 30%, with the 9070 XT reaching 133 fps while the 5060 Ti achieved 102 fps. Both cards provide high frame rates here, but you're still getting roughly a third more performance from the Radeon GPU for the same money.
Performance Summary: 52 Games
Looking at the massive 52-game average across mixed quality settings, the overall picture doesn't get any prettier for Nvidia. At 1440p, the Radeon RX 9070 XT pulls ahead by 62%, averaging 123 fps compared with the RTX 5060 Ti's 76 fps.
In fact, the Radeon card's 1% lows of 97 fps comfortably beat the GeForce card's average frame rate, highlighting just how wide the performance gulf really is.
Step up to 4K and the margin widens to 71% in AMD's favor. Here, the 9070 XT delivers a genuinely smooth 72 fps average, whereas the 5060 Ti is left struggling in the low 40s at just 42 fps, with its 1% lows dipping to 33 fps.
When essentially the same retail price gets you a card capable of smooth 4K gaming on one side and a GPU that's clearly better suited to 1440p on the other, the value equation for the 5060 Ti completely falls apart.
Cost Per Frame
Australian Dollars
To better illustrate the value equation, here's the cost-per-frame data based on current Australian retail pricing. Despite coming in $100 cheaper, the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB still costs 48% more per frame based on our 1440p results and 57% more at 4K. That's crazy.
United States
But the situation is far worse in the United States, and we strongly suspect Australian pricing will catch up over the coming weeks, as retailers currently appear hesitant to restock RTX 5060 Ti cards at today's asking prices.
Over at Newegg, the 5060 Ti comes in 71% more expensive per frame based on our 1440p data and an insane 81% more expensive at 4K.
There's really not much more that needs to be said here.
The GeForce Tax Is Getting Ridiculous
It's hard to say when this madness will end, or even how much worse things might get. If we'd told you just a few months ago that the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB would soon cost as much as, or even more than, the Radeon RX 9070 XT, most of you probably would have laughed us out of the room. And we wouldn't blame you. It's hard to imagine, but here we are.
In part, these inflated prices are the result of the industry-wide memory shortage. The 9070 XT is now at least 23% above MSRP, though the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB is a little over 80% above its MSRP. Both feature 16GB of VRAM, but the GeForce GPU uses GDDR7 memory whereas the 9070 XT still relies on GDDR6, so there are cost differences there.
Tying into this, Nvidia recently notified board partners that it was increasing prices for its GPU and memory bundles, which was quickly followed by significant price increases for GeForce graphics cards, as we've seen with the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB. Exactly how much is the increase isn't publicly known. I have some off-the-record details, but it sounds as though they've added a bit extra on top, which would help explain how the 5060 Ti has ended up more than 80% above MSRP.
Nvidia is also able to get away with these extreme prices because of AI demand. That doesn't just mean data centers, which aren't buying GeForce gaming cards, but also users building systems for local AI workloads. Those buyers are helping soak up these hideously overpriced GeForce GPUs.
As I understand it, and please note that I am far from an expert on this AI stuff, there is significantly greater demand for the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB than the Radeon RX 9070 XT among users running AI workloads locally. As we've just seen, the RX 9070 XT is an extremely capable gaming GPU, and it actually offers more raw memory bandwidth than the RTX 5060 Ti despite using GDDR6 memory. Memory bandwidth can also be an important factor in AI workloads.
However, Nvidia remains the dominant choice for local AI builders. The disparity in demand largely comes down to software support, ecosystem maturity, and ease of use.
Nvidia's CUDA ecosystem remains one of the foundational software layers for modern AI development. New AI models, interfaces, fine-tuning tools, and GitHub projects are frequently developed, optimized, and tested on Nvidia hardware first. Some popular tools and inference frameworks also specifically target Nvidia GPUs.
The Radeon RX 9070 XT can be a compelling option for users willing to work within AMD's software ecosystem, particularly under Linux, where its raw performance and memory bandwidth can be put to good use. But for most local AI users, the RTX 5060 Ti remains the "safer bet" as it guarantees compatibility with upcoming AI tools, requires less troubleshooting, and dominates in image generation. For these reasons, Nvidia has been able to jack up pricing and keep selling GPUs, but in doing so fewer and fewer gamers are now going GeForce, not that Nvidia cares.
If you're building a gaming PC and want more than 8GB of VRAM, as it stands, Radeon is increasingly the only way to go. At these prices, paying the GeForce tax simply isn't worth it.

articles.title: « La radio n’est pas une option » : pour éviter sa disparition des voitures, les radios françaises montent au créneau
articles.text:
La radio ne doit pas devenir une simple option payante ou dépendre d’un abonnement à une plateforme de streaming. C’est le message porté conjointement par Radio France, l’Alliance de la radio et les radios associatives dans un communiqué publié le 21 septembre 2026. Alors que Médiamétrie rappelle qu’un tiers de l’écoute se fait en voiture, plusieurs constructeurs automobiles, venus notamment d’Asie ou des États-Unis, suppriment purement et simplement les tuners hertziens des tableaux de bord. Pour écouter un programme, les conducteurs se retrouvent contraints de passer par la radio streaming sur mobile.
Des enjeux de sécurité civile
Derrière cette bataille de constructeurs se pose aussi la question de la gestion des crises et notamment la résilience des réseaux. Les récentes intempéries et les feux estivaux en Gironde ont lourdement endommagé les infrastructures de télécommunication, détruisant notamment des dizaines de kilomètres de câbles de fibre optique et des centaines de poteaux. En situation d’urgence, les réseaux mobiles s’effondrent rapidement lorsque les batteries relais s’épuisent. L’Espagne a connu la même vulnérabilité lors d’une panne géante d’électricité en avril 2025, où les téléphones étaient déconnectés tandis que les autoradios continuaient de diffuser les informations.
Une voiture qui n’a pas de récepteur hertzien représente donc un angle mort pour la sécurité civile. Contrairement à internet ou au streaming, la diffusion FM et DAB+ (ou Radio Numérique Terrestre) reste entièrement gratuite, anonyme et accessible en toutes circonstances, jouant le même rôle d’alerte indispensable qu’un bon vieux poste à piles. C’est ce qu’a rappelé le Secrétariat général de la Défense et de la Sécurité nationale lors des dernières Assises de la Radio de l’Arcom.
Empêcher un contournement de la loi
Les acteurs de la radio appellent le gouvernement à légiférer pour empêcher le contournement de la loi de 2020 qui rendait déjà le DAB+ obligatoire dans les véhicules neufs dès lors qu’un système radio était présent. La parade actuelle des fabricants consiste à supprimer l’équipement radio de base pour échapper à cette règle. Service public et radios privées font désormais front commun pour que la législation évolue.
Au niveau européen, la négociation en cours du Digital Networks Act doit trancher sur l’obligation d’intégrer des récepteurs FM et DAB+ dans tous les véhicules neufs, utilitaires compris, avec une place importante sur la console multimédia. Au niveau français, le secteur attend un avis favorable du gouvernement lors de l’examen de l’article 2 de la proposition de loi portée par le sénateur Laurent Lafon, qui entend verrouiller cette obligation d’équipement dans l’hexagone.
 👉🏻 Suivez l’actualité tech en temps réel : ajoutez 01net à vos sources sur Google, et abonnez-vous à notre canal WhatsApp.
Source : Radio France

articles.title: ASML says it sold 'absolutely nothing' in Europe in 2026 — lithography giant calls on EU to help create demand
articles.text:
ASML says it sold 'absolutely nothing' in Europe in 2026 — lithography giant calls on EU to help create demand
Subsidies for fabs do not help.
As the world's only supplier of EUV lithography systems, ASML is Europe's largest company by market capitalization, currently valued at around $660 billion. But ASML earned almost nothing in Europe this year, down from 1% in 2025 and 5% in 2024. As it turns out, European chipmakers did not buy any lithography equipment from ASML in 2026. Now, ASML is calling on EU authorities to help create demand for European chips.
Europe's share in ASML's revenue drops to 0%
"So, we are selling absolutely nothing in Europe," said Frank Heemskerk, executive vice president of public affairs at ASML, while speaking at De Balie program on Dutch television. "Because Europe is not investing and because no chip factories are being built in Europe. That is genuinely worrying. […] [Our revenue share in Europe is 0%], it used to be 1%."
Indeed, Europe accounted for 1% of ASML's revenue share in 2025, 5% in 2024, 4% in 2023, and 2% in 2022, based on the company's presentations for investors. However, in the first two quarters of 2026, Europe accounted for 0% of ASML's revenue, according to ASML's earnings reports.
"There simply is no demand here for these kinds of highly specialized machines," Heemskerk said. "That is the problem. So apart from trying to attract investment with capital on the supply side, we should do much more to create demand. […] So, we at ASML are also making an enormous effort, and we are talking with Ursula von der Leyen in Europe, saying: 'try to harness the market power and dynamism that ultimately do exist in Europe in a number of areas.'"
So far, the European Union has been keen on subsidizing building new fabs in Europe (something that did not help to lure Intel in). But ASML is calling on European governments to help aggregate and guarantee demand for European-made chips — which will encourage major European chip consumers to source locally, giving semiconductor manufacturers an economic reason to build or expand fabs in Europe.
"We need to make sure that some of those buyers — the customers of our customers — start talking much more closely with European manufacturers again. In areas such as artificial intelligence for industry, for example, there are still plenty of opportunities that Europe can seize. But you have to organize this collectively."
New fabs are being built…
That said, the ASML EVP may be too pessimistic about Europe's semiconductor industry.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Intel runs its massive Fab 34 near Leixlip, Ireland, and recently announced plans to invest €5 billion in the facility to expand production of CPUs on Intel 4 and Intel 3 process technologies. While the new investment dwarfs Intel's plans to invest roughly €80 billion in its Magdeburg, Germany, fab complex, with two first fabs alone accounting for over €30 billion, it still represents Intel's commitment to its Ireland campus.
In addition, ESMC — which is backed by TSMC, Bosch, Infineon, and NXP — is building a brand-new fab near Dresden that will cost around €15 billion. The fab will be capable of producing chips using 12nm/16nm-class FinFET and 22nm/28nm planar transistor-based process technologies used in a wide range of automotive applications. The same nodes are also used for various consumer electronics and edge applications.
Infineon also opened its new €5 billion Smart Power Fab in Dresden in July 2026, which marked the largest single investment in the company's history and effectively doubled its manufacturing capacity at the site. The 300mm facility produces power semiconductors as well as analog and mixed-signal chips for automotive, industrial, renewable-energy, and AI data-center applications.
Last but not least, GlobalFoundries officially broke ground on the latest major expansion and upgrade of Fab 1 in Dresden this March to increase capacity for its specialty process technologies, including 22nm FD-SOI (22FDX), embedded non-volatile memory (eNVM), and the BCD (bipolar-CMOS-DMOS) node for power management ICs. To some degree, the upgrade was forced by headwinds that GlobalFoundries faced when building the €10.4 billion joint fab with STMicroelectronics in the Grenoble, France, region.
With numerous semiconductor fab projects in place in Europe, ASML will continue to sell its tools to companies in the EU for years to come as the semiconductor industry is far from dead in the bloc. Of course, the important detail is that all of these production facilities are built by multinational corporations (sometimes in collaboration with local companies) — but this is largely a global trend rather than a major issue.
…But there is a catch
Although the fab projects in Europe are large in terms of investment, they pale in comparison with those being built in Taiwan, South Korea, the U.S., and Japan, where tens or even hundreds of billions of dollars are being invested in new semiconductor production facilities.
What is perhaps more important from ASML's standpoint is that none of the ongoing fab projects in Europe are leading-edge fabs set to use EUV and eventually High-NA EUV lithography scanners. The tools that European fabs use today and that new facilities are set to use in the future are mature tools that cost considerably less than advanced EUV or immersion DUV scanners. This is perhaps a concern for ASML, as the company is naturally interested in selling its more sophisticated and expensive equipment.
Another concern is that even advanced silicon produced in Ireland or at ESMC is then shipped to other regions for packaging, meaning that European companies have largely lost their ability to produce sophisticated chips entirely in Europe. In turn, this means that, for now, there is hardly any strategic point for European authorities to create demand for chips that are 'Made in Europe' because they are either not assembled in Europe, not produced in Europe, or not developed in Europe. We have no idea whether this is eventually going to change, but there are currently no signs that it will.
Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.

articles.title: Microsoft desmanteló EvilTokens, la red de fraude con IA que vulneró 12.000 cuentas corporativas
articles.text:
Microsoft anunció que su Unidad de Delitos Digitales desarticuló EvilTokens, una plataforma de fraude por suscripción que usaba un chatbot de inteligencia artificial para automatizar ataques y que comprometió más de 12.000 cuentas de Microsoft en más de 10.000 organizaciones de todo el mundo.
El servicio se vendía por Telegram desde febrero de este año a 1.500 dólares de alta más 500 dólares mensuales, según informó la empresa en un comunicado publicado en su blog oficial.
PUBLICIDAD
Una vez que un delincuente lograba entrar a una cuenta, un asistente con inteligencia artificial analizaba el contenido del correo para detectar transferencias pendientes, facturas y contactos de confianza, y después redactaba mensajes de suplantación creíbles para robar dinero.
“El asistente ayudó a los atacantes a redactar mensajes más convincentes, decidió a quién apuntar, a quién suplantar y cómo explotar mejor esa relación para extraer la mayor cantidad de dinero posible”, explicó Steven Masada, asesor general adjunto y gerente general de la Unidad de Delitos Digitales de Microsoft.
Antes de la irrupción de estas herramientas, revisar una casilla robada y planificar el fraude podía llevarle a un criminal días o semanas de trabajo manual. Con el asistente de EvilTokens, ese análisis se reducía a minutos.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo entraban a las cuentas
Los atacantes no robaban contraseñas de forma directa. Explotaban el código de dispositivo, un mecanismo de autenticación pensado para televisores y otros aparatos sin teclado completo, que permite iniciar sesión ingresando un código en otra pantalla.
Las víctimas recibían correos que las inducían a introducir ese código en la página legítima de inicio de sesión de Microsoft, lo que le daba al atacante una sesión autenticada sin robar la contraseña ni sortear la verificación en dos pasos.
Microsoft advirtió que ese acceso puede sobrevivir a un cambio de contraseña si la víctima no revoca también las sesiones y los tokens asociados a la cuenta comprometida.
PUBLICIDAD
La empresa de inteligencia de amenazas SpyCloud identificó 8.708 cuentas víctimas confirmadas en 6.585 dominios corporativos de 79 países, con las mayores concentraciones en Estados Unidos, Canadá, Australia y el Reino Unido.
Jason Rivera, jefe global de seguridad de la información de SimSpace, señaló que una vez adentro, la inteligencia artificial identificaba quién controlaba los pagos y qué relaciones comerciales gozaban de mayor confianza.
Una causa judicial y dos arrestos en Londres
Microsoft obtuvo una orden de un tribunal federal del Distrito Este de Virginia para incautar la infraestructura del servicio, en una operación conjunta con Health-ISAC, Cloudflare, Coinbase, OpenAI, Railway, SpyCloud, la Fundación Shadowserver y TRM Labs.
PUBLICIDAD
Con esa autorización, la compañía incautó 50 sitios web y deshabilitó otros 150 dominios vinculados a la operación, que Microsoft identifica bajo el nombre en código Storm-2992.
La Policía Metropolitana de Londres detuvo el 11 de septiembre a dos hombres de 32 y 38 años, sospechosos de operar la plataforma, en los barrios de Canary Wharf y Nine Elms. Ambos quedaron en libertad bajo fianza mientras sigue la investigación.
Según Microsoft, esta fue la disrupción número 40 ordenada judicialmente por su Unidad de Delitos Digitales y la primera dirigida contra un servicio de cibercrimen de extremo a extremo construido con inteligencia artificial.
PUBLICIDAD
El negocio detrás del fraude automatizado
Los investigadores hallaron evidencia de que buena parte del código de EvilTokens fue escrito con asistencia de inteligencia artificial. La empresa confirmó además que el servicio recurrió a capacidades de varios modelos de IA distintos, aunque no detalló cuáles.
Un vocero de Microsoft dijo que OpenAI fue un socio importante en el esfuerzo de desarticulación, aunque no dio precisiones sobre qué otras plataformas de inteligencia artificial se usaron para construir o hacer funcionar EvilTokens.
“EvilTokens convirtió en algo accesible para cualquiera, por 500 dólares al mes, tareas que antes requerían experiencia humana”, afirmó Trevor Hilligoss, director de inteligencia de SpyCloud.
PUBLICIDAD
Los sectores más afectados fueron distribución mayorista, construcción, servicios financieros, bienes raíces, educación superior y salud. Casi todas las cuentas comprometidas, un 97,5%, pertenecían a dominios empresariales.
El fraude por código de dispositivo no nació con EvilTokens. La firma de ciberseguridad Huntress documentó la técnica por primera vez en marzo, y hacia abril ya existían al menos diez plataformas que la ofrecían como servicio en el mercado del cibercrimen.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD
