articles.title: India’s tech cos raise $10.3B in 2026: Tracxn
articles.text:
India’s tech cos raise $10.3B in 2026: Tracxn
The report by Tracxn shows that capital is concentrated in fewer but larger, higher-conviction bets.
India’s tech companies raised a combined $10.3 billion in the first nine months of 2026, an increase of 6.18% from $9.7 billion raised in the same period a year earlier, and 3% above the $10 billion raised in the nine months of 2024, according to a report by data intelligence platform Tracxn.
The 'India Tech 9M 2026 Report' also says these numbers are notable, given that the number of funding rounds, first-time funded companies, and soonicorn additions declined sharply.
Enterprise applications, fintech, and enterprise infrastructure emerged as the top-performing sectors, together anchored by 18 rounds of $100 million or more.
There were 1,134 funding rounds in the nine months of 2026, down 38% from 1,838 a year earlier. The period saw 18 rounds of $100 million or more, led by Nxtra’s $1B private-equity round, Neysa’s $600 million Series B, and CRED’s $540 million Series H. A chunk of these mega rounds were from from AI infrastructure, digital lending, and payments, signalling that capital is concentrated in fewer but larger, higher-conviction bets.
However, at the top of the funnel, seed funding fell 37% to $698 million. Early-stage funding rose 27% to $4.2 billion, while late-stage held roughly steady at $5.4 billion.
First-time funded companies dropped 30% to 338 and Series A+ rounds fell 23% to 409, pointing to a market that is backing proven companies over new entrants even as headline dollars edge higher.
The report also said enterprise infrastructure was the fastest-growing sector of the period, with funding up 436% to $1.6 billion from $292 million in the same period a year earlier. Enterprise applications grew 49% to $3.5B, and finTech was up 13% at $2.2 billion.
AI infrastructure was the single most-funded business feed at $1.2 billion, ahead of digital lending ($799 million) and payments ($773 million).
India's unicorns chapter of 2026
India minted 6 new unicorns so far this year, up from 4 in the same period a year earlier. New unicorns raised an average of $101 million before their unicorn round, less than half the $205 million averaged in the first nine months of 2025.
India Tech saw 29 IPOs in the nine months of 2026, alongside 91 acquisitions, down from 131. Fractal Analytics led with a $1.7 billion IPO market cap, followed by Molbio Diagnostics ($973 million) and Amagi ($858 million). Shiprocket also went public in the period.
The average time from first funding to IPO fell to 8.5 years from 13.7 a year earlier, and the average time to acquisition dropped to 6.9 years from 14.7. On the acquisition side, Innovist's $434-milliom sale to LOréal was the period’s largest acquisition, ahead of Adani Energy Solutions' $319M purchase of IntelliSmart and UpGrad’s $218-million acquisition of Unacademy.
Citywise trends: Bengaluru leads, Gurugram surges
Bengaluru remained India’s dominant funding hub in 2026, capturing 43% of all tech capital with $4.4 billion, up from 38% a year earlier. In Bengaluru, CRED ($540 million), Rapido ($240 million), and Sarvam ($234 million) were the top-funded companies of the period, reinforcing the city’s lead across fintech, mobility, and AI.
Mumbai followed at $1.8 billion (18% share), ahead of Gurugram at $1.6 billion, whose share doubled from 8% to 16%, driven almost entirely by Nxtra's $1-billion round.
Noida ($660 million, 6%) and Delhi ($446 million, 4%) rounded out the top five, with Delhi’s share falling sharply from 15% a year earlier.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: GEEKOM A5 Pro Mini PC : -110 € sur ce modèle AMD Ryzen 7000 qui veut tout faire
articles.text:
Jusqu’au 11 octobre, le GEEKOM A5 Pro 2026 Edition profite de 110 € de remise avec le code CLUA5110. De quoi profiter à moindre coût de ce mini PC compact qui mise sur un CPU Ryzen 5, 16 Go de RAM et 1 To de SSD pour jouer pleinement la carte du PC polyvalent.
Depuis quelques années maintenant, les mini PC ne sont plus des curiosités technologiques, mais bien de véritables alternatives aux tours traditionnelles. Et c’est précisément sur ce terrain que GEEKOM entend jouer avec son A5 Pro 2026 Edition. Un format très discret, une configuration suffisamment musclée pour les usages du quotidien et surtout une machine qui peut facilement trouver sa place sur un bureau sans jamais l’encombrer.
À l’occasion de cette offre temporaire, son tarif passe de 549 à 439 €, à condition d’utiliser le code promo CLUA5110. De quoi bénéficier d’une réduction de 110 €, valable jusqu’au 11 octobre.
Un Ryzen 5 et 16 Go de RAM dans un format compact
Au cœur du GEEKOM A5 Pro 2026 Edition, on retrouve donc un processeur AMD Ryzen 5 7530U, accompagné de 16 Go de mémoire vive DDR4. Une combinaison qui vise avant tout la polyvalence et qui va permettre la bureautique, la navigation avec de nombreux onglets, la visioconférence, l’usage multimédia ou encore l’utilisation de certains logiciels relativement exigeants.
Le processeur AMD de la série Ryzen 7000 permet ainsi au Mini PC de ne pas se limiter aux tâches basiques. Les 16 Go de RAM offrent de leur côté une marge confortable pour travailler avec plusieurs applications ouvertes simultanément.
Autre élément important de cette configuration, la présence d’un SSD de 1 To. De quoi disposer d’un espace de stockage particulièrement conséquent pour les applications, les documents, les photos et autres vidéos, sans avoir pour cela à investir dans un disque externe. L’ensemble est d’ailleurs évolutif, avec la possibilité de grimper jusqu’à 64 Go de RAM et 3 To de SSD.
Un Mini PC pensé pour accompagner tous les usages
L’intérêt d’un modèle comme le GEEKOM A5 Pro réside aussi dans son format bien sûr. Là où un PC traditionnel impose généralement de réserver une place conséquente sous ou à côté du bureau, le Mini PC peut se faire beaucoup plus discret (sans compter un bruit de fonctionnement inférieur à 30 dB), et peut tout à fait venir se positionner sur le bureau.
Cette compacité lui permet également d’être envisagé dans différents contextes. Par exemple comme ordinateur principal dans un espace de travail réduit, comme machine familiale ou encore comme PC multimédia. La connectique est complète (ports USB-A, USB-C, HDMI, Ethernet…), sans oublier les connectivités Bluetooth 5.2 et Wi-Fi 6.C’est d’ailleurs tout l’intérêt de cette catégorie de machines, qui ne cherchent pas forcément à remplacer une grosse tour spécialisée, mais plutôt à proposer une solution capable de répondre à une grande variété de besoins.
GEEKOM présente ainsi son A5 Pro comme un PC polyvalent, conçu pour fonctionner aussi bien dans le cadre d’une utilisation classique que dans des scénarios où la machine doit rester disponible sur de longues périodes, avec une promesse de fonctionnement 7 jours sur 7 et 24 heures sur 24.
Le GEEKOM A5 Pro passe à 439 € avec le code CLUA5110
C’est aussi le tarif qui constitue ici l’un des principaux arguments. Affiché habituellement à 549 €, le GEEKOM A5 Pro 2026 Edition est actuellement proposé à 439 €, soit 110 € d’économie grâce au code CLUA5110, avec une offre valable jusqu’au 11 octobre 2026.
À ce prix, la configuration réunit donc un Ryzen 5 7530U, 16 Go de DDR4 et un SSD de 1 To dans un format Mini PC particulièrement compact. Pour profiter de la remise, il suffit de passer par la boutique GEEKOM et d’appliquer le code au moment de la commande.

articles.title: Private cloud gets an AI-era infrastructure reset - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
AI is rewriting the private cloud playbook as Dell moves beyond traditional HCI
Private cloud infrastructure is taking on a new role as enterprises rethink where workloads should run and how systems should be built for artificial intelligence.
The shift is being driven by several pressures at once. Organizations are looking more closely at public cloud costs, seeking greater control over data and weighing how quickly infrastructure can adapt as AI workloads place new demands on compute, storage and networking. At the same time, changing virtualization strategies are creating pressure for systems that support more than one operating environment.
These trends are reshaping the role of private cloud. Rather than recreating traditional data centers, enterprises are looking for infrastructure that provides cloud-like simplicity while allowing compute and storage to scale independently.
“It’s about economics, it’s about control and it’s about AI sovereignty,” said Dave Vellante, chief analyst at theCUBE Research. “But to make private clouds viable in this AI era, some things have to change. There’s a massive demand for disaggregated architectures and infrastructure, but customers, they don’t want to be integrators all over again.”
During the “Rethinking Private Cloud for the Age of Intelligence” event — an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio — Vellante spoke with Caitlin Gordon (pictured, right), vice president of product at Dell Technologies Inc., and Jodey Hogeland (left), PowerStore global evangelist at Dell about how private cloud architecture is changing as enterprises focus on economics, infrastructure flexibility, automation and AI. During the event, Brian Beeler, editor of StorageReview.com also provided an in-depth look at Dell PowerStore Elite and the automation technologies supporting the platform. (* Disclosure below.)
Private cloud priorities change
Renewed interest in private cloud reflects a significant change in what enterprises expect from infrastructure. Control remains important, but cost, flexibility and investment protection are moving higher on the priority list.
“In some sense, private clouds are cool again,” Gordon said. “Having control is becoming top of mind for a lot of customers. But the environment has completely changed from what it was just a few years ago or, in some cases, just a few months ago. So, they’re dealing with a lot.”
The challenge is that private cloud requirements have changed alongside the applications running on top of them. Data volumes continue to expand, infrastructure prices are putting pressure on budgets and enterprises want the freedom to change operating environments without replacing the underlying hardware.
“Really, the number one thing that we hear from customers is cost, and then openness, flexibility and then simplicity,” Gordon said. “Bringing all three of those things together is critical for our customers because, ultimately, every dollar that they’re spending on their IT budget is a decision that they’re making and a trade-off that they’re making.”
That is contributing to greater interest in disaggregated architecture. Hyperconverged infrastructure brought simplified deployment and management by tightly integrating compute and storage, but enterprises could also find themselves scaling resources they did not necessarily need.
A disaggregated model allows those components to grow separately while retaining an integrated operational experience.
“If all I need is to dynamically scale the compute infrastructure, I’ve got the freedom, the cost structures and the affordability to do that,” Hogeland said. “If all I need to do is scale the storage infrastructure, I’ve got the freedom, the cost-effective capabilities to be able to do that.”
Dell Private Cloud targets infrastructure flexibility
Dell Private Cloud was designed around this shift toward independent scaling while retaining the simplicity associated with HCI. The platform separates compute and storage while using automation to manage the infrastructure as an integrated system.
The approach also addresses changes underway in virtualization. Enterprises that previously standardized around one hypervisor are increasingly considering multiple environments based on workload requirements.
Dell Private Cloud supports VMware, Red Hat OpenShift, Nutanix and Microsoft Azure Local, allowing organizations to deploy different operating environments on reusable infrastructure, according to Gordon.
“Dell Private Cloud gives you a disaggregated infrastructure, the ability to buy just the infrastructure you need and then scale independently,” she said. “But, importantly, it keeps the simplicity of HCI.”
The ability to change software environments without replacing the underlying infrastructure is emerging as an important consideration for customers. Most current Dell Private Cloud deployments still involve VMware, but many organizations are simultaneously evaluating other options, Gordon added.
“The value prop they’re buying into is the fact that they know they have the escape hatch to where they’re going to go into the future,” she said. “It’s really that optionality that they’re buying into.”
PowerStore Elite focuses on density and efficiency
Storage is another piece of the private cloud architecture being reshaped by AI. Higher-performance workloads require faster access to increasingly large datasets, while data centers face physical constraints involving rack space, power and cooling.
Dell is addressing those requirements with PowerStore Elite, its latest primary storage platform. The system provides up to 6:1 data reduction while increasing performance and density compared with previous generations, according to the company.
“We’re delivering 3x the performance that we were in previous generations,” Hogeland said. “We’re delivering 3x the efficiencies that we were in previous generations. And we’re delivering all of that in a 3-rack unit form factor.”
The density improvements have implications beyond storage itself. Consolidating infrastructure can free rack capacity, electrical connections and cooling resources that enterprises can redirect toward AI servers.
Organizations are increasingly evaluating infrastructure modernization through this broader data-center lens, Hogeland added.
“We have customers … having to accelerate infrastructure purchases to consolidate, to get more efficient,” he said.
Automation changes private cloud operations
Separating compute and storage can provide flexibility, but it also creates the potential for additional management complexity. Dell is seeking to address that problem through the Dell Automation Platform, which applies lifecycle management and infrastructure validation across the private cloud stack. The goal is to carry forward the operational experience of HCI without tying customers to tightly coupled infrastructure.
“Our test shows … up to 66% time savings with the Dell Private Cloud and all the automation software versus managing a 3-tier environment without that automation,” Gordon said.
The architecture can also make infrastructure updates more granular. Instead of applying a large update across an entire integrated stack, administrators can target storage, compute or individual security patches.
“We can enable an update of just the storage or just the compute or a security patch,” Gordon said. “And that allows customers to have the agility that they need today for updates but still have the trust in the validation and the simplicity that they’re used to.”
Storage itself is becoming more automated as well. PowerStore includes Dynamic Node Affinity, which manages where volumes are placed and can adjust backend paths based on performance and workload conditions.
“We’re really having conversations now about autonomous infrastructure,” Hogeland said. “The storage is so intelligent, it’s so smart, that it’s making decisions in and of itself.”
PowerStore moves deeper into the automation stack
Beeler examined PowerStore Elite in the lab, highlighting hardware changes designed to increase density while making the system easier to manage.
The platform includes 40 E3 SSD bays and moves NVRAM and battery backup functionality into the controllers, freeing the front of the system entirely for storage. Dell has also moved to standard OCP network interface cards, providing more flexibility for connectivity. Yet the more significant change is how storage participates in Dell’s broader private cloud automation model, according to Beeler.
Dell Automation Platform Orchestrator can stand up a private cloud using configuration files and deployment blueprints. The workflow incorporates PowerStore hardware validation, compute and networking preparation, hypervisor installation and storage provisioning.
“The array stops being a destination you provision to and becomes a resource the platform composes for you,” Beeler said.
The system is also designed to reduce the level of specialized storage expertise required for ongoing administration.
“This is a very big deal, especially as some of the traditional graybeard storage admins age out,” Beeler said. “These tools make it easier for even an IT generalist or a service provider to help manage your PowerStore estate in a very intuitive way using tools that most of us are very familiar with.”
Rethinking the private cloud trade-off
Private cloud infrastructure has historically required organizations to balance two competing models: tightly integrated systems that simplified operations and disaggregated systems that offered greater flexibility. Dell’s strategy is to remove some of that trade-off by combining independently scalable infrastructure with software-driven management and automation.
“They can have the flexibility and the efficiency of a disaggregated infrastructure, and yet they can have the experience … of that simplicity all built into one platform,” Gordon said. “And it doesn’t lock them into any one operating environment.”
That flexibility could become increasingly important as organizations decide where to run AI and how much infrastructure they are willing to commit to any single virtualization or cloud platform.
For Hogeland, the changing role of the infrastructure administrator is another sign of what is ahead. Storage teams are increasingly responsible for broader environments while AI-based systems handle more routine operational work.
“A storage admin is no longer just traditionally a storage admin, but they’re becoming managers of AI-based agents that are doing tasks on their behalf,” he said.
Private cloud is therefore becoming less about recreating the data center models of the past and more about building an infrastructure layer capable of changing with workloads. As AI puts greater pressure on data, compute capacity and operating costs, the ability to scale resources independently while automating how those resources are managed could define the next phase of enterprise private cloud.
Stay tuned for the complete video interview, part of SiliconANGLE’s and theCUBE’s coverage of Dell’s “Rethinking Private Cloud for the Age of Intelligence” event.

articles.title: L'iconique Yeti revient chez Logitech avec IA et capteur 3D pour régler le son à votre place
articles.text:
Capteur de proximité, réduction du bruit par IA et écran couleur… Logitech modernise son célèbre microphone USB avec une promesse simple : conserver une voix régulière, même lorsque son utilisateur bouge devant son bureau.
Plus besoin de rester figé devant son micro pour conserver un niveau sonore constant. Officiellement présenté ce 23 septembre, le Logitech Yeti 2 veut corriger l’un des petits travers des enregistrements à domicile : cette voix qui s’éloigne dès que l’on recule sur sa chaise ou que l’on tourne la tête. Héritier du microphone lancé par Blue en 2009, le Yeti 2 arrivera d'ici à fin septembre en noir ou en blanc, à 170 euros.
Un micro qui s’adapte à vos mouvements
La principale nouveauté tient dans un capteur de proximité 3D. Logitech explique qu’il permet d’ajuster automatiquement le gain, l’équilibre sonore et la directivité du microphone selon les déplacements de son utilisateur. Là où le Yeti original demandait de régler soi-même l’amplification et de choisir parmi quatre modes de captation, son successeur veut prendre une partie de ces décisions à votre place.
Une réduction du bruit par IA doit également atténuer les sons indésirables en se concentrant sur la voix. L’écran couleur ne se contente pas d’afficher les niveaux : son petit Yeti animé avertit l’utilisateur lorsque le gain est trop faible ou trop élevé, ou lorsque le signal sature. La molette permet aussi de sélectionner des préréglages et d’ajuster l’égaliseur sans passer systématiquement par l'utilitaire maison, G Hub.
La fiche technique progresse aussi, avec un enregistrement jusqu’en 24 bits/48 kHz, contre 16 bits/48 kHz pour le premier modèle. De quoi offrir davantage de latitude au traitement audio, sans garantir pour autant une voix plus agréable à l’écoute.
Face à Elgato et Shure, Logitech mise sur son capteur 3D
À 170 euros, le Yeti 2 retrouvera notamment l’Elgato Wave:3 MK.2, qui facilite déjà le réglage du niveau sonore et limite les risques de saturation. Le Shure MV6 adapte lui aussi automatiquement son gain à la distance et au volume de la voix, tout en réduisant les bruits de fond.
Logitech compte donc surtout se distinguer par son capteur 3D et sa capacité annoncée à modifier la directivité du micro en fonction des mouvements. Une proposition intéressante pour les streamers, podcasteurs et vidéastes qui ne passent pas leur temps parfaitement alignés devant leur microphone.
Lors de la présentation à la presse mi-septembre (juste avant l'événement Logitech Play de Varsovie), le prototype du Yeti 2 n’était toutefois pas assez abouti pour constater sa qualité sonore et émettre un premier avis. Dix-sept ans après le lancement du modèle conçu par Blue, ce nouveau Yeti sera-t-il à la hauteur de son aîné ? Logitech a clairement la pression…
- La qualité audio des différents modes
- Le rapport qualité-prix
- La qualité de fabrication
- Design compact et moderne
- Qualité audio décente
- Réduction de bruit efficace
- La finition soignée
- La simplicité d'utilisation
- L'accessoire permettant de le fixer sur n'importe quel pied

articles.title: Elon Musk au capital de Paramount ? Le projet financier qui fait trembler Hollywood
articles.text:
À quelques jours de boucler le rachat de Warner Bros. Discovery pour 110 milliards de dollars (environ 97 milliards d’euros), Paramount cherche de l’argent frais pour financer l’opération. Selon des sources proches du dossier citées par Semafor le 23 septembre 2026, les dirigeants du groupe, mené par son CEO David Ellison, ont évoqué l’idée de proposer à Elon Musk de rejoindre les investisseurs qui apportent des fonds propres à l’opération. Le milliardaire n’est qu’un des noms envisagés.
Semafor n’a pas pu connaître le montant envisagé. Le choix du patron de X, Tesla et SpaceX n’a en tout cas rien d’un hasard. Elon Musk est proche du père de David Ellison, Larry Ellison, cofondateur d’Oracle. Larry Ellison a investi dans Tesla en 2018, a siégé à son conseil d’administration, et a apporté 1 milliard de dollars (environ 880 millions d’euros) au rachat de Twitter par Musk en 2022. Larry Ellison garantit personnellement plus de 40 milliards de dollars (environ 35 milliards d’euros) de fonds propres dans le rachat. Selon Semafor, un chèque de Musk allégerait cette charge et diversifierait l’actionnariat du nouvel ensemble.
Un soutien rassurant pour Wall Street et Paramount, mais risqué politiquement
Sur le plan financier, un chèque du milliardaire serait un signe de confiance fort envers le futur Paramount-Warner Bros., souligne Semafor. Très suivi par les petits porteurs, Elon Musk pourrait aussi rassurer Wall Street quant à la solidité du financement de ce géant du divertissement.
Sur le plan politique, l’arrivée d’Elon Musk au capital serait bien plus délicate. L’idée que l’homme d’affaires puisse détenir des parts, même minoritaires, dans des médias d’information comme CNN et CBS News inquiéterait les démocrates, déjà alarmés en 2024 par son argent, son poids politique et son contrôle de X. Même s’il est peu probable que Musk obtienne un rôle opérationnel dans la gestion des rédactions, sa présence au capital de CNN et de CBS News ferait probablement réagir Washington, estime Semafor.
Un rachat débloqué, mais sous conditions
Ces discussions ont été rendues publiques deux jours après l’accord conclu ce lundi 21 septembre entre Paramount et les 12 États américains qui l’attaquaient en justice pour bloquer le rachat. Le groupe évite ainsi de verser aux actionnaires de Warner Bros. Discovery 7 millions de dollars (environ 6 millions d’euros) par jour de retard au-delà du 1er octobre. David Zaslav, CEO de Warner Bros. Discovery, table sur une finalisation au plus tard début octobre. En échange, Paramount s’est engagé auprès des États à sortir 30 films par an au cinéma et à dépenser 1,5 milliard de dollars (environ 1,3 milliard d’euros) de plus dans la production, sous la surveillance d’un juge pendant cinq ans.
Le rachat touche aussi le streaming, puisqu’il réunit HBO Max et Paramount+ sous le même toit. Le groupe doit surtout faire face à sa dette. Il sortira du rachat avec plus de 80 milliards de dollars de dettes (environ 70 milliards d’euros) pour environ 3 milliards de dollars (2,6 milliards d’euros) de trésorerie disponible par an, selon The Hollywood Reporter. Chaque dollar consacré aux intérêts manquera pour financer des films et des séries.
Elon Musk a fait de la lutte contre le « virus woke » l’un de ses combats favoris sur X. S’il investissait dans le groupe qui possède DC Comics, Star Trek, Harry Potter et Game of Thrones, il n’aurait sans doute aucun rôle formel dans la gestion, comme le souligne Semafor. Il pourrait en revanche commenter publiquement les choix du groupe sur X. Paramount n’a pas souhaité commenter.

articles.title: Vergleich mit Crispr: Anthropic-Agent soll eigenständig neues Enzymsystem entdeckt haben
articles.text:
Nach Analyse von DNA-Datenbanken: Claude soll eigenständig neues Enzymsystem entdeckt haben
Erst kürzlich hat Anthropic, das Unternehmen hinter dem Chatbot Claude, die Eröffnung eines neuen Biotech-Labors bekannt gegeben. Das Ziel bestehe darin, mithilfe von KI echte biologische Experimente durchzuführen. Jetzt meldet das Unternehmen eine Entdeckung, die es mit der „Genschere“ Crispr vergleicht. Demnach benötigten rund 950 Claude-Agenten 21 Stunden und 210 Millionen Tokens, um das neuartige Enzymsystem selbstständig zu finden.
Claude-Agenten durchforsten DNA-Datenbank
Laut Anthropic begannen viele bahnbrechende biologische Entdeckungen damit, dass Forscher:innen ungewöhnliche Naturmuster bemerkten. Genau diesen Prozess will das Team jetzt mit KI systematisieren. „Im Frühjahr 2026 gründeten wir eine Forschungsgruppe, um zu untersuchen, ob allgemeine KI-Modelle solche Entdeckungen systematisieren und beschleunigen können”, heißt es in einem Blogbeitrag über die neue Entdeckung. „Wir glauben, dass diese Beschleunigung durch die Etablierung einer neuen Art der biologischen Forschung zustande kommen wird, bei der Agenten in jedem Schritt des Prozesses mit Menschen zusammenarbeiten.”
Rund 950 Claude-Agenten durchsuchten über 21 Stunden eine riesige DNA‑Datenbank. Einer davon habe beim Durchforsten roher DNA-Sequenzen schließlich eine auffällige Wiederholungssequenz entdeckt. Er soll die Wiederholungen gezählt, Muster mit bekannten Systemen verglichen und entsprechende Fachliteratur geprüft haben. Das bislang unbekannte Enzymsystem weise Crispr-ähnliche Eigenschaften auf. Von den Forscher:innen wird es als „array-assoziierte Reverse Transkriptasen“ (ART) bezeichnet. Laut Anthropic sei Claude eigenständig vorgegangen – das Forschungsteam hätte nur den Prompt und die Laborarbeit übernommen.
Wie nützlich ist die Neuentdeckung wirklich?
Die Entdeckung der „Genschere“ Crispr stellte für die Medizin einen bedeutenden Meilenstein dar. Sie schneidet und verändert DNA an genau definierten Stellen und machte es dadurch erstmals möglich, die genetische Ursache von Krankheiten direkt zu korrigieren, anstatt nur die Symptome zu behandeln. Der Vergleich mit dieser Entdeckung heizt die Erwartungen also gezielt an.
Feng Zhang gilt als einer der Pioniere der Crispr-Genom-Editierung. Er ist als Professor am MIT sowie am Broad Institute tätig. „Dies ist ein spannendes Beispiel dafür, wie KI-Agenten zu biologischen Entdeckungen beitragen können”, sagte er laut Anthropic nach Durchsicht des Preprints. „Die Identifizierung von RNA-Wiederholungssequenzen im Zusammenhang mit reversen Transkriptasen ist wirklich faszinierend und verdient weitere Untersuchung.“
Anthropic will in die Forschung expandieren
Trotz der Vergleiche mit Crispr bleibt zunächst unklar, ob die neue Entdeckung praktische Anwendungen finden wird. Die Ankündigung erfolgt zu einem Zeitpunkt, an dem Anthropic versucht, mehr Wissenschaftler:innen für sein Labor zu gewinnen und in Bereiche wie die Arzneimittelforschung zu expandieren. Der Schritt passt auch zu den Versprechen führender KI-Labore, dass ihre Technologie bei der Bekämpfung von Krankheiten helfen könnte. Anthropic-CEO Dario Amodei hat selbst kürzlich in einem Post auf X angedeutet, dass KI die meisten schweren Krankheiten innerhalb von fünf bis zehn Jahren heilen könnte.
Derzeit laufen laut Anthropic weitere Experimente zur Funktionsweise von ART. Das Unternehmen habe die ersten Ergebnisse veröffentlicht, um der wissenschaftlichen Gemeinschaft zu zeigen, dass Claude autonom Anomalien erkennen und Analysen vorantreiben kann, um biologische Entdeckungen anzustoßen. Am Ende des Blogbeitrags lädt das Unternehmen andere dazu ein, Vorschläge für weiterführende Forschungsfragen einzureichen. „Wir möchten gerne mit anderen Wissenschaftler:innen zusammenarbeiten, um diesen Ansatz auf ein breites Spektrum von Problemen in der Genomik und in anderen Bereichen auszuweiten”, heißt es hier.

articles.title: Hubble Network raises $200M to bring global coverage to all Bluetooth LE devices - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Hubble Network raises $200M to bring global coverage to all Bluetooth LE devices
Hubble Network Inc. is doing something nobody expected was possible by connecting Bluetooth to satellites, and today announced it has raised $200 million in a Series C round to build out the capability.
With Hubble’s product, any device with a Bluetooth LE, or Low Energy, radio can connect to satellites orbiting kilometers above.
Unlike classic Bluetooth, LE can transmit data at a fraction of the power using small bursts, letting small devices run for months, or even years, on a single coin-cell battery. It also runs on the same 2.4 gigahertz frequency as Wi-Fi, typically with a range of 100 meters.
Hubble is building a constellation of 60 low-Earth orbit satellites that can interact with a ground-based network to monitor objects embedded with Bluetooth chips, including packages, vehicles and pharmaceuticals.
The satellite is on track to go online by 2030 and will work alongside 100 million gateways on the ground across 170 countries and more than 3 million square miles.
“When we said we’d connect Bluetooth chips to satellites, most of the industry said the physics wouldn’t allow it,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Alex Haro. “Today we’re turning that early skepticism into a global opportunity.”
Smith Point Capital led the round, with participation from Seraphim, Carthona Capital, Earthshot Ventures, Y Combinator and RPM Ventures. Today’s funding brings the company’s total raised to $300 million at a $1.6 billion valuation, one year after its $70 million Series B.
The technology turns any Bluetooth LE radio already inside a device into global connectivity for location and sensor data. That means a package can send its location and a small amount of data wherever it goes, such as temperature and pressure readings.
The company said its newest design adds under 50 cents to the total materials, roughly a 10th of the cost of a cellular modem and a 15th of a satellite modem’s cost. Until the advent of this technology, tracking any individual box or device ended at the pallet and was extremely costly, sometimes on average $25 or more per device, meaning only the most valuable commodity or bulk shipment gets tracked.
Hubble said over the past year, it partnered with Texas Instruments Inc. to send location and sensor data without the need for gateways, GPS or cellular. The company also partnered with InPlay Inc. to pair a sub-$1 chip with Hubble’s gateways for item-level tracking at RFID tag scale and with Reelables Inc. to print active wireless smart labels for cargo.

articles.title: This guy has spent two years hunting fake job listings on LinkedIn, and found 60,000 of them
articles.text:
Big quote: Verified profiles, company pages, and polished job listings are being used to lure job seekers into scams that can cost them money or expose their personal information. Jay Jones, a Chicago-area job seeker who calls himself The Profiler, has made it his mission to find them. Since being laid off from an advertising role in late 2023, Jones says he has helped get nearly 60,000 fake job listings removed from the internet, most of them from LinkedIn. He has also flagged about 7,000 profiles that he believes were used in job scams.
The fraud is not limited to obvious fake accounts. Some scammers create batches of recruiter profiles using copied photos and similar account details. Others take over dormant, verified LinkedIn accounts and attach them to legitimate companies. Still others place job ads on legitimate company pages that direct applicants to outside websites or email addresses.
The approach is becoming increasingly sophisticated. Jones said scammers use artificial intelligence to tailor job pitches to a person's résumé or career history. A recruiter might tell an applicant that their résumé needs work and then offer to help for a fee. Other scams seek more valuable information, including a driver's license or Social Security number.
Jones recently came across several LinkedIn accounts using the name Linda Anthony. The accounts used the same image, showed recent creation dates, and listed similar roles at "Confidential Jobs." One profile described Linda Anthony as a contract recruiter in Smyrna, Ga., while another identified her as a contract specialist in California.
Jones said the profile URLs also appeared to follow the same pattern, suggesting the accounts had been created in bulk. After he posted about them online, the links went dark.
Image credit: The Wall Street Journal
"You turn the lights on," he told The Wall Street Journal, "and the roaches run."
The scams are landing at a difficult time for people looking for work. In August, 27% of unemployed Americans had been searching for a job for more than six months, near the highest level in more than a decade outside the pandemic.
LinkedIn said its automated systems stop most scam activity before users see it. The company said it blocked nearly 90 million fake accounts before they went live in the second half of 2025. It has also introduced new safety features and worked with the FBI this summer to educate job seekers about scams.
Still, the platform faces a persistent problem: fake accounts and fake listings can borrow credibility from real people and real companies.
One scheme Jones has tracked involves hijacked LinkedIn accounts. Some users verify their identities on the platform, receive a verification badge, and later stop using their profiles. Scammers can take control of those accounts, change the work history, and list the account holder as a recruiter for a legitimate business.
That can give a scammer a verified profile and a company affiliation at the same time.
Jones found several such accounts listed as employees of Argenta Talent Acquisition, a Colorado recruiting firm. One account belonged to a dentist in Chile. Argenta CEO Kelley Barcus said the bogus profiles created a direct threat to her company.
"It's my brand, it's my reputation," she said.
Barcus hired Jones to get the accounts disconnected from Argenta's LinkedIn page. LinkedIn accepted reports on the profiles, but the accounts had 14 days to update their information or appeal before LinkedIn could remove their company affiliation. LinkedIn said that process can help correct inaccurate employment information.
Jones said the delay gave scammers more time to reach job seekers. "Scammers don't deserve fairness," he said. "It's economic terrorism."
Oscar Rodriguez, LinkedIn's vice president of trust product, said scammers adapt quickly as platforms add new defenses. LinkedIn asks recruiters to verify their identities, but Rodriguez said verification doesn't guarantee that a profile or job posting is legitimate.
The company plans to introduce a tool later this month that would allow verified employers to immediately remove users' affiliations with their companies.
Jones also looks for fraud inside legitimate company pages. In one case, he found what appeared to be 30 job listings on Hyundai Motor's verified LinkedIn page. The positions included data-entry specialist and customer-service representative. Screenshots reviewed by The Wall Street Journal showed that the ads contained errors and linked to an outside site not affiliated with Hyundai. Applicants were told to email résumés to an outside address.
He found a similar issue involving Capital One. Job ads for administrative assistants appeared on LinkedIn but led to an unaffiliated website. Jones compared the listings with Capital One's own career site, where similar openings were generally listed under titles such as senior administrative assistant or administrative assistant III.
Hyundai and Capital One said they work with LinkedIn to remove fraudulent job postings.
For Jones, the work has become more than a side project. He still searches for a permanent job, drives for Uber, and trains cybersecurity professionals to recognize scam tactics. He also seeks paid speaking work, raises money online, and sells apparel with anti-scam slogans.
He often keeps about 50 browser tabs open while tracking leads, he said, and his browser crashes several times a week.

articles.title: Top produit – La montre connectée Garmin Fenix 8 à 675,00 €
articles.text:
Top produit – La montre connectée Garmin Fenix 8 à 675,00 €
La montre connectée Garmin Fenix 8 s'affiche aujourd'hui à 675,00 € chez Amazon et Joybuy. C'est actuellement l'un des meilleurs produit de notre comparatif.
Montre multisport par excellence chez Garmin, la Fenix monte encore un peu plus en gamme avec sa version 8. Elle intègre désormais un haut-parleur, un micro, un écran Amoled, un profondimètre et revoit son interface. De quoi ravir les sportifs de l'extrême et athlètes connectés.

Points forts
- Dalle Amoled plus lumineuse et offrant plus d’informations que les écrans MIP transflectifs.
- Matériaux solides et belles finitions.
- Micro et haut-parleur.
- Lampe torche.
- Autonomie correcte pour un écran Amoled.
- Précision du GPS et du cardiofréquencemètre.
- Très bonne réactivité de l’écran tactile.
Points faibles
- Montre lourde au cadran épais.
- Interface repensée, mais toujours aussi dense (plusieurs jours sont nécessaires pour s’y habituer).
- L’app ne change pas, mais pourrait être plus intuitive.
- Utilisateurs iOS toujours plus lésés que les utilisateurs Android.
Avec la Fenix 8, Garmin enfonce le clou et assoit sa position d’expert sur le marché. Montre connectée résolument tournée vers le sport, elle se targue d'être une spécialiste des activités outdoor grâce à des matériaux particulièrement résistants et des capteurs très précis. Pour de l’endurance ou du fractionné, la tocante suit la cadence sans flancher. Ceci étant, Garmin ne néglige pas les utilisateurs connectés pour autant. Cette montre à tout faire intègre des équipements lifestyle bienvenus, qui la rendent agréable à porter sans être un sportif acharné. Avec un écran Amoled et une autonomie correcte, la montre connectée haut de gamme se peaufine. Reste à savoir si tous ces équipements sont nécessaires et si le prix demandé, plutôt élevé, est justifié.

articles.title: CISA: Ransomware gangs now exploiting critical TeamCity flaw
articles.text:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warned federal agencies on Wednesday that ransomware gangs are now also exploiting a critical JetBrains TeamCity vulnerability patched in July.
JetBrains patched the security flaw (tracked as CVE-2026-63077) on July 25 in TeamCity On-Premises versions 2025.11.7 and 2026.1.3, saying it is a critical authentication bypass vulnerability that lets attackers with HTTP(S) access execute arbitrary operating system commands.
"An unauthenticated attacker could exploit the vulnerability via the TeamCity agent polling protocol to bypass authentication checks and execute arbitrary operating system commands with the privileges of the TeamCity server process," it said.
"Depending on the privileges granted to the TeamCity server process, a successful attack could expose TeamCity data, configurations, and stored credentials, modify server state, and potentially compromise the integrity of build artifacts and downstream CI/CD pipelines."
Almost two weeks later, on August 5, CISA added CVE-2026-63077 to its catalog of actively exploited vulnerabilities and ordered U.S. federal agencies to secure their networks against ongoing attacks within three days.
JetBrains confirmed that the flaw was exploited in the wild on August 7, shared indicators of compromise, and urged customers who couldn't immediately patch their servers to limit access to trusted networks.
Now exploited in ransomware attacks
While CISA has not yet shared information about attacks targeting CVE-2026-63077, it updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog (KEV) again on Wednesday, flagging the vulnerability as being abused by ransomware gangs.
In total, since October 2023, the cybersecurity agency has tagged four TeamCity security issues as exploited in the wild, all of which have also been abused in ransomware attacks.
Security threat watchdog Shadowserver is now tracking just over 160 TeamCity servers unpatched against the CVE-2026-63077 flaw, down from an initial 700 Internet-exposed servers vulnerable to attacks spotted right after the vulnerability was patched.
Because state-backed hacking groups and ransomware gangs have often leveraged TeamCity vulnerabilities in attacks, IT administrators are advised to patch Internet-exposed servers immediately.
For instance, in October 2024, U.S. and U.K. cyber agencies warned that APT29 hackers linked to Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR) were targeting vulnerable JetBrains TeamCity and Zimbra servers "at a mass scale."
TeamCity is a Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) platform used by software developers and DevOps teams to automate building, testing, and deploying software code.
JetBrains says more than 30,000 DevOps teams use TeamCity at many high-profile companies, including Citibank, Amazon Games, Tesla, and Samsung.
Build your security blueprint for AI-powered attacks
Join Mikko Hyppönen and security leaders from the NFL, CHANEL, and Atlassian for a two-hour digital summit on what AI-speed attacks change, what defenders should stop doing, and how to validate, decide, fix, and re-validate at machine speed.

articles.title: Discord comienza a exigir verificación de edad pese a la oposición de los usuarios
articles.text:
Discord comenzará a implementar desde este miércoles 23 de setiembre nuevas medidas de verificación de edad para sus usuarios, después de haber retrasado inicialmente el despliegue debido a las críticas de la comunidad.
La plataforma utilizará información de las cuentas y modelos de aprendizaje automático para determinar si una persona pertenece al grupo de adultos, adolescentes o si su edad no ha podido ser confirmada.
PUBLICIDAD
La compañía sostiene que más del 90 % de sus usuarios no tendrá que realizar una verificación adicional. En esos casos, Discord utilizará señales que ya forman parte de la actividad habitual de las cuentas, como su antigüedad, información del dispositivo y determinados patrones de uso.
El cambio responde también a la expansión de las leyes que exigen controles de edad en servicios digitales. Según Stanislav Vishnevskiy, director de tecnología de Discord, la plataforma ya tuvo que implementar este tipo de medidas en regiones como Brasil y Texas.
Discord utilizará un sistema para estimar la edad
La plataforma explica que su sistema de aprendizaje automático ha sido entrenado para identificar patrones de comportamiento asociados con distintos grupos de edad. Entre las señales utilizadas están el tiempo que lleva activa una cuenta, el dispositivo desde el que se conecta y determinadas características de su actividad.
PUBLICIDAD
Discord asegura que no utilizará el contenido de los mensajes, los datos del perfil ni atributos demográficos para realizar esta estimación.
La compañía explica que el sistema parte de una diferencia general en los patrones de uso. Por ejemplo, la forma en que una persona adolescente utiliza la plataforma puede diferir de la actividad habitual de un adulto en aspectos como las comunidades a las que pertenece o la manera en que interactúa con otros usuarios.
La tecnología se entrenó utilizando datos cuya edad había sido confirmada de forma fiable, obtenidos en el contexto de las obligaciones de verificación que Discord ya había tenido que cumplir en determinadas regiones.
PUBLICIDAD
Más del 90 % de los usuarios no tendrá que comprobar su edad
La principal diferencia para los usuarios será que quienes sean identificados como adultos podrán continuar utilizando Discord sin cambios importantes. La empresa afirma que la mayoría de las cuentas no necesitará pasar por una comprobación adicional.
Cuando el sistema no pueda determinar con suficiente confianza que una persona es adulta, el usuario tendrá la posibilidad de demostrar su edad.
Discord afirma que esta comprobación no requiere necesariamente datos biométricos ni un escaneo de un documento de identidad. Entre las alternativas disponibles está compartir información de una tarjeta de crédito o utilizar el grupo de edad asociado a la cuenta de la App Store de Apple o Google Play.
PUBLICIDAD
De esta manera, la compañía busca ofrecer una vía alternativa para los casos en los que su sistema automático no pueda determinar correctamente la edad de una cuenta.
Los adolescentes tendrán nuevas restricciones
La identificación de una cuenta como perteneciente a un adolescente tendrá consecuencias dentro de la plataforma. Estas cuentas quedarán bloqueadas automáticamente para acceder a servidores y canales que tengan restricciones de edad.
Discord también modificará la forma en que los adolescentes reciben comunicaciones de personas que no forman parte de su lista de amigos. Las solicitudes de mensajes procedentes de desconocidos serán enviadas a una bandeja de entrada separada.
Además, los usuarios adolescentes recibirán alertas cuando acepten solicitudes de amistad de personas con las que no compartan amigos en común.
Para los adultos cuya edad haya sido confirmada, la experiencia de uso de Discord continuará siendo esencialmente la misma.
La privacidad sigue siendo uno de los principales cuestionamientos
Discord había retrasado sus planes de verificación de edad en febrero después de que usuarios expresaran preocupación por el posible uso de datos biométricos y documentos de identidad.
PUBLICIDAD
Las dudas sobre la protección de esta información también están relacionadas con un incidente ocurrido el año pasado, cuando un proveedor externo que trabajaba con Discord sufrió una brecha de seguridad que pudo haber expuesto información de unos 70.000 usuarios, incluidas fotografías de documentos oficiales y selfies utilizadas para verificar identidades.
La compañía reconoce que la verificación de edad genera preocupación, pero sostiene que los cambios regulatorios la obligan a incorporar estos mecanismos en cada vez más mercados.
El despliegue coloca a Discord ante un problema que afecta a numerosas plataformas: cumplir con las nuevas exigencias destinadas a proteger a los menores sin aumentar innecesariamente los riesgos relacionados con la privacidad y la seguridad de los usuarios.

articles.title: Claude Opus 5.5 domine sur la puissance, mais GPT-6 Sol est six fois moins cher à l'usage
articles.text:
Les deux annonces sont tombées à environ 90 minutes d’intervalle. Anthropic a dégainé le premier avec Claude Opus 5.5, son modèle public le plus capable après Fable 5.1 (avec qui il est au coude à coude selon la firme). Le même jour, OpenAI a répliqué avec GPT-6 Sol, la version économique de son haut de gamme GPT-6 Astra. Anthropic mise sur la puissance brute quand OpenAI cherche surtout à alléger la facture. Que vous codiez, manipuliez de nombreux documents ou fassiez tourner un assistant maison, votre choix se joue sur cet écart.
À noter que les deux modèles se pilotent avec un curseur d’« effort », du plus économe au plus poussé, qui décide du temps que le modèle passe à réfléchir avant de répondre.
Les deux modèles sont disponibles depuis ce mardi 22 septembre. Claude Opus 5.5 est accessible via l’API d’Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI et Microsoft Foundry, ainsi que dans les abonnements Claude Pro, Max, Team et Enterprise, mais pas dans la version gratuite. GPT-6 Sol est proposé dans l’API d’OpenAI, dans ChatGPT Work et dans Codex, mais pas encore dans le mode de discussion classique de ChatGPT.
    À lire aussi : 
    Claude Opus 5.5 : Anthropic promet 40 % moins cher et 30 % plus rapide
Côté tarif, tout se compte en tokens, ces petits fragments de texte que les modèles facturent à l’unité, en entrée comme en sortie. Anthropic facture Claude Opus 5.5 à 4 dollars le million de tokens en entrée et 20 dollars en sortie. GPT-6 Sol descend pile à la moitié, à 2 et 10 dollars. Anthropic affirme au passage qu’Opus 5.5 coûte 40 % de moins qu’Opus 5 à l’usage, tandis qu’OpenAI assure que Sol commet environ deux fois moins d’erreurs factuelles que son prédécesseur.
| Caractéristiques | Claude Opus 5.5 | GPT-6 Sol | 
|---|---|---|
| Éditeur | Anthropic | OpenAI | 
| Prix entrée (par million de tokens) | 4 $ (~3,50 €) | 2 $ (~1,75 €) | 
| Prix sortie (par million de tokens) | 20 $ (~17,40 €) | 10 $ (~8,70 €) | 
| Coût par tâche (effort max) | 5,98 $ (~5,20 €) | 1,06 $ (~0,92 €) | 
| Contexte maximum | 1 million de tokens | 1,05 million de tokens | 
Au token, Sol coûte donc deux fois moins cher. Les tests indépendants montrent toutefois des écarts plus marqués, sur les performances comme sur le coût réel d’une tâche.
Les graphiques officiels ne se comparent même pas
Premier écueil quand on veut départager les deux : aucun éditeur ne se mesure au nouveau modèle de l’autre. Comme les annonces sont sorties le même jour, chacun se compare à l’ancienne génération du rival. OpenAI oppose GPT-6 Sol à Claude Opus 5, tandis qu’Anthropic place Opus 5.5 face à GPT-6 Astra et au précédent GPT-5.6 Sol. Les deux annonces n’ont donc quasiment aucun test en commun, et quand un test porte le même nom, il n’est pas mesuré dans les mêmes conditions.
    À lire aussi : 
    « Pas besoin de lui demander de réfléchir » : voici les astuces pour bien utiliser Claude Opus 5.5
Anthropic le reconnaît d’ailleurs dans son annonce : à ce niveau de performance, les écarts aux benchmarks sont devenus « un guide moins fiable des différences réelles ».
Sur les tests indépendants, Opus 5.5 garde dix points d’avance
Pour comparer proprement, il faut passer les deux modèles dans les mêmes tests standardisés, les fameux benchmarks. C’est le travail d’Artificial Analysis, une plateforme qui évalue chaque IA dans des conditions identiques. Claude Opus 5.5 y prend la tête du classement avec 58 points en effort maximal, contre 48 pour GPT-6 Sol. À réglage d’effort égal, Opus garde entre 8 et 12 points d’avance.
|  | Claude Opus 5.5 | GPT-6 Sol | 
| Index Artificial Analysis (effort max) | 58 | 48 | 
Plus parlant encore, Opus 5.5 réglé en effort moyen (51 points) fait déjà mieux que Sol poussé à fond. Métier par métier, Artificial Analysis donne aussi Opus devant partout : en finance (61 contre 48), en juridique (63 contre 51) ou en ingénierie (60 contre 49).
Artificial Analysis a testé Opus 5.5 avec le mécanisme de repli qu’Anthropic active par défaut. Quand un filtre de sécurité bloque une requête, en cybersécurité par exemple, elle peut être confiée à un modèle plus ancien comme Claude Opus 4.8. Ces scores mesurent donc le service tel qu’Anthropic le propose, et pas uniquement Opus 5.5.
GPT-6 Sol coûte moins cher, mais attention aux détails
GPT-6 Sol est deux fois moins cher au token, on l’a vu, mais l’écart se creuse à l’usage. En effort maximal, une tâche du test d’Artificial Analysis revient en moyenne à 5,98 dollars (environ 5,20 euros) avec Opus 5.5, contre 1,06 dollar (environ 0,92 euro) avec Sol, soit près de six fois moins.
En effort maximal, Opus 5.5 réfléchit beaucoup plus longtemps et produit environ quatre fois plus de tokens que Sol pour la même tâche (119 000 contre 31 000 en moyenne). Il est aussi plus lent à démarrer. En effort moyen, Sol commence à répondre au bout de 2 secondes environ, Opus au bout d’une vingtaine de secondes. Sol génère ensuite 114 tokens par seconde, contre 78 pour Opus.
Cette économie a toutefois une limite. Jusqu’à un score d’environ 44 points sur l’index d’Artificial Analysis, Sol reste le moyen le moins cher d’atteindre n’importe quel niveau. Au-delà, il plafonne, et seul Opus continue de grimper. Pour un budget serré, Opus réglé en effort moyen ne coûte que 26 % de plus que Sol poussé à fond, pour environ 3 points de mieux.
Claude Opus 5.5 ou GPT-6 Sol : lequel choisir ?
Pour un agent de code chargé de longues tâches, de l’analyse juridique ou financière, ou des réponses où l’exactitude compte beaucoup, Opus 5.5 justifie sa facture.
Pour un chatbot, du service client, de gros volumes ou de l’automatisation simple, GPT-6 Sol fait presque aussi bien pour une fraction du prix, et répond bien plus vite en effort bas ou moyen. Un point à garder en tête avant de trancher : les scores d’Artificial Analysis bougent souvent dans les jours qui suivent un lancement, et ces écarts pourraient encore évoluer. Nous tâcherons de mettre à jour cet article en conséquence.
    À lire aussi : 
    ChatGPT : son fonctionnement, son potentiel et ses dangers… Le guide ultime pour tout comprendre

articles.title: Como recuperar um SSD corrompido (guia prático) • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Resumo
- Para recuperar dados de um SSD corrompido, você pode usar uma ferramenta como o EaseUS Data Recovery Wizard.
- O EaseUS Data Recovery Wizard pode recuperar dados de mais de 1.000 formatos diferentes e é compatível com vários sistemas de arquivos.
- A solução também é de uso fácil. O passo a passo para recuperar dados com ela é descrito a seguir.
SSDs não estão imunes a falhas. Unidades do tipo podem ser corrompidas por causa de uma queda de energia, por problemas de formatação ou pela ação de um vírus, por exemplo, o que resulta em perda de dados. Mas há métodos para restaurar o SSD e, com a ferramenta certa, você pode recuperar os arquivos perdidos com facilidade.
Ao contrário dos clássicos HDs (discos rígidos), que contam com “pratos” para armazenar dados, os SSDs usam chips de memória Flash para essa função. Apesar dessa diferença, ambas as categorias possibilitam que arquivos perdidos sejam restaurados em caso de partição corrompida, sistema de arquivos danificado e problemas semelhantes.
Isso porque, nessas circunstâncias, o espaço ocupado pelos dados é sinalizado como livre para uso, mas não apagados de imediato, afinal, o erro que causou o problema não faz esses dados serem excluídos automaticamente.
É por isso que, ao usar ferramentas capazes de analisar a unidade, esses dados podem ser recuperados. Mas é preciso que a ferramenta seja sofisticada o suficiente para fazer esse trabalho com eficácia. Uma solução que atende a esse critério é o EaseUS Data Recovery Wizard que, além de confiável, tem uma interface bastante intuitiva.
Cuidados antes de iniciar a recuperação de dados no SSD
Antes de iniciar o procedimento, você deve deixar de usar imediatamente o SSD que teve dados perdidos ou apagados. Não salve, crie ou armazene arquivos nessa unidade para evitar que eles sejam armazenados no espaço ocupado pelos dados a serem restaurados.
Nesse sentido, também é importante que o recuperador de arquivos não seja baixado no SSD a ser analisado. Instale a ferramenta em outra unidade de armazenamento existente no computador.
Se o SSD corrompido for justamente o principal de seu computador, instale-o como uma unidade secundária em outra máquina. Faça a recuperação por meio desta última.
Em todos os casos, a restauração só irá funcionar se a unidade for reconhecida pelo sistema (via BIOS/UEFI ou Gerenciamento de Disco, por exemplo) e, claro, não tenha sofrido danos físicos.
Aviso importante: é comum o TRIM estar ativado no SSD. Essa tecnologia efetivamente apaga os dados de uma área previamente gravada. Por isso, é importante desativar o TRIM antes de iniciar a recuperação dos dados do SSD. Para isso, faça o seguinte:
- no Windows: abra o Prompt de Comando como administrador e digite: 
fsutil behavior set DisableDeleteNotify 1
- no macOS: abra o terminal e digite: sudo trimforce disable
Como recuperar dados do SSD com o EaseUS Data Recovery Wizard?
O passo a passo para usar o EaseUS Data Recovery Wizard para recuperar dados de uma unidade SSD é este (observe como é simples):
1. faça download e instalação
Baixe e instale o EaseUS Data Recovery Wizard no computador a ser usado para recuperar os dados. A ferramenta tem versões para Windows e Mac.
Após o download, siga os passos de instalação, lembrando-se de fazer isso em uma unidade diferente do SSD a ser analisado.
2. selecione o SSD a ser analisado
Abra o EaseUS Data Recovery Wizard e, na coluna à esquerda, escolha o tipo de unidade a ser analisado (no caso, SSD).
Agora, na área à direita, selecione o SSD ou a partição deste que será analisada. Clique no botão de procurar dados perdidos.
3. escolha os arquivos a serem recuperados
Os arquivos que podem ser recuperados serão mostrados pelo EaseUS Data Recovery Wizard. Se houver muitos deles, você pode usar a opção de filtro no topo direito para escolher uma categoria de arquivos (fotos, vídeos, documentos, entre outros). Você também pode usar o campo de busca para encontrar um arquivo específico.
Agora, selecione os arquivos a serem restaurados. Então, clique no botão de recuperação para iniciar o procedimento e aguarde.
Alerta: lembre-se de salvar os arquivos restaurados em uma unidade diferente — nunca salve os dados no SSD analisado!
Como reparar o SSD corrompido após recuperar dados?
Agora que você restaurou os dados do SSD com problemas, é hora de tentar corrigir a falha. Abaixo, você confere como fazer o procedimento em um PC com Windows e no Mac.
Corrigindo o SSD no Windows 11 ou Windows 10
- digite “CMD” no campo de busca da Barra de Tarefas ou do Menu Iniciar;
- clique com o botão direito do mouse em “Prompt de Comando” e escolha “Executar como administrador”;
- no Prompt de Comando, digite: chkdsk X: /f /r (troque ‘X’ pela letra que identifica o SSD).
Corrigindo o SSD no Mac
- no macOS, vá em “Aplicativos” / “Utilitários” / “Utilitário de Disco”; no menu superior, clique em “Visualizar” / “Mostrar Todos os Dispositivos”;
- na lateral, selecione o SSD e clique em “Primeiros Socorros” (“First Aid”);
- clique em “Executar” e aguarde o procedimento ser realizado.
Por que o EaseUS Data Recovery Wizard é recomendado?
Muita gente considera o EaseUS Data Recovery Wizard o melhor software de recuperação de SSD. Isso porque seus atributos incluem:
- capacidade de fazer varreduras profundas e de baixo nível na unidade a ser analisada, permitindo encontrar arquivos até em dispositivos com erro “RAW”, com falha na alocação de espaço ou em partições corrompidas;
- possibilidade de recuperar arquivos em mais de 1.000 formatos diferentes, como JPEG, PNG, DOC, DOCX, PDF, PPTX, MP4, MOV, ZIP e tantos outros;
- compatibilidade não só com SSDs, mas também com HDs, pendrives, cartões de memória, entre vários outros dispositivos de armazenamento;
- suporte a variados sistemas de arquivos, como FAT16, FAT32, ext2, ext3, ext4, ReFS, NTFS, exFAT e mais.
Outra caraterística notável do EaseUS Data Recovery Wizard é o modo de pré-recuperação, que exibe uma prévia de fotos, vídeos, documentos e áudios antes de sua efetiva restauração para que o usuário possa confirmar a integridade dos dados. Por causa de todos esses recursos, o EaseUS Data Recovery Wizard é muito bem avaliado por seus usuários, chegando a registrar 4,9 pontos (de 5) no índice da Trustpilot.
O que fazer se o SSD não for reconhecido?
Em caso de não reconhecimento da unidade, é preciso abrir o computador para verificar se o cabo de dados e o cabo de alimentação do SSD estão íntegros. Desconecte-os e conecte-os novamente. Troque os cabos se o problema persistir.
Você também pode acessar o setup do BIOS/UEFI pressionando botões como Delete, F1 ou F12 (varia conforme a marca do equipamento) e usar os recursos de reconhecimento de SSD por lá.
Se nada disso der certo, é possível que o SSD tenha danos físicos em um ou mais componentes. Neste caso, você pode contratar um serviço de recuperação de dados, a exemplo do EaseUS Manual Data Recovery Services. Se a unidade ainda estiver na garantia, entre em contato com o suporte do fabricante.
O que causa SSD corrompido e como prevenir
As principais causas para falhas que deixam o SSD corrompido ou com partição perdida são listadas abaixo. Note que cada item é seguido de dicas de prevenção:
- queda de energia: conecte o computador a um filtro de linha, no-break ou equipamento que possa protegê-lo em caso de queda ou oscilação na rede elétrica;
- aquecimento excessivo: tome cuidado para não bloquear as saídas de ar de seu desktop ou notebook para evitar superaquecimento;
- remoção indevida: sempre use a função de ejetar do computador antes de desconectar um SSD, se ele for externo; já SSDs internos só devem ser removidos com o computador desligado;
- sobrecarga de atividade: mantenha pelo menos 10% de espaço livre no SSD; isso ajuda a prevenir o desgaste precoce das células de armazenamento;
- desfragmentação: não desfragmente o SSD, pois esse procedimento pode gastar ciclos de escrita desnecessariamente (a desfragmentação é útil somente em HDs);
- firmware com bug ou desatualizado: verifique junto ao fabricante do SSD como obter o firmware (software interno de controle) mais recente para a unidade;
- falha no sistema de arquivos: tabelas de sistemas de arquivos como NTFS e exFAT podem ser corrompidas durante particionamentos incorretos, por isso, somente use softwares confiáveis para esse fim.
Dica final: use ferramentas de diagnóstico periodicamente para checar o estado de “saúde” do SSD. Troque a unidade o quanto antes se encontrar sinais acentuados de desgaste, que ocorrem à medida que as células de memória Flash NAND se aproximam de seu limite de ciclos de gravação.
Como problemas podem ocorrer mesmo com todos os cuidados, convém criar cópias de seus dados seguindo a estratégia de backup 3-2-1:
- mantenha 3 cópias dos dados;
- use 2 mídias diferentes (como um HD externo e um servidor NAS);
- mantenha pelo menos 1 cópia remota (armazenada nas nuvens, por exemplo).
Perguntas frequentes (FAQ)
É possível recuperar dados com o EaseUS Data Recovery Wizard gratuitamente?
Sim. Você pode usar a versão gratuita do EaseUS Data Recovery Wizard, que permite analisar, visualizar e recuperar até 2 GB de dados sem nenhum custo.
O recurso TRIM impede a recuperação de dados do SSD?
Nem sempre. O TRIM apaga arquivos excluídos sob condições de uso normais, mas pode ser desativado automaticamente se o SSD ficar corrompido ou apresentar erro “RAW”, por exemplo. Nessas circunstâncias, os dados brutos continuam alocados nas células de memória Flash NAND, permitindo que o EaseUS Data Recovery Wizard recupere-os.
Como sei que meu SSD tem um dano físico?
Se o SSD não é reconhecido pelo BIOS/UEFI ou não aparece no Gerenciamento de Disco do Windows / Utilitário de Disco do Mac mesmo se estiver corretamente conectado ao computador, provavelmente, ele está com um dano físico (falha de hardware).
Pode-se executar o comando CHKDSK no SSD corrompido antes de recuperar os dados?
Não. Executar o CHKDSK em um SSD corrompido antes da recuperação dos dados pode sobrescrever ou alterar os arquivos existentes ali. Sempre execute o EaseUS Data Recovery Wizard para restaurar os arquivos antes de tentar reparar a unidade.
Quanto tempo leva para o EaseUS Data Recovery Wizard analisar um SSD corrompido?
Não há uma resposta exata para isso, pois o tempo de análise varia de acordo com uma série de parâmetros, como capacidade do SSD, tecnologia de comunicação (SATA ou NVMe) e volume de dados armazenados. Mas, em média, a análise de um SSD NVMe de 500 GB, por exemplo, leva de 10 a 20 minutos para ser concluída.
Conclusão
Não é incomum um SSD ficar corrompido, bem como apresentar falhas no sistema de arquivos ou em partições. Felizmente, há ferramentas que permitem recuperar os arquivos armazenados em uma unidade danificada. O EaseUS Data Recovery Wizard se destaca na missão de recuperar SSDs por ser altamente eficiente.

articles.title: Building a Collaborative Platform Culture in a Bank
articles.text:
A platform is a collaboration system, not infrastructure. Culture follows structure: platform teams can build open support sessions, create super user awards for contributing developers, and establish shared open standards to grow an engineering mindset, Marcy Paramonova and Stéphane Cusin explained in their talk Building Cloud Native Culture in a Bank at KubeCon & CloudNativeCon Europe.
Developers and product teams depend on a platform team, Paramonova said. The platform team depends on application teams, and both need to go forward; for that, they need shared standards.
A platform is not a piece of infrastructure; it’s a collaboration system through which lots of communication goes, Paramonova and Cusin explained in How Open Source Enables Collaboration in Creating a Platform.
Cloud native is a cultural shift, not just a technical one; their transformation journey also required a cultural shift, Paramonova argued. The platform team started offering open support sessions where developers could come, and they could solve their problems with them:
We wanted to step back from the usual support for driver tickets and offer something new and fresh to our users. Many people got interested, including infrastructure, cybersecurity, network, identity, and cloud teams. We sit together, share solutions, and help to solve problems collaboratively.
If every action required a ticket, manual intervention, or direct support from a platform engineer, we would unintentionally create a culture of dependency, Cousin said. Teams would wait for the platform team instead of learning and operating independently.
Paramonova mentioned that they created events to recognize adoption of their platform. They introduced super user awards for developers who actively contributed to improving the platform:
Their feedback, sometimes hard to hear for us and a little bit painful, actually helped us to create something more beautiful and better. So we’re grateful for that.
The activities they organized changed how they perceive and value human skills.
When you use open source with open standards, your skills become very transferable, Paramonova said. You don’t relearn something from zero; you build on a shared foundation that’s shared across the open technologies, she added.
An engineering mindset is the most important thing, Paramonova argued. It’s not what you know today, but your capacity and ability to take new technologies, to learn them, to execute and to operate them:
Being an engineer is about problem solving, being passionate about that, and sharing your passion about problem solving.
Culture follows structure. You cannot wait for culture to emerge on its own; you have to design systems that create the culture you want, Cousin explained:
If your team complains about being interrupted all the time, don’t blame the other team. Ask yourself: have you defined a structure for people to reach out to you?
Kubernetes transformed more than our platform. It transformed how our organization builds software, Cousin concluded.
InfoQ interviewed Marcy Paramonova and Stéphane Cusin after their talk.
InfoQ: How did your engineering culture shift over time?
Stéphane Cusin: One principle we established from day one was that platform capabilities should never depend on manual intervention. Instead of opening a ticket and waiting for an engineer to make a change, teams interact with the platform through declarative configuration and automated workflows. For example, enabling a capability can be done through a simple configuration change in Git, which is automatically applied by our GitOps process. This creates a self-service experience while providing full traceability and visibility into platform adoption.
This approach changed how we operate the platform. We can now understand which capabilities are being adopted, which ones are no longer needed, and which users are affected by a change. It has already allowed us to safely retire unused features and migrate teams toward newer platform capabilities with confidence.
InfoQ: How did you design systems that create the culture that you wanted to establish?
Marcy Paramonova: You cannot mandate a culture into existence, but you can design structures that make certain behaviors natural. For us, that meant building rituals around collaboration rather than just talking about it.
We run a "Genius Bar" twice a week, two hours each session. If you have a question about the platform, if something is not working the way you expected, if you just want to understand how a component fits together, you come there. No ticket, no waiting for someone’s calendar to open up. It keeps feedback loops short, and it keeps us honest, because you hear very quickly when something is confusing or painful.
We also run user insights sessions where we share priorities, work done, and visibility gained, and we prioritize together with users rather than for them. And we do demos, showing what is shipped, what is on the roadmap, and how to actually use the platform day today.
Internally, the platform team has its own planning sessions to stay aligned and to make space for deliberate decisions, rather than just reactive work.
None of this is revolutionary. But when you stack these rhythms together, the culture you want starts to emerge from the structure you build. It is not magic, but it is also not accidental.
Cusin: We tried to make platform decisions visible. Platform capabilities are delivered through versioned artifacts, reusable deployment patterns, and documented interfaces rather than individual agreements between teams. This creates consistency and shared understanding across the organization.
Another important design principle was that every platform feature should have a lifecycle. We wanted to know who was using a capability, how it was being used, and whether it was still providing value. That visibility allows us to evolve the platform intentionally instead of accumulating complexity over time.
In many ways, our platform became a mechanism for reinforcing the behaviors we wanted to encourage: self-service over ticket-driven operations, standardization over customization, transparency over tribal knowledge, and shared ownership over dependency on a few experts.
When those principles are embedded into the platform itself, the desired culture becomes the easiest way for people to work.

articles.title: Bentley dévoile le Torcal, son premier SUV électrique de 888 ch dérivé du Porsche Cayenne
articles.text:
La foudre s’est abattue à Crewe, au Royaume-Uni. Dans un communiqué publié ce 23 septembre 2026, Bentley vient de lever le voile sur sa toute première voiture électrique, baptisée Torcal. Ce SUV n’a pas été développé à partir d’une feuille blanche. Pour mémoire, la marque britannique fait partie du groupe Volkswagen et peut donc profiter des technologies de ce dernier.
Ainsi, le nouveau Torcal reprend la plateforme PPE (Premium Platform Electric) utilisée par le Porsche Cayenne Electric. Voici tout ce qu’il faut savoir sur ce cousin anglais qui mise tout sur le luxe.
Un style caricatural pour le Bentley Torcal
Fait amusant, avec ses 5 mètres de long, le Torcal est la plus courte des Bentley à quatre portes ! Mais par sa carrure musclée, le SUV électrique en impose davantage que le reste de la gamme du constructeur anglais. Mercedes peut d’ailleurs aller se rhabiller, Bentley est le nouveau roi de la calandre illuminée. Admirez plutôt ces 76 diamants à LED, posés à la main. Le lien de parenté avec le Porsche Cayenne se devine de trois quarts arrière, mais le design reste bien celui d’une Bentley.
À bord aussi, Bentley soigne le raffinement. Les yeux avisés remarqueront en revanche un certain détail identique au cousin technique allemand : l’écran tactile incurvé au centre. Pour le reste, Bentley fait dans l’exclusivité et cela donne un habitacle qui semble moins chargé. Le coffre est annoncé à 460 litres, plus 90 litres sous le capot avant, contre 781 litres pour le Cayenne. Bentley semble avoir sacrifié du volume de chargement au profit de l’espace pour les passagers arrière.
Le Torcal se distingue aussi par le son. Pour imiter le rythme d’un vrai V8 Bentley, le son moteur artificiel, baptisé Dynamic Symphony, a été enregistré avec de vrais instruments (batterie, alto, guitare basse). Ça, c’est le luxe. Enfin, Bentley ajoute un tissu 100 % laine mérinos, un placage fait de noyer et quatre portes qui s’ouvrent et se ferment électriquement.
Moins puissant que le Cayenne Turbo Electric
Sans surprise, l’ensemble mécanique du Cayenne se retrouve dans le plancher du Torcal : deux moteurs électriques pour une transmission intégrale et une large batterie de 113 kWh nets en 800 V. Dans sa version de base, le SUV britannique développe 821 chevaux et 1 194 Nm, pour un 0 à 100 km/h en 3,4 secondes et 250 km/h en pointe.
Dans la version S, le SUV monte à 888 ch et 1 350 Nm avec le launch control, de quoi expédier le 0 à 100 km/h en 2,9 secondes et atteindre 260 km/h. Si le Torcal reste moins puissant que le Cayenne (1 156 ch en version Turbo), c’est parce que «la plupart des clients trouvent qu’une accélération plus brutale que celle-ci est une expérience désagréable », souligne Bentley. Quelle que soit la version, l’autonomie atteint jusqu’à 600 km WLTP.
Suspension indépendamment active, roues arrière directrices et recharge de 10 à 80 % en 16 minutes à 400 kW, le Torcal reprend encore bon nombre d’éléments au SUV allemand.
Quel prix pour le Bentley Torcal ?
Bentley n’a encore donné ni le prix français ni la date de livraison en France. Au Royaume-Uni, le Torcal débute à 173 300 livres sterling (environ 200 000 €) et le Torcal S à 199 300 livres (environ 230 000 €). C’est environ 33 000 € de plus que le Cayenne Turbo Electric (167 200 € en France), et près de 40 000 € de plus que son compatriote, le tout nouveau Range Rover Electric, vendu 161 500 €.
