articles.title: Malas noticias para 'Gremlins 3', que lanza su primer tráiler pero retrasa (y mucho) su fecha de estreno
articles.text:
Cuando hace unos meses se confirmó el desarrollo de Gremlins 3, los fans se llevaron una inesperada alegría. La saga de fantasía los ochenta regresaba con una nueva entrega que, además contaría con Chris Columbus, guionista de la original, como director. El cineasta de obras como Solo en casa, La Señora Doubtfire o las dos primeras cintas de Harry Potter se haría cargo de un proyecto que generaba mucha ilusión. Ahora, sin embargo, llegan noticias agridulces.
Warner Bros. ha lanzado el primer teaser tráiler de Gremlins 3. En él, el bueno de Gizmo se asoma tímidamente desde dentro de una mochila. El pequeño personaje regresará otra vez a las andadas para volver a generar el caos. Sin embargo, este adorable primer vistazo a su retorno ha venido acompañado de una noticia bastante menos agradable para los fans que con tanto ansia esperan el título.
Y es que la compañía ha confirmado que Gremlins 3 retrasa su fecha de estreno hasta el 6 de octubre de 2028. Anteriormente estaba prevista para noviembre de 2027, por lo que el retraso es bastante importante, de prácticamente un año entero. Un inesperado revés que obliga a armarse de paciencia para poder disfrutar de la próxima aventura de estas alocadas criaturas demoníacas.
Qué sabemos de Gremlins 3
Por el momento, la sinopsis y el reparto de Gremlins 3 se mantienen en secreto. El filme fue anunciado originalmente en 2025, cuando se desveló además que el mismísimo Steven Spielberg será productor ejecutivo del proyecto. La guionista se está encargando de escribir la película basándose en una idea original del propio Chris Columbus junto a Zach Lipovsky y Adam B. Stein (Destino Final: Lazos de sangre).
La primera entrega de Gremlins, estrenada en 1984 y dirigida por Joe Dante, fue un éxito rotundo de taquilla. El filme recaudó 212 millones de dólares en todo el mundo pese a contar con un presupuesto de apenas 11 millones. Seis años después, en 1990 llegó la secuela, Gremlins 2, la nueva generación. Esta logró recaudar tan solo 41 millones de dólares, cifras muy por debajo de su predecesora. En cualquier caso, también se la considera un clásico.

articles.title: Is Nigeria’s higher education sector ready for a true digital leap?
articles.text:
Nigeria is sitting on one of the greatest demographic dividends in the world. With over 60% of its population under 25, the demand for higher education is surging at an unprecedented rate. To meet this demand, universities across the country are expanding curricula, launching new tech hubs, and pushing for global accreditation.
But behind the ambitious academic goals lies a quiet operational crisis: the administrative bottleneck.
While Nigerian students are digital natives who manage their finances, socialise, and work on their smartphones, their university experiences remain legacy-heavy and disconnected. Long registration queues, misplaced transcripts, weeks-long waits for admission letters, and portal crashes during fee-payment windows are still the norm across many campuses.
The question is no longer whether Nigerian universities need a digital transformation. The question is: are they infrastructurally ready to transition from fragmented software to unified ecosystems?
The friction of “Frankenstein” IT systems
For years, the standard approach to university digitisation in emerging markets was piecemeal. A university might buy one software for finance, another for admissions, and rely on manual spreadsheets for everything else. This creates messy ‘Frankenstein’ systems where campus departments and data simply cannot talk to each other.
The operational toll is staggering.
Global education technology benchmarks reveal that university administrative teams lose an average of 17 hours each week simply reconciling conflicting data across disconnected legacy platforms.
Furthermore, many Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems historically sold to African universities were originally designed for corporate accounting rather than for students. They are heavy, expensive to maintain, and notoriously difficult to navigate on mobile devices — a critical flaw in a mobile-first economy like Nigeria.
A unified “Campus Operating System”
However, a major shift is underway.
Much as Africa leapfrogged landline telephones straight to mobile networks, Nigerian universities now have the opportunity to bypass clunky, legacy IT systems and jump straight to unified, cloud-native architectures centred on a single-database campus operating system.
To build a future-ready university, we cannot rely on corporate software retrofitted for education. I believe deeply in ‘in-residence’ software design—building technology specifically tailored to the unique, complex workflows of a campus. Instead of spending millions on customising outdated, rigid corporate ERPs, Nigerian universities can adopt a unified, AI-driven architecture from day one.
My goal has always been simple: to put the student experience at the absolute centre of the digital ecosystem.
Replacing friction with functional AI
Nowhere is the disconnect between institutional technology and the student reality more evident than in the recent arrival of Artificial Intelligence on campus.
To date, AI’s primary footprint in Nigerian higher education has been largely adversarial. Driven by urgent concerns about academic integrity, institutions rushed to deploy detection tools, such as Turnitin, to identify AI-generated text in essays, dissertations, and assignments.
For students, this reactive deployment has transformed AI into a source of friction and anxiety rather than empowerment. Scholars frequently find themselves navigating an environment of digital surveillance, where the fear of false positives and automated plagiarism flags looms over legitimate drafting and research. Worse still, it creates an ironic double standard: students face punitive scrutiny for exploring cutting-edge digital tools, while their institutions remain mired in manual, paper-intensive bureaucratic workflows.
The critical task for academic leaders is not to abandon academic integrity, but to expand their vision of what AI on campus should accomplish. Higher education must shift from using AI purely as an academic police force to deploying functional, operational AI that genuinely enriches the student experience.
This is where purpose-engineered higher education platforms are shifting the paradigm. Rather than treating AI solely as a punitive filter, platforms such as Academia by Serosoft embed functional AI natively across the academic lifecycle, demonstrating how intelligent automation can directly alleviate administrative drag:
- Intelligent Conversational Assistance: Instead of waiting in exhausting queues outside departmental offices or the bursary, students can engage 24/7 with conversational AI assistants—such as Academia’s SERA (AI Student Assistant)—via mobile portals and chat to instantly check course requirements, track fee clearances, verify degree audits, and access exam timetables.
- Predictive Academic Advising & Early Intervention: Academia’s AI capabilities continuously analyse engagement, attendance trends, and continuous assessment metrics to flag early signs of academic distress, enabling faculties and advisors to intervene proactively before a student falls behind.
- Automated Lifecycle Verification: Repetitive back-office tasks—from AI-driven secondary certificate and transcript validation during admissions to automated graduation clearance workflows—can be executed with speed and precision, reducing weeks of clerical friction to mere minutes. Data from Academia’s recent global implementations show that automating the admissions process can reduce processing times by more than 30%.
When AI is channelled toward removing administrative barriers rather than merely monitoring coursework submissions, it transforms campus technology from an instrument of suspicion into a catalyst for institutional trust and student success.
A new era of higher education infrastructure
Proof that Nigeria is ready for this leap is already visible.
Recently, James Hope University, an exclusive, visionary postgraduate business institution in Lekki, Lagos, founded by legendary banker and philanthropist Jim Ovia (CFR), opted to bypass traditional, fragmented IT entirely. The university deployed a modern, unified, and AI-driven campus operating system to ensure its internal operations match the elite, forward-thinking nature of its curriculum.
This is the blueprint for the future of Nigerian higher education. Top-tier institutions are realising that to cultivate world-class talent, they must run on world-class, frictionless infrastructure.
The verdict
Is Nigeria’s higher education sector ready for a digital leap? Absolutely.
The demand from the student population is undeniable, and the technology required to build borderless, intelligent campuses is already available and proven on the continent.
The universities that will dominate the next decade of African education will not be the ones with the oldest buildings. They will be the ones that tear down their data silos, abandon legacy tech, and partner with modern, student-centric innovators to put the student experience at the absolute centre of their digital ecosystem.
Arpit Badjatya is the Founder and CEO of Academia by Serosoft, a global education technology pioneer and thought leader. He is a frequent keynote speaker on international education stages, including the World Education Summit, the Swiss Higher-Ed Executive Roundtable in Zurich, and the African TVET Conference in Johannesburg. His work focuses on reshaping campus operations through unified data systems and functional artificial intelligence.

articles.title: Raspberry Pi's RAM lock was built to stop scalpers, but it's blocking repairs too
articles.text:
Winners & losers: Raspberry Pi has confirmed that its firmware prevents users from changing a board's factory RAM configuration, a restriction that blocks not only unofficial memory upgrades but also some attempts to replace failed RAM chips with equivalent parts. The company says the measure is meant to stop resellers from passing off untested, modified boards as factory configurations, but it also limits a capability long used by Raspberry Pi repair and maker communities.
The issue came up on the Raspberry Pi forums after a user replaced the RAM on a Compute Module 5 but couldn't get the board to recognize the new 4 GB chip. PhilE, a Raspberry Pi engineer and forum moderator, said the company has been "locking devices to their original RAM size" for some time.
The firmware does more than check capacity. It also stores other attributes linked to the original memory device, according to PhilE. That could prevent even a same-capacity replacement chip from working. For users trying to fix a failed RAM IC, the limit could make a board impossible to repair even when a compatible replacement part is available.
Raspberry Pi said the policy is meant to stop untested modified boards from entering the resale market. The company said some resellers could buy lower-memory products, install larger chips "of dubious origin," and sell them as factory 8 GB models.
"If labor is cheap enough then there may be a minor financial gain in buying a part with say a 2GB part, swapping it for an 8GB part of dubious origin, and reselling it as an 8GB device," PhilE wrote.
Those modified boards may have stability problems because Raspberry Pi did not test them in their altered configuration. Buyers could still contact Raspberry Pi for support, however, leaving the company responsible for problems caused by third-party modifications. Raspberry Pi's answer is to eliminate the upgrade option in the first place.
PhilE was direct about the result for users attempting a RAM swap: "don't waste your time trying - it won't work."
The restriction also applies to users who are not trying to create unofficial higher-spec models. Raspberry Pi boards have long been used in home labs, embedded products, edge deployments and custom hardware. A developer may find that an existing board no longer has enough memory for a new workload, while a repair technician may want to replace a failed chip without changing the device's specification. Under the firmware policy, neither use case is guaranteed to work.
The lock reportedly began rolling out in firmware updates in late 2024. It was therefore in place before the recent increase in RAM prices tied to demand from AI data centers. Raspberry Pi's explanation points instead to product validation, resale practices and support costs.
Raspberry Pi 4 and Raspberry Pi 5 users have demonstrated memory upgrades by removing and replacing BGA-mounted RAM packages. Such work requires specialized soldering equipment and carries obvious risks, but it showed that the hardware could support higher-capacity configurations.
Because of the current firmware, a user might still be able to complete the physical work, but the board could reject the altered memory configuration. Users may need to revert to an older firmware version to bypass the restriction, if one is available for that model.
The policy may frustrate Raspberry Pi's repair and maker communities, which have long treated the company's hardware as unusually open for low-cost computing platforms. Some supporters have suggested a warranty flag or one-time setting that would identify a modified board and remove Raspberry Pi support without blocking the modification itself.
Raspberry Pi has instead chosen to enforce the original RAM configuration in firmware. For most users, the change will have little effect. For repair shops, developers and hardware modders, it removes one more option.

articles.title: 5 GHz im Smartphone: Qualcomms neuer Chip schafft PC-Leistung
articles.text:
5 GHz im Smartphone: Qualcomms neuer Chip schafft, was bisher nur PCs konnten
Android-Handys könnten bald schneller werden: Der Chipspezialist Qualcomm hat zwei neue High-End-Chips für Smartphones vorgestellt: Den Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 und die stärkere Variante Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6. Der Gen 6 löst den bisherigen Gen-5-Prozessor ab und ist laut Qualcomm der erste Smartphone-Chip, der 5 GHz Taktrate erreicht – zumindest mit seinen beiden Prime-Kernen. Solche Werte kannte man früher nur von PCs.
Was der Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 drauf hat
Neben den beiden Prime-Kernen stecken sechs Performance-Kerne in der Oryon-CPU des Elite Gen 6, die bis zu 4 GHz schaffen. Gegenüber dem Vorjahreschip verspricht Qualcomm zehn Prozent mehr Rechenleistung oder 37 Prozent höhere Energieeffizienz bei gleicher Leistung. Die Adreno-Grafikeinheit soll um 35 Prozent zulegen. Möglich macht das vor allem ein neues Fertigungsverfahren. Qualcomm spricht grob von 2 Nanometern. Vermutlich wechselt das Unternehmen vom N3P-Prozess auf N2P beim Produzenten TSMC aus Taiwan.
Zu Verbesserungen an den CPU-Kernen selbst sagt Qualcomm bislang nichts. Der Grund dürfte schlicht sein, dass es abseits des höheren Takts kaum welche gibt. Der Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 schafft bis zu 4,6 GHz, der Nachfolger liegt knapp neun Prozent darüber. Den restlichen Prozentpunkt dürften übliche Feinarbeiten an der Sprungvorhersage bringen. Dabei rät der Prozessor vorab, welche Befehle er als Nächstes abarbeiten muss.
Allerdings hat Qualcomm die wichtige KI-Hardware des Chips überarbeitet. Ein neuer „Element Accelerator“ soll den Hexagon-NPU stärker machen – jene Einheit, die KI-Berechnungen übernimmt. Der Sensing Hub, der im Hintergrund sparsam Sensordaten auswertet und etwa Sprachbefehle erkennt, bekommt zwei eigene KI-Einheiten. Dazu kommen zwei Bildsignalprozessoren (ISP), mit denen sich zwei Kameras ansteuern lassen, um durchgehend Daten aufzunehmen.
Die Extreme-Variante setzt bei der Grafik an
Der Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 bringt alle Eigenschaften des Schwesterchips mit, dazu einige Extras. Die CPU-Kerne sollen durch ein optimiertes Package etwas mehr leisten – denkbar ist eine verbesserte Signalführung auf dem Träger. Wie groß der Unterschied ausfällt, beziffert Qualcomm nicht.
Deutlich aufgewertet hat das Unternehmen die Adreno-GPU. Der Grafikchip bekommt drei Matrix-Cores, die auf KI-Berechnungen ausgelegt sind. Damit erhöht sie in Spielen die Auflösung und erzeugt zusätzliche Zwischenbilder. Qualcomm nennt das „Neural Fusion“ und zieht damit mit ARM gleich: Dessen Mali-GPU G2-Ultra NX bietet dieselben Funktionen.
Die ersten Geräte mit den neuen Chips stehen kurz bevor. In den vergangenen Jahren kamen sie meist von chinesischen Marken wie Honor und Xiaomi. Xiaomi zeigt das 18 Pro und das 18 Pro Max noch in dieser Woche für den chinesischen Markt, später sollen die Modelle auch global erscheinen. Auch Motorola ist früh dran und kündigt mit dem Signature 27 ein erstes Smartphone mit dem Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 an.

articles.title: Lookout launches mobile module to detect AI-powered text and voice scams - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Lookout launches mobile module to detect AI-powered text and voice scams
Mobile security company Lookout Inc. today launched Social Engineering Protection, a module that analyzes text messages and phone calls for signs an employee is being manipulated into handing over credentials or money.
The release goes after a problem Lookout argues email security tools and awareness training were never built to solve. Business conversations have moved onto SMS, voice calls and messaging apps, where corporate inspection tools mostly have no reach. Generative artificial intelligence made the lures running over those channels cheap to personalize.
Smishing protection is the first of three components. The software reads incoming text and multimedia messages on iOS and Android, including those sent over Rich Communication Services, and flags malicious links in them. Lookout said the same analysis weighs the intent behind a message, which catches approaches that carry no link at all.
Voice coverage works on live calls and voicemail. Transcription surfaces the scam patterns in what a caller actually says. A separate check examines the voice itself for signs it was cloned or machine-generated.
The third component works on the number rather than the content. Mobile identity signals and phone number attributes feed a risk assessment that separates a legitimate caller from one behaving suspiciously. Administrators can block known or suspicious numbers across an entire workforce from a single console.
“Frontier AI has fundamentally changed the economics of cyber offense, making highly sophisticated social engineering accessible to mainstream attackers,” said Praveen Mamnani, chief product officer at Lookout. He added that those defenses were built before attackers could run the same approach across text, voice and messaging at once.
The launch gives Lookout a third pillar for what it calls its Mobile AI Security Platform. In April the company shipped AI Visibility and Governance, a product that tracks what employees do with generative and agentic AI apps on their phones. The Mobile Software Exposure Center followed in July. That tool takes compiled mobile apps apart to find vulnerable libraries and outdated software development kits buried inside them.
Lookout released Smishing AI in September last year, bringing large language models to bear on the content and intent of incoming text messages. Executive impersonation protection had landed on the platform a year before that.
Social Engineering Protection is sold as a native add-on to the Mobile AI Security Platform. Existing customers can switch it on from the admin console they already run, with no additional agent or infrastructure to deploy.

articles.title: China's YMTC wins patent battle against Micron in ongoing 3-year legal war over memory patents — new injunctions could restrict Micron's supply into Germany
articles.text:
China's YMTC wins patent battle against Micron in ongoing 3-year legal war over memory patents — new injunctions could restrict Micron's supply into Germany
Micron continues to deny any wrongdoing and has appealed the ruling.
A court in Germany has granted court injunctions against Micron, marking a win for YMTC on the European/German front in the 3-year legal war between the two companies over memory technology patents.
According to a Digitimes report, the court ruled on Sept. 18 that Micron did infringe YMTC’s 3D NAND technology patents in two instances. The injunctions could restrict Micron’s supply in Germany and impact the broader European NAND market. Micron said it disagreed with the court ruling and has already filed an appeal. It is also challenging the validity of the related patents in separate legal cases across various countries.
YMTC filed the lawsuit that won the recent injunctions in late 2025 at the Munich 1 Regional Court, opening five cases involving four German utility models and a European patent. The court granted injunctions on two of the utility models with 10-year protection periods — DE202020006166U1 (case No. 7O12615/25) and DE202021004551U1 (case No. 12614/25) — and adjourned the others. The injunctions are only first-instance rulings and can be suspended if Micron successfully appeals at the Munich Higher Regional Court.
The ruling is the latest development in a years-long dispute between the two memory makers that started in 2023 when YMTC sued Micron in California, alleging violations of eight 3D NAND architecture patents. The dispute has since snowballed into a multi-front war involving over 20 patents, with suits and countersuits on both sides. The cases cover patent infringement, declaratory judgment, spyware, libel, false advertising, and invalidation actions, and have been filed in courts across China, the U.S., the U.K., Germany, and in other parts of Europe.
Micron has vehemently denied any wrongdoing and has filed multiple patent invalidation challenges since 2024, the first of which came after YMTC dragged the company to court in China over related issues. Seven of the disputed patents have already been declared invalid, and Micron has said it will continue pushing to safeguard its intellectual property.
3D NAND is a flash-memory storage technology that stores data in products ranging from smartphones and SSDs to enterprise storage systems. Unlike older planar NAND, where memory cells are arranged side by side on a flat surface, 3D NAND stacks cells vertically in multiple layers, allowing manufacturers to pack more storage into a given area while increasing density and lowering cost per bit. Modern NAND chips can contain hundreds of these layers, making the architecture and manufacturing techniques behind them commercially valuable intellectual property.
The Micron-YMTC fight is playing out against the backdrop of the much larger technology dispute between the U.S. and China. Washington has tightened restrictions on China's access to advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment and other chip technologies, while Beijing has placed export restrictions on many critical raw materials.

articles.title: Mine My Phone : Back Market détourne les codes d’Apple pour dévoiler le coût humain et écologique des smartphones
articles.text:
Mine My Phone : Back Market détourne les codes d’Apple pour dévoiler le coût humain et écologique des smartphones
On le sait, la fabrication d’un smartphone de 200 g requiert l’extraction d’environ 200 kg de matières premières. Mais derrière ce chiffre un peu simpliste se cachent des réalités écologiques et humaines assez méconnues, sur lesquelles Back Market veut lever le voile grâce à son nouveau site Mine My Phone.
C’est une opération de sensibilisation déguisée en pied de nez fait à Apple. Le spécialiste du reconditionné Back Market vient de dévoiler une nouvelle plateforme destinée à montrer les dégâts de la frénésie minière liée au commerce de smartphones.
Astucieusement nommé Mine My Phone, le site reprend les codes esthétiques d’Apple en mettant sur la carte non pas l’emplacement de votre iPhone perdu, mais la provenance des différents métaux qui le composent et l’impact de leur extraction sur le climat, les vies humaines et l’équilibre géopolitique de la planète.
Le but de la plateforme est “d’accompagner les gens pour qu’ils puissent prendre des décisions éclairées sur la consommation de tech”, détaille Marie Castelli, responsable des affaires publiques chez Back Market. Sans culpabiliser le consommateur, le spécialiste du reconditionné veut participer à “changer la discussion autour de la tech” en rendant ludiques et accessibles des sujets souvent présentés comme complexes et lointains.
Mine My Phone : rendre compte de la réalité environnementale
La carte et les nombreux “points d’intérêt” qui la jonchent se décomposent en trois catégories : “impact environnemental”, “impact humain” et “impact géopolitique”. Il est possible de cliquer sur chacun des points pour obtenir plus d’informations sur le minerai en question, ses effets sur la planète et nos vies, son lieu d'extraction et ce qu’il est possible d’en faire en fin de vie. Plusieurs articles rédigés par des experts accompagnent l’exploration pour offrir un point de vue aussi complet que possible.
Selon un sondage effectué par Back Market, près de quatre personnes sur 10 “sont choquées par le nombre de fournisseurs impliqués dans la fabrication d’un smartphone” et 43 % ignorent que l’extraction du cobalt est associée au travail des enfants en République démocratique du Congo (RDC). Mine My Phone ambitionne donc d’être un outil pédagogique au service de l’allongement de la durée de vie de nos téléphones, mais aussi une plateforme de mobilisation, puisque des outils d’appels à l’action y sont présents.
*“Derrière chaque smartphone, il y a une réalité d’extraction intensive et massive des ressources minières, explique David Maenda Kithoko, spécialiste de l’extraction minière en RDC et fondateur de l’ONG Génération Lumière. Il faut rendre compte de ces réalités pour que les gens puissent être informés de ce type de problématiques en vue d’un changement culturel.”
Le site tente donc de rappeler certains chiffres : 1,4 milliard de personnes à la santé abîmée par l’extraction minière, 407 000 personnes maintenues en situation d’esclavage moderne en RDC, des milliers d’hectares de forêt rasés au Ghana. David Maenda Kithoko rappelle aussi que les bandes armées ont régulièrement recours aux agressions sexuelles et viols pour soumettre les femmes des pays vassalisés. “Je peux affirmer que, pour faire un smartphone comme celui qui est posé sur cette table, il faut comptabiliser deux viols de femmes congolaises”, rappelait-il dans le magazine Climax fin 2024.
Plaidoyer ou marketing ? La stratégie de Back Market
Pas franchement très réjouissante, cette réalité doit être affrontée pour infléchir notre rythme de consommation, estime Back Market. Le risque pour la plateforme n’est-il pas de faire la promotion du téléphone reconditionné sur le dos de populations et de territoires maltraités pour autant ? “Pour nous, notre rôle va au-delà de la vente de téléphones, c’est plus gros que nous”, avance Marine Libaud, responsable de la communication chez Back Market. “On aura réussi notre pari si l’on multiplie le nombre d’entreprises qui nous font concurrence”, complète Marie Castelli.
L’objectif de Mine My Phone est donc davantage d’effectuer un travail de plaidoyer que de marketing, nous explique Back Market. “On s’est aussi posé cette question, assure David Maenda Kithoko au nom de Génération Lumière. Notre travail n’est pas d’inciter à consommer, au contraire. Mais quand ce discours est porté par des gens qui ont une activité économique, je trouve ça très bien. Je n’aurais pas été chez Apple pour faire la même chose”, s’amuse le militant.
Pour autant, l’opération n’est pas complètement désintéressée. Au-delà de sa mission didactique, Mine My Phone veut changer à la fois les habitudes des consommateurs, mais aussi des législateurs. Le but ? Permettre de construire un monde où il est possible (et facile) de faire durer un téléphone 10 ans. “On ne dit pas que chacun doit le garder 10 ans, mais qu’il reste opérationnel tout ce temps”, explique Marine Libaud. Pourquoi pas grâce au miracle du reconditionné ?

articles.title: Technics tease un nouveau casque à fluide magnétique pour le 29 septembre 2026 — Frandroid
articles.text:
La marque japonaise Technics, qui appartient à Panasonic, a publié sur son compte Instagram officiel une très courte vidéo assez évocatrice. Sur fond noir, on peut voir dans un premier temps des éclaboussures rappelant une matière liquide, puis un casque circum-aural argenté apparaît en gros plan, avec le logo doré de la marque gravé sur l’oreillette droite.
Enfin, toujours avec des éclaboussures en fond, une date s’affiche : 2026.9.29, accompagnée de la formule « Stay Tuned ».
Une technologie jusqu’ici réservée aux écouteurs
Aucune caractéristique technique n’est dévoilée, mais l’esthétique du visuel, avec son jeu de matière fluide, rappelle clairement le procédé baptisé « Magnetic Fluid Driver », développé par la marque. Cette technologie s’appuie sur un liquide huileux chargé de particules magnétiques, injecté entre l’aimant du transducteur et la bobine mobile. Selon Technics, ce fluide maintient la bobine centrée, ce qui réduit la distorsion et améliore la restitution des basses fréquences.
Ce procédé avait d’abord équipé les écouteurs intra-auriculaires filaires EAH-TZ700, avant d’être miniaturisé pour les écouteurs sans fil EAH-AZ100, lancés en janvier 2025. Le format circum-aural visible sur le teaser laisse penser à un successeur du casque EAH-A800. Si cette piste se confirme, l’intégration du fluide magnétique sur un casque circum-aural serait une première pour la marque, réservée jusque-là aux écouteurs.
    Pour aller plus loin
            Test des Technics EAH-AZ100 : des ambitions premium, des compromis sonores
            
Sur ce segment, la concurrence reste dense, avec Sony, Bose ou Sennheiser déjà positionnés sur le casque premium à réduction de bruit. Technics n’a encore communiqué ni le prix ni la date de sortie de ce casque, deux informations attendues lors de la présentation du 29 septembre.

articles.title: Amsterdam-based Duqu raises €1.5 million to unlock cash tied up in unpaid invoices | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Duqu, an Amsterdam-based FinTech startup that gives businesses immediate access to money tied up in outstanding invoices, has raised €1.5 million in a pre-Seed round from Curiosity VC and No Such Ventures.
The company has also developed its own AI underwriting engine, automating 95% of the credit assessment process. It also offers the technology as a white-label solution to banks, lenders and leasing companies. The Dutch startup plans to use this capital to grow both parts of the business.
“Businesses can arrange almost everything instantly today, yet after completing the work they can still wait weeks to get paid. That no longer matches the pace at which businesses operate. Growth cannot wait for an invoice to be paid,” said Duqu co-founder Maas de Goede.
Founded in October 2025 by de Goede, Victor Brouwer, and Diederik Nassenstein, Duqu states that, through its platform, businesses can apply for a short-term advance without selling their invoices and without a minimum or maximum amount.
The company highlighted that nearly half (47%) of B2B invoices in Western Europe are overdue. It notes that this means money businesses have already earned can stay tied up for weeks, while expenses such as employee salaries, inventory investment, marketing, or a new hire cannot wait.
Duqu claims to solve this with a short-term advance, giving businesses access to funds tied up in an outstanding invoice as soon as the invoice is issued. It assesses outstanding B2B invoices and, based on that assessment, advances the invoice amount to the business.
The company notes that unlike factoring, businesses do not sell their invoices and retain control of the customer relationship. There is no minimum or maximum amount, and businesses pay a fee only when they use an advance. Once approved, the money is transferred within 24 hours, and often within an hour.
According to investor Curiosity, Duqu’s technology enables profitable processing of smaller credit applications. “Small applications are relatively expensive for traditional lenders to assess and process. Duqu has built a fully AI-driven credit assessment and processing stack. As a result, businesses with smaller credit or working capital needs can be better served,” said Herman Kienhuis of Curiosity.
Duqu has been building its proprietary AI underwriting engine for the past year and a half, currently automating around 95% of the credit assessment process. The technology is modular and can also be deployed outside Duqu’s own platform. Lenders can use the engine as a white-label solution to automatically assess applications in line with their own credit policies. 
Thijn van Helvoirt of No Such Ventures said, “Credit assessment is still a labour-intensive process for many providers. As a result, processing more applications often means hiring more people. Duqu automates a large part of that process while allowing lenders to retain their own credit policies. The same technology can also be applied to areas such as leasing, mortgages and buy now, pay later. This means that alongside its solution for businesses, Duqu is building technology that can be applied across a much broader part of the credit market.”
The platform currently has almost 1,500 users and has processed €4.6 million in applications since launch, of which more than €1.2 million has been advanced.

articles.title: Srijan Realty aims to redefine residential living in Kolkata with the launch of Orizon
articles.text:
Srijan Realty aims to redefine residential living in Kolkata with the launch of Orizon
Spread across 8.3 acres on the Southern EM Bypass, the six‑tower, 702‑unit community blends 80% open space, barrier‑free design, and IGBC Platinum pre‑certified sustainability.
Srijan Realty, one of Eastern India’s most established residential developers, has announced the launch of Orizon, a 702-unit residential community spread across 8.3 acres off the Southern EM Bypass in Jagaddal, South Kolkata.
The launch arrives as the corridor completes a decade-long transformation from a peripheral suburb into one of the city’s most aspirational residential addresses, supported by expanding metro and suburban rail connectivity, dual EM Bypass access, and a maturing ecosystem of schools, hospitals and retail destinations.
Located on BC Roy Road in Jagaddal, with two access points off the Southern EM Bypass roughly 400 metres and 750 metres apart, Orizon comprises six high-rise towers ranging from 17 to 23 storeys, housing 702 three-bedroom residences sized between approximately 1,208 and 1,650 square feet.
Roughly 80% of the 8.3-acre site, 85% including podium-level landscaping, has been kept open, an unusually low-density ratio for a development of this scale so close to the city.
Shahid Khudiram Metro Station is roughly 14 minutes away, with Sonarpur railway station around 15 minutes; Spencer’s, Wood Square Mall and Southwinds Galleria are all within a six-minute drive.
A life beyond the ordinary
Orizon’s design philosophy takes its name from the word “horizon”, built around the idea that space, light, and an unobstructed view are increasingly scarce commodities in a city that has grown denser over the past two decades.
Residences feature terrace-style and standing balconies intended to maximize natural light and cross-ventilation, while the project’s golden façade, visible from the EM Bypass, is conceived as a visual landmark along the corridor.
Despite its dual EM Bypass access and proximity to South Kolkata’s commercial nodes, the development has been planned to function as a self-contained green enclave, insulated from the congestion typically associated with high-density urban corridors.
Schools, including BDM International and Narayana, along with healthcare providers such as Apollo Hospital’s upcoming campus, Peerless Hospital and RN Tagore Hospital, are within a 20-minute radius.
Lifestyle infrastructure
At the centre of the development sits a roughly 33,000-square-foot clubhouse featuring an infinity-edge swimming pool, jacuzzi and dedicated kids’ pool, alongside a 21,000-square-foot podium-level garden anchoring a sports arena with facilities for tennis, basketball, pickleball and badminton.
Indoor offerings extend to a gymnasium, yoga and meditation studio, squash court, co-working space, home theatre, library, and a dedicated senior citizens’ lounge. The developer says these amenities are designed to serve every age group within a single community rather than cater narrowly to one demographic.
Inclusive, barrier-free design
A defining feature of Orizon is its barrier-free design, incorporating wheelchair access ramps, lift cabins wide enough to accommodate wheelchairs, Braille and voice-enabled lift controls, accessible toilets and designated accessible parking throughout common areas.
Srijan Realty positions this not as a regulatory minimum but as a forward-looking response to India’s multigenerational households, where ageing parents, differently abled family members, and young children increasingly share a single home and require equal, independent access to shared spaces.
Sustainability and future readiness
Orizon has been pre-certified for IGBC Platinum design, India’s highest green building rating, with features including rainwater harvesting, solar power for common areas, low-flow water fixtures, energy-efficient LED lighting, organic waste management, and EV charging infrastructure.
Buildings certified to this standard typically deliver 20-30% energy savings and 30-50% water savings compared with conventional construction.
Srijan Realty has been among Eastern India’s most respected real estate developers for over two decades, with a portfolio of residential communities, integrated townships, retail destinations and commercial developments across Kolkata and beyond.
Leadership Perspective
Dinesh Agarwal, Director, Srijan Realty, said Orizon reflects how they believe Kolkata wants to live today. “Homebuyers are no longer choosing between space and connectivity, or between design and responsibility - they expect all of it together. Southern EM Bypass has moved past being an emerging corridor - it is now one of South Kolkata's defining growth engines, and we have been part of that story for over a decade,” he said.
Agarwal added that Srijan Realty has built Orizon as a “community first, planned around low-density living, open space, and lifestyle infrastructure that we believe will hold its value well beyond the next market cycle, with inclusivity and sustainability designed into its foundations rather than added on at the end”.
Guided by the philosophy that “great homes are built on trust,” the company continues to focus on design quality, customer-centric innovation, and long-term community building.

articles.title: Placeholder domain used in dev docs now serves ClickFix attacks
articles.text:
The "third-party.com" domain, commonly used as a placeholder in developer documentation and code examples, is serving a fake Cloudflare verification page that attempts to trick Windows users into executing PowerShell commands.
The domain third-party.com has long been used in documentation to represent an arbitrary external website, API, or service, similar to how developers use domains such as example.com.
However, unlike example.com, example.net, and example.org, which IANA reserves specifically for documentation, third-party.com is a normally registered domain whose content its owner can control.
This difference is now a security concern after the domain began serving a ClickFix attack that impersonates a Cloudflare security check.
Manifold Security first reported the malicious use of the domain after discovering it while examining public AI skills and MCP server documentation that referenced the domain.
BleepingComputer has since confirmed that the page displays a fake Cloudflare "Performing security verification" CAPTCHA screen containing a "Verify you are human" prompt.
After the user clicks the verification box, the site copies a malicious PowerShell command into the Windows Clipboard, and then instructs the user to press the Windows key + R, paste the contents of their clipboard using Ctrl+V, and press Enter.
When the PowerShell command runs, it reconstructs the payload URL elxxvvx[.]xyz/f, downloads a PowerShell script from that address, and then executes it.
This technique is commonly known as ClickFix, where attackers use fake errors, CAPTCHA prompts, or verification pages to convince victims to manually execute commands copied to their clipboard.
ClickFix attacks have become a popular way to distribute malware, as the malware is installed via commands executed by the user rather than downloaded from websites or as email attachments. In some cases, this could allow malware to install while bypassing traditional antivirus software.
At the time of BleepingComputer's testing, elxxvvx[.]xyz no longer resolved, leaving the current attack chain broken.
However, a Hybrid Analysis report from May 2, 2026, shows the site distributed a PowerShell script configured to download a 134MB zip archive from:
https://elxxvvx[.]xyz/update2.zip
The PowerShell script saved the archive as update26.zip, extracted it, and then attempted to launch an executable named draw.io.exe.
Because the update2.zip archive is no longer available, BleepingComputer couldn't determine what the payload does.
Manifold's Ax Sharma says the attack specifically targets Windows users, and Linux and Mac visitors will see errors stating their operating system is unsupported.
"A macOS or Linux user-agent gets none of that. It gets a near-identical page that stops at an error: "macOS is not supported. This website requires a Windows PC to access." No clipboard poisoning, no payload," explains Sharma.
"The attacker only shows the weapon to the targets it works against, which is precisely why a casual look, or a scanner on a Linux datacenter IP, sees nothing wrong."
A placeholder that wasn't reserved
The more interesting aspect of the attack is the third-party.com domain chosen to host the ClickFix page.
Public developer documentation has treated third-party.com as a generic example hostname for many years.
For example, the W3C Geolocation specification currently demonstrates granting geolocation permissions to an external iframe using third-party.com as a placeholder domain:
The W3C Compute Pressure specification similarly uses the domain when demonstrating how a website can enable the API for remote content:
<iframe src="https://third-party.com" allow="compute-pressure"/>
Chromium's documentation for its Telemetry Extension API also uses third-party.com as an example website permitted to communicate with a Chrome extension:
Other examples go further and use the domain in code that would actually make network requests if copied literally.
A PrivacyCG proposal on GitHub also uses the domain as the destination of a JavaScript fetch() request from a service worker.
Posts online indicate that developers have copied these and similar examples into their own code and projects.
In a 2015 Stack Overflow question, a developer said they had applied an asynchronous loading example containing https://third-party.com/resource.js to their website before discovering that it did not behave as expected after publishing the site.
These examples do not mean that the associated projects or documentation are compromised.
However, applications or test code that copied such placeholder URLs could now cause a browser or automated tool to contact the real third-party.com domain and potentially display the ClickFix attack in a browser or application.
Unlike example.com, which IANA maintains for documentation and does not allow to be registered or transferred, the third-party.com domain has no such protection, and was clearly hijacked or registered at some point to conduct these ClickFix attacks.
"third-party[.]com has been a generic documentation placeholder for years, the same role example.com plays," explains Manifold.
"A public code search turns it up in skills, MCP-server docs, and over 1,500 files across 1,700+ repositories from names as trusted as Chromium, Sanity, and Vercel. Since at least June 2026 it's been serving the ClickFix lure."
While the widespread use of third-party.com as a placeholder in documentation makes the domain attractive to attackers, there is no evidence that it was registered for malicious purposes.
The domain was first registered in 1996, long before the current campaign, and BleepingComputer has not determined when or how control of the site changed.
At this time, there have been no reports that these references to third-party.com have actually resulted in ClickFix attacks being executed on developer's devices or within their applications/webpages.
However, as the domain remains live, it could easily be switched to a new, live payload domain and actively utilized in future attacks.

articles.title: Apple Reference Image Signs Photos at the Sensor, Moving Provenance Trust Away from C2PA
articles.text:
Apple has published the design of Apple Reference Image, an opt-in camera mode on the main sensor of the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max that produces a timestamped photograph verifiable as a real sensor capture. The design moves trust in image provenance away from the editing chain certified by the C2PA standard and toward the sensor, Apple's Private Cloud Compute infrastructure, and Apple's own signing service.
Apple's argument is that C2PA attaches provenance after capture, leaving the chain open to compromise before signing, and can tie an image to a public identity. In Reference mode, the sensor secure-boots into a dedicated state and signs pixel data immediately after capture, while the Secure Enclave signs metadata that originates elsewhere, such as zoom and focal length. Capture time is bounded by two signed RFC 3161 timestamps, one collected over the push notification heartbeat before capture and one requested after, with requests routed through Oblivious HTTP. The result is stored as a secure digital negative in DNG format.
Development happens in Private Cloud Compute. PCC verifies the signature chains back to factory certificate authorities, confirms the sensor and Secure Enclave belong to the same device, then performs demosaicing, tone mapping, and JPEG compression. PCC builds are recorded in a transparency log with binaries available for inspection. The final image carries a composite ML-DSA-87 and RSA-3072 signature, which Apple describes as the only quantum-secure image provenance scheme.
Revocation covers individual photos and whole sensors. Before signing, PCC computes a confidence score for whether the image has the physical characteristics of raw sensor output, using what Apple describes as a neural network with hidden weights, and a companion service keeps a running score per sensor. The development code is published for inspection, while the model informing revocation is not.
The final image carries no photographer or device credential. It is signed by Apple's signing service, so that observers cannot tell whether two images came from the same device. Third-party apps can view reference images through APIs in iOS, iPadOS and macOS 27, but Apple has not described a verifier for other platforms or the web.
Community reactions on Hacker News and Reddit have been sharply divided, and less about the cryptography than about what it proves.
The most direct challenge concerned what the sensor is pointed at. Commenter tristanj described the replay route:
Photoshop / AI-gen an image -> display on a high-resolution monitor -> photograph the monitor with iPhone 18 Pro -> valid Apple Reference image.
Commenter HALtheWise countered that a 48-megapixel sensor makes that harder than it sounds, since a monitor without several times as many pixels would likely leave detectable moire patterns, and suggested this is presumably what the hidden-weights confidence score is for.
A second thread questioned the anonymity guarantee. Commenter microtonal pointed out that PCC briefly holds both the device's original certificate chain and Apple's replacement signature:
So in the end it all depends on how much you trust Apple's cloud and PCC nodes.
Commenter lxgr asked why Apple did not use Direct Anonymous Attestation, which provides similar privacy properties without a centralized server. On Reddit, commenter IntelArtiGen made the same point about revocation more briefly:
It's not a zero-trust method, but I guess most people would trust Apple.
The third thread concerned use cases. Commenter tgsovlerkhgsel called journalism the PR story, arguing the real demand lies in insurance claims and identity verification, and noting that people will verify images by looking at a reposted screenshot of the verification UI rather than checking the original. A related concern surfaced on Reddit, where commenter b_a_t_m_4_n noted that almost all websites transcode uploaded images to save storage. Commenter turtleship_2006 replied that in cases where it matters, such as a court case or an important news article, the original would be used or linked.
On Hacker News, commenter dwaite disagreed that identity verification was a good fit:
This tech would just indicate that they got authentic pixels capturing a potentially fake license.
He added that identity verification is moving to digital credentials such as mobile driving licenses and eIDAS 2, and that the system does not support video, protect against man-in-the-middle attacks, or allow time-of-flight measurement, concluding that it shuffles the risks around.
On competition, commenter jeroenhd argued that C2PA phones already offer comparable capture signing, and that the timestamping and verified-compute components are the hard part. That holds for Google's Pixel 10, which signs photos at capture, while Samsung's Galaxy S25 attaches C2PA credentials only to images edited with its generative AI tools. Commenter Topfi replied that those implementations still depend on the operating system being trusted, which is the gap Apple's sensor-level signing addresses.
If these reactions are representative, the debate is less about whether the signatures hold than about where trust ends up. Signing at the sensor addresses the gap C2PA leaves before capture, while the anonymity guarantee rests on Apple's cloud, and the detection of photographed screens or prints rests on the confidence model. C2PA remains the open, multi-vendor standard, backed by Adobe, Microsoft and the BBC among others, with support in cameras from Leica and in Google's Pixel phones. Apple also plans to support Google's SynthID standard for identifying AI-generated or edited images, in a software update later this year.
The feature is opt-in and must be selected at capture, so it cannot be applied to existing photographs. Negatives can be shared undeveloped, and after development the negative moves to the deleted photos folder, where it is purged after 30 days unless recovered. Capture is not available at launch in the EU, although devices running iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27 can develop and view reference images, and the feature is not available in China at launch because of regulatory requirements.

articles.text:
Despertarse por las mañanas con el pitido del móvil suele ser una de las formas más bruscas e incómodas de empezar la jornada. Para cambiar esta rutina y apostar por un descanso más progresivo, Action tiene rebajada, esta semana, esta luz despertador con alarma de Grundig, que ahora puedes comprar por 7,95 euros.
Si no tienes una tienda Action cerca, en Amazon también hay alternativas para este producto. Por ejemplo, este despertador solar con luz multicolor cuesta ahora 18,95 euros y lo puedes controlar incluso por app y por comandos de voz.

Simula el amanecer y tiene un diseño compacto
Si hay algo por lo que destaca este dispositivo, es por integrar una función de simulación del amanecer, incrementando gradualmente la intensidad de la luz minutos antes de que suene la alarma para que el cuerpo se adapte de forma natural al despertar.

Cuenta con un panel digital claro para consultar la hora, varios tonos de alarma configurables y un diseño compacto e intuitivo. Sin duda alguna, se trata de una opción muy asequible para acabar con el estrés matutino por un precio irrisorio.

articles.title: Apple préparerait une alternative moins chère, et sans écran, à l'Apple Watch
articles.text:
Selon le toujours très bien informé Mark Gurman, journaliste chez Bloomberg, Apple travaille sur un traqueur de santé et de forme physique, sans écran. Le projet en est encore au stade de prototype, mais l’entreprise à la pomme pourrait venir concurrencer certains géants du secteur, comme Whoop et Oura. Par ailleurs, ce bracelet serait commercialisé à un prix inférieur à celui des Apple Watch.
Apple travaillerait activement sur un bracelet connecté
Selon les informations de Mark Gurman, journaliste chez Bloomberg, Apple travaille activement sur la conception d’un bracelet connecté, sans écran. Celui-ci viendrait repenser la gamme de montres connectées et étoffer l’offre des objets connectés de la marque. Mais surtout, Apple entrerait directement en concurrence avec Whoop, Oura, Google, qui a récemment sorti le Fitbit Air, ainsi qu’avec Garmin qui s’est lancé sur ce marché avec le bracelet baptisé Cirqa.
Apple travaillerait sur plusieurs prototypes de bracelets connectés depuis maintenant des mois. Le projet en serait toujours à un stade préliminaire et une commercialisation de ce produit n’aurait pas lieu avant 2028. D’ailleurs, Gurman précise qu’une commercialisation n’est pas encore sûre, mais le projet existerait donc bel et bien. Tim Cook aurait manifesté un intérêt particulier pour ce traqueur de santé, tandis que Eddy Cue, responsable des Services et de la Santé chez Apple, inciterait ses équipes à adopter des fonctionnalités issues de ses nouveaux concurrents.
Un produit moins cher qu’une Apple Watch
Toujours selon Mark Gurman, le bracelet connecté d’Apple serait moins cher qu’une Apple Watch. En soi, cette information est logique. Le dispositif n’intégrant pas d’écran, il pourra être mis sur le marché à un prix inférieur à celui des Apple Watch. Il faudrait surtout voir à quel tarif ce bracelet connecté serait proposé face à ses concurrents.
Par ailleurs, la commercialisation d’un bracelet connecté pourrait permettre à Apple de proposer de nouveaux abonnements. Si Garmin a mis en avant le fait que son bracelet connecté Cirqa (commercialisé à 199,99 euros) ne nécessite pas d’abonnement payant, Apple pourrait, de son côté, en proposer un. Il reste maintenant à attendre une annonce officielle de la part d’Apple, mais elle ne risque pas d’arriver de sitôt.

articles.title: Nintendo cumple 137 años: Super Mario Bros, Donkey Kong, Zelda y hasta el exitoso Switch 2
articles.text:
Nintendo cumple 137 años desde su fundación, ocurrida el 23 de septiembre de 1889. Mucho antes de crear franquicias como Super Mario Bros., The Legend of Zelda y Donkey Kong, la compañía nació como fabricante de cartas de juego conocidas en Japón como hanafuda.
La empresa fue fundada como Nintendo Koppai por Fusajirō Yamauchi. Sin embargo, no obtuvo la denominación como personalidad jurídica de capital abierto hasta mediados de la década de 1960. Su primera consola fue lanzada en 1977.
PUBLICIDAD
El último lanzamiento en consolas de la empresa fue Nintendo Switch 2, que registró ventas récord tras su lanzamiento. El dispositivo vendió más de 3,5 millones de unidades en todo el mundo durante los cuatro días posteriores a su llegada al mercado, el 5 de junio de 2025.
No obstante, en 2026, Nintendo anunció un aumento global en los precios de sus consolas Switch. La medida entró en vigor en Japón el 25 de mayo y, en Estados Unidos, Canadá y Europa, el 1 de septiembre.
En Estados Unidos, el precio de la Nintendo Switch 2 pasó de USD 449,99 a USD 499,99. En Canadá, aumentó de 629,99 a 679,99 dólares. En Europa, la consola ahora tiene un precio de €499,99, frente a los €469,99 anteriores.
PUBLICIDAD
Luego del aumento, Nintendo reconoció el impacto de la medida y pidió disculpas a los usuarios durante una reunión con inversores posterior a la publicación de sus resultados financieros en mayo.
La compañía explicó que el incremento responde al aumento de los costos globales y adelantó que buscará mantener el interés de los jugadores mediante la ampliación del catálogo de videojuegos exclusivos para la consola.
A continuación, un repaso de los hitos de la compañía japonesa.
Cuál fue la primera consola de Nintendo
La primera consola de videojuegos de Nintendo fue la Color TV-Game, lanzada en Japón el 1 de junio de 1977. La compañía la desarrolló en colaboración con Mitsubishi Electronics y la comercializó exclusivamente en el mercado japonés.
PUBLICIDAD
La consola no utilizaba cartuchos ni juegos intercambiables, ya que los títulos estaban incorporados directamente en su placa.
El primer modelo, Color TV-Game 6, ofrecía seis variantes de juegos de tenis inspirados en Pong, entre ellas tenis, hockey y voleibol. Sus controles eran diales o ruedas giratorias integradas en la carcasa de la consola.
Cuáles fueron los primeros videojuegos de Nintendo
El primer acercamiento de Nintendo a los videojuegos fue EVR Race, lanzada en 1975. Era una máquina arcade electromecánica de apuestas basada en carreras de caballos, que utilizaba cintas de video para reproducir las imágenes.
Cuatro años después, la compañía desarrolló Sheriff, su primer videojuego arcade completamente electrónico y original. El título contó con diseño de Genyo Takeda y gráficos de Shigeru Miyamoto. En 1980, Nintendo lanzó Space Firebird, un juego de disparos espaciales que se convirtió en uno de sus primeros éxitos arcade a mayor escala.
PUBLICIDAD
La consagración internacional llegó en 1981 con Donkey Kong, el juego de plataformas creado por Miyamoto que presentó a Jumpman, el personaje que más tarde sería conocido como Mario.
Dos años después, Nintendo lanzó la consola Famicom en Japón, acompañada por adaptaciones de sus juegos arcade, entre ellos Donkey Kong, Donkey Kong Junior y Popeye.
La llegada de la NES a los mercados occidentales en 1985 impulsó aún más la expansión de la compañía. Entre los títulos que marcaron esa etapa estuvieron Super Mario Bros., Duck Hunt y Excitebike.
Llegada de la primera consola portátil de Nintendo
En 2004, Nintendo lanzó la Nintendo DS, su primera consola portátil con dos pantallas, una de ellas táctil. El dispositivo se convirtió en el sistema más vendido de la compañía.
PUBLICIDAD
Dos años después, presentó la Wii, una consola que incorporó controles por movimiento y amplió su alcance entre jugadores de distintas edades.
En 2017, Nintendo lanzó la Nintendo Switch, una consola híbrida que combinó las funciones de un dispositivo de sobremesa con la posibilidad de jugar de forma portátil.
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Meta colocou seres humanos para concluírem tarefas de agentes de IA • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Meta colocou seres humanos para concluírem tarefas de agentes de IA
Empresa suspendeu testes no Muse após funcionários apontarem riscos à privacidade dos usuários.
A Meta estaria testando o uso de atendentes humanos terceirizados em chamadas telefônicas que deveriam ser operadas pelo agente de IA Muse. A funcionalidade experimental, batizada de “concierge humano”, permite que, em algumas ocasiões, atendentes humanos discretamente assumam o controle de uma ligação.
O tal concierge seria um complemento a uma funcionalidade do Muse que permitia aos usuários usar o assistente para contatar estabelecimentos para agendar horários ou checar disponibilidade de produtos, entre outras ações. Os testes vinham ocorrendo desde agosto.
Em mensagens obtidas pela agência Reuters, a empresa explicava que “o Muse agora é capaz de repassar pedidos a um agente treinado, que realiza a chamada e cuida de todo o processo”. Essa operação com auxílio humano, porém, foi encerrada após críticas de funcionários.
Segundo apuração da agência, as queixas internas seriam motivadas por riscos à privacidade dos usuários. A preocupação é com a possível exposição de dados pessoais e outras informações sensíveis a funcionários terceirizados de call centers.
Não há muitas informações sobre o funcionamento da ferramenta, mas, como estamos falando de um redirecionamento “discreto”, entende-se que a transição possa não ser bem sinalizada.
Em resposta à repercussão negativa, uma executiva do Laboratório de Superinteligência admitiu em outro comunicado que “foi uma falha” iniciar os testes com operadores sem os devidos avisos de transparência. Ela confirmou que a novidade foi revertida por enquanto.
O porta-voz Daniel Roberts contrariou os vazamentos da agência: ele disse que o feedback teria sido “esmagadoramente positivo” e defendeu o aprimoramento do sistema. “Estamos trabalhando com comerciantes para continuar refinando esse potencial recurso de chamadas e só vamos lançá-lo quando estiver pronto”, afirmou.
Essa insistência, curiosamente, vem com o reconhecimento de que a intervenção humana trouxe mais eficiência à ferramenta – nenhuma novidade em serviços de atendimento. As taxas de sucesso do novo serviço ficariam entre 95% e 98%, segundo um documento interno, índice superior ao registrado pelas ligações via inteligência artificial.
A novidade segue o lançamento até então muito bem-sucedido do Muse, que assumiu a liderança do ranking de downloads de apps nos Estados Unidos, acumulando mais de 2,5 milhões de instalações nas primeiras duas semanas. O app não está disponível no Brasil.
O assistente é projetado para operar com autonomia na execução de rotinas como envio de e-mails, compras online e reservas de viagem. Ele rivaliza com o Gemini Spark e o Claude Cowork, entre outras ferramentas do tipo.
Durante a apresentação, a Meta deu ênfase redobrada à segurança: afirmou que cada usuário contaria com uma “máquina virtual” isolada na nuvem para blindar as sessões e que credenciais sensíveis ficariam guardadas em cofres criptografados específicos. A Amazon está entre as grandes companhias que bloquearam o agente.

articles.title: Bell, Cohere deploy Canadian cybersecurity AI for threat investigation
articles.text:
Bell Canada and AI company Cohere announced the launch of a cybersecurity AI model that will exist within Bell Cyber’s security operations.
The large language model (LLM), announced at Bell’s Cybersecurity Summit in Toronto, was built using Cohere’s enterprise AI technology and is designed to speed up threat investigations and equip analysts with more relevant, consistent analysis. It’s a domain-specific model, which means that it’s trained for a specific industry or function using data from that industry to improve accuracy and performance compared to general-purpose models.
According to the companies, the model was trained for cybersecurity use with data and operational knowledge from Bell Cyber. The press release also mentions that it is currently being integrated into Bell Cyber’s Autonomous Security Operations Centre (ASOC).
Bell says the model is designed to analyze and summarize complex security information, surface the context that is most relevant to an investigation, and support standardized investigative workflows. The company also noted that the model will reduce the time analysts spend gathering and interpreting information, allowing them to focus on validating threats, determining their impact, and directing the response.
Now, it was also noted that Bell Cyber’s ASOC already uses AI and automation to perform tasks like detecting, prioritizing, and containing threats. However, the new model will extend the current capability by “applying enterprise AI grounded in Bell Cyber’s domain knowledge to the language, evidence, and workflows used in investigations, while keeping analysts in control of consequential decisions.”
This partnership was first announced last year alongside a separate Cohere partnership with the Canadian Government. Interestingly, Cohere recently merged with German company Aleph Alpha.

articles.title: Review: Apple's hyper-pricey M5 Ultra Mac Studio made me into a vibe coder
articles.text:
When Apple was using Intel processors and AMD GPUs, the idea of an expandable and upgradeable tower made sense. But Apple Silicon chips bring the CPU, GPU, and memory interface all under one roof in a way that makes that sort of upgradeability not just superfluous but impossible. At least not without breaking some of the chips’ key benefits.
And as it happens, Apple Silicon’s combination of a fast CPU, solid GPU, and unified memory architecture has made it a good fit for a modern “pro” workload that really pushes high-end hardware: running language models and agents locally.
That’s really the core audience for the M5 Ultra Mac Studio, Apple’s tippity-top config that is jumping two processor generations in a single refresh (there was no M4 Ultra, if you recall). The highest-end Studios have always felt like a bit of overkill for most people, but now there’s a particular kind of AI-pilled coder or designer who can legitimately benefit from having this kind of system on their desk.
Apple was caught off guard by the demand for these systems from people running software like OpenClaw and running open-weight models locally, which, along with the AI-fueled memory shortage, is why it has been nearly impossible to buy most of these systems for months. That’s the context that the new Mac Studio is launching into.
Same design, new hardware
Same design language as the Mac mini, but less mini.

Andrew Cunningham
The new Mac Studio looks the same as it did when it launched with the M1 Max and M1 Ultra back in 2022. It’s a small, squat box, with the same 7.7-by-7.7-inch footprint as the old Mac mini, but it’s taller. Both the Max and Ultra variants of the Studio look the same, but the M5 Ultra version weighs two pounds more because it has heavier but more-conductive copper in its heatsink to help cool the more powerful chip.
Both Studio models also come with nearly all the same ports. On the back, you’ll find four 120Gbps Thunderbolt 5 ports, a 10Gbps Ethernet port, an HDMI 2.1 port, and a pair of 5Gbps USB-A ports. On the front, both Studios have a UHS-II SD card reader, but the Max comes with two 10Gbps USB-C ports, and the Ultra comes with two more 120Gbps Thunderbolt 5 ports.
The Ultra’s additional oomph extends to external display support. The M5 Max supports up to five external displays, and the M5 Ultra supports up to eight, though both come with caveats depending on the resolution and refresh rates you’re using.
Display support details for the M5 Max and M5 Ultra Mac Studios.
Credit:
Apple
Display support details for the M5 Max and M5 Ultra Mac Studios.
Credit:
Apple
The M5 Max is a known quantity at this point, and Apple has been shipping it since March in the MacBook Pro. It improved over the last-generation M4 Max by introducing new “super” cores for the CPU and nudging the maximum memory bandwidth up from 546GB/s to 614GB/s. The number of GPU cores stayed the same (40), but new neural accelerators built into each GPU core helped improve its performance for ML/AI-assisted technologies like MetalFX upscaling and frame generation.
The M5 Ultra is a bigger departure for a few reasons. The first is that there was no M4 Ultra, so we’re effectively hopping two processor generations despite only jumping a single product generation.
