articles.title: Leasing social 2026 : voilà combien de véhicules il reste (et quels modèles sont encore disponibles)
Graphify: Unifying Codebase Context to Streamline Agentic Software Engineering
articles.text:
Graphify is an open-source tool that converts codebases, documents, and unstructured data into queryable, multimodal knowledge graphs to optimise AI coding workflows. Launched in April 2026, it follows a rapid release cadence of frequent weekly updates. Recent improvements bring advanced parser features, such as Terraform block attribute preservation and cross-file method resolutions. Community feedback on Reddit and developer blogs highlights its strong conceptual appeal for architectural mapping, balanced by early-tool adoption friction in daily workflows.
As software systems grow in complexity and AI coding assistants become central to modern development workflows, the challenge of giving large language models accurate cross-file awareness has intensified. Graphify, an open-source utility, tries to bridge this gap. Released under the dual MIT and Apache-2.0 licenses, the project first kicked off in April 2026 and quickly captured developer attention, crossing thousands of GitHub stars within its first ten days. Operating with a rapid, fast-paced release cadence of multiple updates per month, the project continuously evolves to refine how codebases and documentation map into structured knowledge graphs. By automatically transforming repositories and mixed folders into searchable nodes and edges, Graphify moves developers away from linear file browsing and token-heavy searching toward structured graph navigation.
The core purpose of Graphify centres on solving the context-window and memory limits of AI coding agents. Traditional coding assistants often struggle with multi-file reasoning and deep dependencies because they treat repositories as isolated pools of text. Graphify solves this by executing a multi-stage pipeline that scans target directories, extracts structural AST elements using tree-sitter alongside semantic cues from documentation, and builds a unified graph clustered through community detection algorithms. This output can then be queried directly or integrated with AI coding assistants via Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, achieving substantial token reductions compared to naive file reading approaches.
The FastAPI codebase mapped by graphify. Every node is a concept, colours are detected communities, and the whole thing is clickable. Image Source: Graphify GitHub Repo
Recent changes implemented across recent iterations have focused heavily on deepening language parser intelligence and reducing false positives. Notable updates include advanced Terraform block attribute preservation, which keeps infrastructure configurations queryable alongside standard source code. Engineers working with multi-language codebases have also received robust cross-file method resolution upgrades, including split impl block support for generic types in Rust, external receiver tracking for Kotlin, and scope-qualified static call routing for C++. Furthermore, recent releases introduced smart Markdown code span tracking that maps inline documentation references directly to code symbols, embedded script indexing inside PHP files, and cleaner dependency mapping for subpath package imports.
Graphify in action. Image Source: Graphify GitHub Repo
Graphify was built with the intention of mapping repositories that contain multiple types of information sources, like code, documentation in Markdown or PDF and even images. Once the knowledge graph is created, it will allow you to navigate and further understand the repository in an easy and fast way. It's available on macOS, Windows and Ubuntu/ Linux, and it can be installed via uv. Its first-party benchmarks report LOCOMO recall@10 of 0.497, 45.3% QA accuracy, 76% on a 50-question LongMemEval-S subset and an ERPNext key-fact coverage lift from 70.8% to 82.0% across six questions.
Community feedback across platforms like Reddit and independent engineering blogs paints a nuanced picture of the tool's current maturity curve. Developers discussing the project on communities such as r/ClaudeAI and detailed technical reviews like those on Kevin Kinnett's blog note that the project's conceptual architecture is exceptionally promising for large-scale repo orientation, onboarding, and architectural reviews. Users have shared mixed experiences regarding day-to-day integration; while some praise its context-mapping magic inside tools like Claude Code, others on threads like r/ClaudeAI - Graphify vs Code-Review-Graph point out that brute-force navigation or standard grepping can still feel faster for mid-sized repositories until the graph tooling matures further. Ultimately, the community views Graphify as a visionary step forward for agentic coding workflows that will continue to sharpen as its parsing backend evolves.

articles.title: Meta Connect 2026, everything Meta announced including Muse
articles.text:
Table of contents
Meta Connect 2026 took place on September 23 and 24 at Meta’s headquarters in Menlo Park, California, where Mark Zuckerberg unveiled new smart glasses, a lighter VR headset, and a small device designed to work with Muse, Meta’s AI agent.
Meta also introduced its first smart glasses without a camera, as concerns grow about people being recorded without their knowledge by camera-equipped glasses. The new glasses remove the camera but retain microphones and can still connect to Meta’s AI services.
If you live in Africa, you also want to know which of these devices you can buy at home. This article covers every big announcement, prices, release dates, and what you can expect in your country.
Everything Meta announced at Meta Connect 2026
Here is a quick look at each device’s price and release date.
| Product | Starting price | Availability | 
|---|---|---|
| Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 | $449 | On sale now in supported markets | 
| Ray-Ban Meta Audio | $349 | Pre-orders open; ships October 13 | 
| Meta Adventurer | $249 | Pre-orders open; on sale October 23 | 
| Meta Glasses LISA Edition | $399 | Announced; check your local store | 
| Meta VR Glasses | $1,299.99 | Spring 2027 | 
| Muse Charm | Not announced | Release date not announced | 
These are Meta’s US prices. Prices in your country may be different.
1. Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3
Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 starts at $449 and is on sale now in markets where Meta sells its glasses. It replaces the Gen 2 model from 2025. Here is what changes:
- Slimmer frames and adjustable temple tips for a better fit
- Up to nine hours of battery life, one hour more than Gen 2
- A new action button that opens Meta AI fast, so you can skip saying “Hey Meta” on a quiet train
- Six microphones that Meta says block more than 90% of background noise on calls
The camera stays the same. You still get 12-megapixel photos and 3K video.
Gen 3 comes in 27 frame-and-lens combinations, including the new Aviator and Zena cat-eye frames alongside the classic Wayfarer. A limited-edition Aviator Connect model starts at $579. That is $70 more than the Gen 2’s launch price, according to Gear Live.
2. The LISA edition
Meta teamed up with BLACKPINK star LISA on two frames: Adventurer LISA Edition and Capri LISA Edition. Both start at $399. You get:
- Star details on the frames
- A special case
- Case charms based on her pets
- Digital photocards you unlock with the glasses
These frames are part of the Meta Glasses range. They are separate from the Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3.
3. Ray-Ban Meta Audio
Ray-Ban Meta Audio is Meta’s first pair of audio glasses. Open-ear speakers let you play music, take calls, listen to podcasts, and chat with Meta AI. The glasses have no camera, so they cannot take photos or record video.
This is Meta’s clearest answer to people uneasy about camera glasses. Some privacy questions remain. The glasses still have microphones, and your voice requests still go to an AI service.
- Weight: 43 grams
- Battery: up to 12 hours per charge, plus up to 48 more hours from the case
- Frames: Clubmaster and Burbank, with 23 colour and lens combinations
- Price and date: from $349, pre-orders open now, ships October 13
4. Meta VR Glasses
Meta VR Glasses look like thick glasses instead of a strapped headset. They weigh about 100 grams. Meta says that makes them five times lighter than Quest 3.
Meta gets there by splitting the device in two. The glasses hold the displays and sensors. A small puck holds the processor and battery, and it also stores your apps. An optical cable links the glasses to the puck, which you can clip to your pocket or set on a table.
Meta VR Glasses cost $1,299.99 and arrive in spring 2027.
How you control them
You control the glasses with your eyes and hand gestures. Voice commands work too. Controllers are optional.
- More than 75 games work with hand gestures at launch
- Touch Plus controllers work for games that need them
- A Bluetooth gamepad works with Xbox Cloud Gaming
- Beat Saber gets a new hand-tracking mode called Flux next spring, on both VR Glasses and Quest
Work and entertainment
For work, you can open several virtual screens at once. Meta says your desk can act as a keyboard and touchpad. You can also connect a Mac or Windows PC.
For fun, Meta lined up streaming and sports partners. You also get immersive versions of Avengers: Infinity War and Star Wars: A New Hope. Some films and sports streams depend on your country and your subscriptions.
Hologram calls
Meta also showed a feature it calls hologram. You scan your face with your phone, and Meta builds a lifelike digital version of you. It copies your face and expressions live during calls. It comes to Meta VR Glasses at launch. Meta Ray-Ban Display users in the US get early access on WhatsApp first.
5. Muse Charm
Muse Charm is a small, pocket-sized gadget for talking to Muse. It uses Muse’s live voice model, so you speak to it the way you speak on a phone call.
Meta showed Muse Charm on stage but shared few details. It has not announced a price or a release date and says it will share more later this year.
Tom’s Guide reports that the device has a fingerprint sensor on its edge and works without a phone. The outlet also reports that Zuckerberg wants it out in time for the holidays. Meta has not confirmed these details, so treat them as early reports.
6. Muse, Meta’s AI agent
What Muse does
Meta launched Muse on September 8, two weeks before Connect. Muse can open websites, fill forms, plan trips, and shop for you. It asks for your approval before sensitive steps, like sending an email or paying for something. Muse runs inside its own protected virtual computer, which Meta calls Muse Secure VM.
Shopping, travel and work tools
Meta added new connections so Muse can do more for you:
- Shopping: Walmart, Best Buy, Sephora, Ulta, Wayfair, Gap and Fanatics
- Payments: Shop Pay and PayPal, on top of Stripe’s Link, which Muse already supported
- Travel and groceries: Expedia for trips and Instacart for grocery orders
- Work: Notion, Granola, GitHub and Box
Check that a service works in your country before you rely on it. Meta’s list does not promise that every partner works everywhere.
Muse on Mac and on your glasses
Muse for Mac can now use the apps on your computer, with your permission. You can give it a list of tasks, walk away, and it keeps working.
On supported AI glasses, Muse will answer to its name and help with whatever you are looking at. Meta says this arrives in the next few months. It has not shared dates for each model or country.
A custom voice and face
You can describe the voice you want Muse to have, including how fast it talks and its accent. Meta also announced a live avatar that gives Muse an expressive face on screen. Muse also gets its own email address.
7. New features for Meta glasses
Hearing enhancement
Meta announced FDA-cleared software that helps adults with mild to moderate hearing loss. It arrives in the US later this year on supported glasses. You pay $149.99 to add it, or you get it with a Meta One subscription. Meta has not said if the $149.99 is a yearly fee.
Better maps on Meta Ray-Ban Display
Meta Ray-Ban Display gets cycling and public transit directions later this month in the US and Canada. Early access to hologram calls on Display comes to the US in the coming months. Meta also opened online orders for Display and started selling it in more countries outside the US.
Private Processing and camera tools
Meta says Private Processing is coming to its AI glasses. It lets some AI requests run without Meta seeing your data. Meta also announced new camera tools, including dynamic photos and Dolby Atmos video capture later on. Meta has not shared one rollout date for all these features.
Other Meta Connect 2026 announcements
- Meta Adventurer: Meta’s cheapest Meta Glasses yet. It pairs a black frame with grey lenses and ships with a plug-in case. It costs $249 and goes on sale October 23 in all countries where Meta Glasses are sold
- New frames: Capri and Nova frames join the range. A limited Meta Fury edition with a clear frame and mirrored lenses sells only at Connect and Meta Lab stores at launch
- Mix & Match: a new US programme that lets you build your own pair
- More styles: Meta says it will offer more than 100 glasses options across its brands by the end of 2026
Meta’s event recap does not include a new Quest headset.
Detailed specs
These are the specs Meta has confirmed so far.
Display
- Meta VR Glasses: micro-OLED 5K Infinite Display
- Meta VR Glasses: 37 pixels per degree
- Meta VR Glasses: Dolby Vision support
- Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 and Ray-Ban Meta Audio: no display
Processor
- Meta VR Glasses: Qualcomm Snapdragon Reality Elite, housed in the puck
- Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 and Ray-Ban Meta Audio: Meta has not named the chip
Battery and charging
- Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3: up to 9 hours
- Ray-Ban Meta Audio: up to 12 hours, plus up to 48 hours from the case
- Meta VR Glasses: up to 3 hours of high-resolution media playback
- Meta VR Glasses: 45W charging on the puck
Camera
- Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3: 12MP photos and 3K video
- Ray-Ban Meta Audio: no camera
Audio and microphones
- Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3: six microphones that cut more than 90% of background noise
- Meta VR Glasses: Dolby Atmos audio
Weight
- Ray-Ban Meta Audio: 43 grams
- Meta VR Glasses: about 100 grams for the glasses
Some spec sheets online list the VR Glasses’ per-eye resolution, plus RAM, storage size, and puck weight. Meta has not confirmed those numbers yet.
Will the new glasses come to Nigeria, Kenya and South Africa?
South Africa
Meta names South Africa among 12 new markets getting Ray-Ban Meta and Oakley Meta glasses later in 2026. Ray-Ban Meta Optics is on the list too.
Meta has not shared a local date or price. It also has not promised South Africa the new Audio glasses or the VR Glasses, and Muse Charm has no launch market yet.
Nigeria and Kenya
Meta has not announced a launch in Nigeria or Kenya for any of these devices. You may find imported units from sellers on Jumia, Konga, Jiji, or Slot. Before you pay, check these four things:
- The exact model and generation
- Warranty cover
- Which AI features work in your country
- The seller’s return policy
Naira and shilling prices move with exchange rates and import costs. The price you see this week may change next week.
Features with country limits
Some features only work in certain countries for now:
- Hearing enhancement: US only
- Hologram calls on Display: US early access
- Cycling and transit directions on Display: US and Canada
- Muse shopping partners: mostly US stores
If you live in Lagos, Accra, Nairobi, or Johannesburg, wait for local support details before you pay for a device because of these features.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. articles.title: Vulnerability alert fatigue nearly swamped WHOOP. But its fix still keeps a human in charge.
articles.text:
Vulnerability alert fatigue nearly swamped WHOOP. But its fix still keeps a human in charge.
With often hundreds of thousands of alerts a day, many tech organizations are buried in vulnerabilities and worn down by alert fatigue. The rise of AI has only made it harder to cut through the noise and to find actionable alerts. Manual security and site reliability engineering is not an option.
The engineering team behind WHOOP‘s health and fitness tracker felt this pain, relying on multi-day, all-hands triage sessions to stay on top of the alert deluge. But, as a high-growth consumer health company handling sensitive user data, it couldn’t afford to miss anything. Which is why the team at WHOOP built an automated vulnerability-response workflow based on the company’s specific technical, operational, and trust considerations.
Join The New Stack on Wednesday, October 7 to learn from WHOOP staff engineer Vinay Raghu and Datadog senior product engineer Amber Tunnell how WHOOP built and implemented this workflow using Datadog Bits AI and Workflow Automation for faster, at-scale response.
Join us on October 7, 2026, for a live Datadog x TNS event
You have successfully registered for the webinar.
DevSecOps, security, and cloud/platform engineers should bring their questions to this live demo-slash-case study to learn how to reduce friction between developer velocity and security requirements without increasing headcount.
What you’ll take away from our live webinar
Raghu and Tunnell engineers will share how they were able to:
- Focus on real exposure vs. scanner noise. Not everything is critical. You’ll learn how WHOOP used Datadog’s Software Composition Analysis (SCA) to analyze runtime code execution and prioritize active threats.
- Route the right vulnerability to the right engineer. WHOOP automated vulnerability mapping to microservice owners, so developers received tickets with full context attached.
- Build automated guardrails for devs to self-resolve. This let security engineers pivot from frustrating gatekeeping and ticket-pushing to more proactive, systemic work that adds value.
- Maintain a human in the loop. With such sensitive data and a demand to be always-on, WHOOP isn’t ready to automate the engineer out. Learn how they decided their team’s response had to change.
And then, of course, we will end the live discussion with how to measure it all. Don’t miss out and register to attend on October 7.

articles.title: Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 reaches 5GHz while going big on agentic AI
articles.text:
First look: Echoing Apple's recent iPhone 18 unveiling, Qualcomm has introduced two new Snapdragon 8 Elite mobile processors with AI assistants as a primary focus. While the chips significantly outperform the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 in CPU performance, GPU performance, and power efficiency, Qualcomm clearly sees AI agent support as the new lineup's main selling point.
Qualcomm revealed the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 at this year's Snapdragon Summit. The mobile SoCs will power future flagship Android devices from Doubao, Honor, Motorola, Oppo, RedMagic, Stepx, Vivo, and Xiaomi.
Built on a 2nm process node that enhances power efficiency by 37%, both chips feature two Oryon Prime CPU cores that achieve 5GHz, six 4GHz performance cores, and 16MB of Flex Cache. While the standard Elite Gen 6 improves CPU performance by 10% over its predecessor, the Extreme variant extends the gain to 13%.
GPU and NPU performance enhancements are much more impressive. The new Adreno GPUs outperform the Elite Gen 5 by 35% and 44% in the standard and Extreme models, respectively, while raising power efficiency by 40%, partially thanks to AI rendering via the new Adreno Neural Fusion.
Meanwhile, the Elite Gen 6's Hexagon NPU runs AI applications 14% faster in the standard model and 35% faster in the extreme variant, with AI performance-per-watt increasing by 20% and 33%, respectively.
Most of Qualcomm's trailer for the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 focused on showing AI agents automating various everyday tasks that might take humans multiple steps. In one clip, an agent automatically sorts a newly recorded video and provides options for editing it. In another, a jogger receives a notification about a nearby property that meets their preferences, with the option to automatically share a photo and book a viewing appointment.
Regarding sound, AI also facilitates audio separation and voice isolation. Even the Qualcomm X105 5G wireless modem is AI-enhanced, improving energy efficiency while also increasing upload and download speeds. Meanwhile, Qualcomm's Wi-Fi 8-compliant FastConnect 8800 can achieve 10Gbps with a 4x4 Wi-Fi configuration, tripling the gigabit range over prior models.
Camera performance is another notable difference between the two tiers. 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6-powered phones can record video at up to 60fps in 8K, while the cheaper SoC only achieves 30fps at that resolution.
The earliest devices powered by Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 will include the RedMagic 12Pro+, iQOO 16, and iQOO Pad Ultra.

articles.title: ZeroDrift launches three models for real-time AI compliance checks - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
ZeroDrift launches three models for real-time AI compliance checks
ZeroDrift Inc., a startup that automates compliance for artificial intelligence communications, today launched Anchor 3.0, a family of small language models designed to check messages generated by AI agents before they’re sent.
The company said the models can enforce financial regulations and internal corporate policies while operating fast enough to examine every outgoing message in real time. Anchor 3.0 is generally available through ZeroDrift’s Enforcement application programming interface.
The approach targets a growing operational problem: Autonomous agents can generate thousands of customer communications faster than human compliance teams can review them.
ZeroDrift reported that its flagship model detected more than 95% of violations in a benchmark based on Financial Industry Regulatory Authority rules. It said the model matched the overall accuracy of OpenAI Group PBC’s GPT-6 Astra and Anthropic PBC’s Claude Fable 5.1 while operating more than 34 times faster and at 1/12th the cost.
The benchmark used attorney-labeled data produced independently by data-labeling company Surge AI Inc., according to ZeroDrift. However, ZeroDrift published the benchmark itself, so the performance figures remain company claims.
“Frontier models made it easy to build capable agents,” founder and Chief Executive Kumesh Aroomoogan said in a statement. “The hard part is running them inside a regulated business, where every message has to follow the rules and the check has to happen every time, before anything goes out.”
Anchor operates within ZeroDrift’s broader compliance platform, which intercepts communications and checks them against regulatory requirements and company policies. The system can flag, rewrite, block or route problematic messages for human review while recording the decision for later audit. The company recently introduced Guard for Agents, an API-based service that inserts those checks directly into agent workflows.
The new family has three versions. Anchor 3.0 Mini is a 9 billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 4 billion active parameters. Intended for high-volume traffic, it runs prebuilt rule packs and flags violations. ZeroDrift said Mini caught about 5% more violations than Claude Fable 5.1 and about 20% more than GPT-6 Astra in its FINRA test, with fewer than half as many false positives as Claude.
The flagship Anchor 3.0 model has the same parameter count but can apply more than 200 prebuilt rules covering FINRA, the Securities and Exchange Commission and other regulations. It identifies the lines that violate a rule and can rewrite them before a message is released.
Anchor 3.0 Max is a 27 billion-parameter model intended for long documents, attachments and enforcement of a company’s own policies without additional fine-tuning. The models were post-trained from Google LLC’s Gemma E4B and Alibaba Group Holding Ltd.’s Qwen3.8-27B models.
The production release follows an August preview in which ZeroDrift disclosed that Anchor combined deterministic checks with an open-source model trained on regulatory material and attorney-labeled communications. At that time, the company described the software as a risk-reduction layer rather than a guarantee that every violation would be caught.

articles.title: NUSX expands into Munich through UnternehmerTUM partnership (Sponsored) | EU-Startups
articles.text:
NUS Enterprise, the entrepreneurial heart of the National University of Singapore (NUS), is deepening its global links as NUSX through a new partnership with UnternehmerTUM.
The collaboration will connect the Singapore and Munich innovation ecosystems, giving NUS DeepTech ventures more direct access to European partners, investors and market opportunities, while opening Singapore and Asia to Munich-based ventures.
Munich is one of Europe’s leading technology and innovation hubs, ranking among Europe’s top five in the Global Tech Ecosystem Index 2026 and 11th globally for AI. Its strengths in research, technology and venture creation make it a strategic base for NUSX ventures looking to access partners, capital and markets across Europe.
The partnership will focus on three areas: reciprocal outposts, investment and talent development, with initial efforts centred on biotech, AI and semiconductors.
A new NUSX base in Munich
At the centre of the partnership is NUSX’s second global outpost, which will be based at the Munich Urban Colab, an 11,000-square-metre innovation centre jointly established by UnternehmerTUM and the City of Munich.
From there, NUSX will connect NUS DeepTech ventures with the wider UnternehmerTUM and TUM Venture Labs ecosystem, providing access to industry partners, technical expertise and opportunities to validate technologies in the European market.
The connection is intended to work both ways. TUM Venture Labs, a joint initiative of the Technical University of Munich (TUM) and UnternehmerTUM, is exploring a representative presence at the NUS i³ building in Singapore, where NUSX is based.
This would give Munich-based ventures a direct entry point into Singapore’s innovation ecosystem and wider connections across Asia.
The collaboration builds on NUS Enterprise’s longstanding relationship with TUM through the NUS Overseas Colleges (NOC) programme. NOC Munich was established in 2017 and has since connected nearly 120 NUS students and more than 90 TUM students through exchanges between Singapore and Munich.
Alumni of the programme have gone on to build ventures including Factorem.
“This collaboration with UnternehmerTUM builds on our longstanding ties with the Technical University of Munich as NUSX deepens its global venture-building network,” said Dr. Tan Sian Wee, NUS Senior Vice President (Innovation & Enterprise).
“Through reciprocal outposts, deeper investment links, and new opportunities for our students and startups, we are bringing talent, research and capital closer together. This gives founders greater access to the partners, expertise and markets they need to validate, build and scale DeepTech ventures from Singapore.”
Deepening investment links
Investment will form another part of the collaboration. NUS is in advanced discussions with a Munich-based venture capital firm closely affiliated with UnternehmerTUM to join the €102 million NUS VC Programme as its fifth VC partner.
The move would expand the network of international investors supporting NUS-affiliated ventures and give founders stronger links to European capital. More broadly, the partnership is designed to support ventures across the full journey from talent development and research commercialisation to investment and global market entry.
Its initial focus on BioTech, AI and semiconductors reflects areas of strength across both ecosystems. TUM ranks first in Germany in data science and AI, while its School of Life Sciences is home to 10 of the university’s 17 most-cited researchers.
The areas also align with NUSX’s innovation priorities and Singapore’s RIE2030 strategy, which commits €25 billion (S$37 billion) over five years to research, innovation and enterprise, including flagship programmes in semiconductors and health.
Building venture talent across borders
The partnership will also create new opportunities for NUS students to gain hands-on venture-building experience in Munich.
NOC students will have opportunities to intern with portfolio companies of the Munich-based VC partner, gaining direct exposure to building and scaling technology ventures in Europe.
Selected NUS students will also be able to access UnternehmerTUM programmes focused on IP-based venture creation, including Startup Launchpad, Digital Product School and the UnternehmerTUM Incubator.
These opportunities build on NUS Enterprise’s existing presence in Munich while broadening students’ exposure to research commercialisation, venture creation and technology businesses in Europe.
“With this partnership, we open a direct gateway between two of the world’s most dynamic innovation ecosystems,” said Professor Helmut Schönenberger, CEO, UnternehmerTUM and Vice President, Entrepreneurship, TUM.
“DeepTech ventures need more than one home market to grow – they need access to research, capital and industry partners across continents. By connecting Munich and Singapore through reciprocal outposts, we give founders on both sides exactly that: a direct path from an idea to a global venture. This is a natural next step in our long-standing collaboration with NUS, and we look forward to building it together with NUSX.”

articles.title: Los errores más comunes al mantener un vehículo híbrido, según experto
articles.text:
El mercado de vehículos híbridos en Colombia crece a un ritmo acelerado, pero ese entusiasmo por la nueva tecnología no siempre viene acompañado del conocimiento técnico necesario para cuidarla. Entre enero y agosto de 2026 se registraron 63.210 unidades híbridas en el país, un 61% más que en el mismo periodo de 2025, según el Informe de Registro de Vehículos de FENALCO y ANDI.
Solo en agosto se sumaron 9.195 vehículos, un 51,6% más que un año atrás. Ante este panorama, especialistas advierten que el mantenimiento de estos autos exige atención específica, distinta a la de un vehículo de combustión tradicional, y que ignorar esas particularidades puede derivar en desgaste prematuro o reparaciones costosas.
PUBLICIDAD
Por qué un híbrido exige más cuidado en el mantenimiento del aceite
Uno de los errores más frecuentes entre nuevos propietarios es suponer que un híbrido demanda menos mantenimiento por combinar motor eléctrico y de combustión. La realidad es la opuesta, según explica Jesús Cano, técnico regional de Castrol.
El motor de combustión de estos vehículos no funciona de manera continua: se enciende, se apaga y vuelve a arrancar en ciclos constantes para alternar con el sistema eléctrico.
Esa intermitencia expone al aceite a mayor humedad y oxidación, mientras que las variaciones de temperatura obligan a reforzar la protección interna del motor.
“Un aceite pensado para híbridos debe ofrecer excelente protección contra el desgaste, alta resistencia a la oxidación, rápida circulación en arranque en frío y capacidad para mantener limpio el motor. Todo esto ayuda a conservar la eficiencia de combustible y el desempeño del sistema de carga de la batería”, explica Cano.
PUBLICIDAD
A esto se suma otro error habitual: elegir el lubricante sin considerar las especificaciones técnicas del vehículo. “Los híbridos suelen requerir viscosidades bajas y una mayor reducción de fricción por sus constantes arranques y apagados”, señala el especialista, lo que descarta la idea de usar cualquier aceite disponible en el mercado sin verificar su compatibilidad.
Intervalos de cambio de aceite: por qué no conviene extenderlos
Otro comportamiento riesgoso es asumir que, como el motor de combustión trabaja menos tiempo, los cambios de aceite pueden espaciarse por decisión propia. Cano aclara que los intervalos dependen de las especificaciones del fabricante, el tipo de conducción, el clima y las condiciones de uso, y que estos factores no deben interpretarse de forma libre por el conductor.
PUBLICIDAD
“El error más común que vemos es asumir que un híbrido necesita menos mantenimiento. Usar un fluido que no cumple la especificación del fabricante o extender demasiado los intervalos de cambio puede derivar en desgaste prematuro, pérdida de eficiencia, sobrecalentamiento de componentes y, en los casos más severos, reparaciones costosas tanto en el motor de combustión como en el sistema eléctrico”, advierte Cano.
Este punto resulta especialmente relevante porque el impacto de un mal mantenimiento no se limita al motor tradicional, sino que puede extenderse al sistema eléctrico del vehículo, uno de los componentes más costosos de reparar.
PUBLICIDAD
El papel del refrigerante en la protección del sistema eléctrico
El aceite no es el único fluido que requiere seguimiento riguroso en un híbrido. En varios modelos, el refrigerante también cumple una función en la regulación térmica de componentes de alto voltaje, como la batería, el inversor y el motor eléctrico.
Un manejo inadecuado de la temperatura en estos sistemas puede afectar directamente el desempeño, la eficiencia y la durabilidad del vehículo, por lo que descuidar el refrigerante equivale a exponer no solo el motor de combustión, sino también la parte eléctrica que distingue a esta tecnología.
Un híbrido es un vehículo que combina motor eléctrico y de combustión, y su motor térmico se enciende y apaga de forma constante para alternar con el sistema eléctrico. Ese funcionamiento intermitente exige un aceite con mayor resistencia a la oxidación y una vigilancia especial del refrigerante, que además protege la batería de alto voltaje.
PUBLICIDAD
Recomendaciones para prolongar la vida útil de un vehículo híbrido
A partir de estos señalamientos, existen pautas concretas que los propietarios de híbridos deberían seguir para evitar fallas evitables:
- Seguir siempre las especificaciones de aceite y refrigerante que indique el fabricante del vehículo, sin aplicar criterios propios de un carro de combustión tradicional.
- No espaciar los cambios de aceite más allá de lo recomendado, aun cuando el motor de combustión funcione menos tiempo que en un vehículo convencional.
- No pasar por alto el refrigerante, ya que en varios híbridos protege también la batería de alto voltaje y el motor eléctrico, no solo el bloque del motor. Usar lubricantes totalmente sintéticos formulados para bajas viscosidades y ciclos frecuentes de arranque y apagado.
Los beneficios de un híbrido en materia de eficiencia y reducción de emisiones dependen, en buena medida, de que su propietario entienda cómo funcionan sus sistemas internos. Utilizar los fluidos correctos y respetar los intervalos técnicos son factores que inciden de forma directa en la vida útil del vehículo.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Anthropic anuncia novo Claude Opus 5.5, com capacidade ainda maior • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Anthropic anuncia novo Claude Opus 5.5, com capacidade ainda maior
Modelo promete igualar desempenho do Mythos 5.1 para trabalhos de cibersegurança e biologia. Recursos de segurança também são reforçados.
A Anthropic revelou seu novo Claude Opus 5.5, o modelo de IA mais avançado da empresa até o momento. Ele alcança a capacidade de Mythos 5.1 e Fable 5.1 em atividades relacionadas a cibersegurança e biologia, garantindo também novas salvaguardas para mitigar casos de uso indevido.
Segundo a desenvolvedora, a IA é também mais rápida e assertiva, migrando códigos de 680 mil linhas em apenas um dia. Outra vantagem citada pela empresa é o custo, 40% inferior ao do Opus 5. Esse modelo é o mais recomendado da Anthropic para trabalhos aprofundados de programação, engenharia de software e automação.
Além do Opus 5.5, outras duas IAs devem ser atualizadas nas próximas semanas: Sonnet 5.5 e Haiku 5.5, voltados para maior velocidade e eficiência, respectivamente. O lançamento do novo modelo vem na sequência da polêmica envolvendo as denúncias de um funcionário da Anthropic e o posicionamento do próprio CEO, Dario Amodei, pedindo a diminuição no ritmo de desenvolvimento da IA.
Com a novidade, a Anthropic promete capacidade semelhante aos modelos mais avançados Mythos 5.1 e Fable 5.1 para assuntos relacionados a cibersegurança e biologia. Da mesma forma, mecanismos de defesa presentes no Fable aparecem no novo Opus 5.5, como o downgrade pontual para o Opus 4.8 e Opus 5 a depender da situação.
Segundo a Anthropic, a novidade alcançou as melhores notas em uma auditoria comportamental automatizada realizada internamente. Isso significa que o modelo tem menos chances de burlar salvaguardas em tentativas de uso indevido, além de ser mais resistente que seu antecessor Opus 5 a tentativas de prompt injection.
Em termos de performance, a empresa fala em um grande salto para trabalhos complexos. Segundo a Anthropic, de 40 repetições de processos de reparo de software, o novo Opus 5.5 resolveu 39 casos, ficando acima do Opus 5, que buscou alternativas menos eficientes. Também foi testada a qualidade da IA para desenvolver jogos do zero com um único prompt, com destaque para os resultados da nova inteligência em gráficos e acabamentos.
Da mesma forma, o “preço” para rodar o Opus 5.5 também se destaca, com 40% menos custo para trabalhos em geral. A Anthropic promete US$ 4 a US$ 20 (R$ 20 a 100, em conversão direta) para cada 1 milhão de tokens, um quinto da precificação do Opus 5 padrão. Já pensando em leituras de cache, relacionadas principalmente aos trabalhos agênticos, a empresa fala em US$ 0,20 (R$ 1) a cada milhão, valor 60% menor.
A Anthropic divulgou gráficos com vantagens frente ao mais recente GPT-6 Astra, da Open AI (aquele que decifrou uma antiga mensagem cifrada da Primeira Guerra Mundial), tanto em custo-benefício quanto em trabalhos de coding e pesquisa. A companhia também promete uma comunicação mais fluida e assertiva, com informações mais importantes vindo primeiro e um estilo de escrita mais fácil de entender.
A Anthropic já liberou o novo Opus 5.5 em sua plataforma, que pode ser ativado com o código “claude-opus-5-5”. Segundo a empresa, há um limite de 5 horas para usar o modelo, disponível nas assinaturas Pro, Max, Team e Enterprise. Esse tempo pode ser regulado pelos próprios usuários ao escolherem apenas tarefas específicas.

articles.title: TechPowerUp GPU-Z v2.71.0 Released
articles.text:
Wednesday, September 23rd 2026
	
									
	
	
	
TechPowerUp GPU-Z v2.71.0 Released
TechPowerUp released the latest version of GPU-Z, our lightweight graphics subsystem information, diagnostics, and monitoring utility for gamers, engineers, and enthusiasts. Version 2.71.0 introduces NVIDIA GeForce RTX 50-series "Blackwell" hot-spot temperature monitoring, which tells you the temperature of the hottest spot on the GPU die. GPU-Z also introduces RTX 50-series memory chip temperature reading. By default, the hottest memory chip's temperature is put out, but hovering your mouse over this puts out memory temperature values for all memory chips present on your graphics card.
With GPU-Z v2.71.0, we are also introducing the "overclocking" readout in the Advanced tab for NVIDIA GPUs, letting you see OC frequencies, including for internal clock domains such as crossbar (XBAR), SYS, video clock, and identify boost locks. We are also introducing the ability to read NVIDIA SYS, and L2 cache clocks. These have to be enabled to appear in the Sensors tab, they are disabled by default. A new feature reports PCI-Express bandwidth in GB/s for NVIDIA GPUs. We've introduced a way to identify if log-to-file is disabled for a sensor: its dropdown arrow will be grayed out. Among the new GPUs supported with this release are NVIDIA RTX 5060 (GB205), RTX 4070 10 GB, RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server, H100 PCIe variant, Tesla V100-SXM2-16 GB variant, P102-101; AMD Steam Machine GPU and Radeon PRO V710 (second variant); Intel Panther Lake, Lunar Lake, Arrow Lake H (285H, 265H, 255H, 235H, 225H), RPL-H Refresh (240H, 210H), Twin Lake (N355, N350, N250, N150); and Qualcomm Snapdragon X2-90, X2-85, X2-45. articles.title: RFK Jr.'s CDC isn’t letting states order COVID-19 shots for kids, blocking access
articles.text:
As respiratory virus season nears and fall vaccination drives get underway, more than half of US children are facing uncertainty over access to this year’s COVID-19 shot. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has unexpectedly delayed the distribution of the shots to a key federal program and some states.
Usually, the CDC would allow states to order the newly available seasonal COVID-19 vaccines through the federal Vaccine for Children (VFC) program, which provides vaccines at no cost to children who are uninsured, underinsured, Medicaid-eligible, or Indigenous people in the US. Approximately 52 percent of all US children are eligible for vaccines through the program.
Additionally, The Guardian reports that at least 11 states and one US territory are part of a universal vaccine purchase program, in which they buy all vaccines for children—regardless of their ability to pay or insurance status—through contracts otherwise for the VFC. The 11 states and one territory include: Alaska, Connecticut, Hawaii, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New Mexico, Rhode Island, Vermont, Washington, Wyoming, and American Samoan.
“The delay in VFC means delays in these states’ ability to get vaccine for all children,” Demetre Daskalakis, former director of the CDC’s National Center for Immunization and Respiratory Diseases and chief medical officer at Callen-Lorde Community Health Center, told The Guardian.
Kennedy’s track record
In a statement, the Department of Health and Human Services told Ars Technica that “CDC has not yet finalized procurement decisions for COVID-19 vaccines through the Vaccines for Children and Section 317 programs.” The department—currently run by ardent anti-vaccine activist Robert F. Kennedy Jr.—declined to answer the question of why there was a delay in the decision. But the statement suggested that Trump officials were questioning whether children should get the vaccine.
“HHS and CDC are committed to … ensuring that vaccines purchased through federally funded programs are appropriate for the populations those programs serve,” the department said in the statement. It added that additional information about the decision will be released “soon.”
The unexplained delay fits with Kennedy’s well-established disdain for COVID-19 vaccines, which he has falsely called “the deadliest vaccine[s] ever made,” and has actively tried to blame them for the deaths of children, despite no evidence to support the allegations.

articles.title: Alibaba claims new Qwen Image 2.1 AI model beats Google Nano Banana 2.0 with minuscule 7B parameter model — benchmarks show open-weight contender is competitive with OpenAI and Meta image models
articles.text:
Alibaba claims new Qwen Image 2.1 AI model beats Google Nano Banana 2.0 with minuscule 7B parameter model — benchmarks show open-weight contender is competitive with OpenAI and Meta image models
Open weights have once again thrown the guantlet down.
Alibaba Cloud has released a new lightweight image generation AI model, called Qwen Image 2.1. Sporting just 7 billion parameters, it's an extremely lean open-weight model, able to run on even older consumer graphics cards like the RTX 3090. Despite its lightweight design, its developers claim it is more capable than a range of closed-weight models, including Google's Nano Banana 2.0.
That is on its own internal benchmark, so we'd like to see some additional testing before making any concrete claims, but early reports suggest it's a very capable image model, with native transparency support and the ability to create unified images from a range of reference images.
One area that has raised eyebrows, though, is the change to the Qwen Image 2.1 licensing agreement. Unlike the previous version, this one explicitly forbids commercial resale of the model, requiring anyone who wants to use it for that to obtain a separate license directly from the developer.
Competing with the best?
Qwen Image 2.1 introduces a number of new features that improve its utility and help it better compete with established alternatives. It supports native transparency, so you can have it generate images with transparent backgrounds, which can make it particularly useful for artists wanting to use AI as part of something else, or for print-on-demand products like stickers.
It also improves image editing, with the ability to use up to 10 reference images. Cited examples include taking an existing image of a person, feeding the model images of clothing items, and then it can composite an image of the person wearing those clothes. The Qwen team promises consistency across images, preserving people and products effectively.
The standout feature of Qwen Image 2.1, though, is its compact size. Its visual generation component has just 7B parameters, making it one of the leanest models of its kind. In first-party comparison testing, the only model with fewer parameters was LongCat-Image developed by Meituan, coming in at 6 billion parameters. Most other models are several times that size, or closed-weight entirely.
It's those closed-weight models that Qwen Image 2.1's developers claim it can compete directly with, though. On that same internal benchmark, its model scored 60.2 on the Qwen Image Benchmark. In comparison, OpenAI'S GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst scored 67, Muse Image 62.34, and Google's Nano Banana 2.0 59.82.
Preliminary testing on AI Arena suggests it's not quite as strong as that in less favorable benchmark conditions, but still very close. There, it achieved a score of 1228, while Nano Banana 2 managed 1260. Musw Image is ranked a few steps higher again, with a score of 1276, while GPT 65 Sunburst sits at the top with a score of 1423.
On the image editing front, AI Arena claims it's now the best of the open-weight options:
These are still early results, and more testing will be needed to fully confirm or refute the Qwen team's claims, but so far they seem to track pretty closely to reality. Although we can't know how many parameters the proprietary models lean on to achieve their higher scores, Qwen Image 2.1 appears to be nipping at their heels with its modest weights.
It works well on local hardware
Reports from individual early adopters of Qwen Image 2.1 claim it runs just fine on their consumer graphics cards. Hacker News forum member Vunderba, developer of the GenAI Showdown site, claims they were able to convert a 1MP image using Qwen Image 2.1 in around five seconds on an RTX 4090.
On the Stable Diffusion subreddit, user cgs019283 praised its capabilities, stating that it could generate 1MP images in around 25 seconds on modern Nvidia 50-series graphics cards like the RTX 5070 and 5080. They did, however, state that it can take a lot longer if you use lots of reference images, and that editing an image was the slowest function of the model in their testing.
Others have the model working on older and much lighter hardware. One user claims to be using it to generate 2K resolution images in around 50 seconds using an Nvidia RTX 3060 and 64GB of memory.
One user is lucky enough to have an RTX 6000 Pro to play around with. There, the powerful hardware is able to put out 1024 x 1024 images in just a few seconds.
Although the setup and use of local AI is still a far cry from the accessibility of cloud-based platforms like Google's Nano Banana and OpenAI's GPT Image models, the early results appear, at least on the surface, to be impressive. If the feature set holds up under more rigorous testing, those wanting the kind of rapid, quality image generation but running locally with full control and no need for cloud accounts or subscriptions could make it a fierce competitor.
The licensing conundrum
Of all the commentary from Qwen Image 2.1 early adopters, a discussion that keeps coming up is how the developers are handling licensing. The wording comes across as ambiguous:
"You are granted a non-exclusive, worldwide, non-transferable, and royalty-free limited license under our intellectual property or other rights owned by us embodied in the Materials to use, reproduce, distribute, copy, create derivative works of, and make modifications to the Materials FOR NON-COMMERCIAL PURPOSES ONLY. "
It then says that anyone wanting to use those "Materials" for commercial purposes would need to acquire a license from the Qwen team specifically for that use case. It's caused enough concern among the community that the Qwen team released a statement on Twitter/X:
That mostly seems to clear things up. Whatever you generate with the model shouldn't be classed as a licensed material, so it shouldn't be covered by this clause.
What this does mean, though, is that the model itself cannot be re-sold without a license from Alibaba. That's quite different from the Apache model the original Qwen Image was based on, and potentially stretches the definition of open-weight. It's certainly not as open as it could be.
But for most people, this is no concern. You can run Qwen Image 2.1 on your local hardware to make some pretty effective generated imagery and use them however you wish. With such a lightweight design offering such impressive capabilities, the response from closed-weight model developers will be interesting to see.
Jon Martindale is a contributing writer for Tom's Hardware. For the past 20 years, he's been writing about PC components, emerging technologies, and the latest software advances. His deep and broad journalistic experience gives him unique insights into the most exciting technology trends of today and tomorrow.

articles.title: 'El Señor de los Anillos: La caza de Gollum' brilla con el primer vistazo a Frodo y muchas nuevas imágenes
articles.text:
La esperada película de El Señor de los Anillos: La caza de Gollum tiene su rodaje en marcha de cara a un estreno que apunta a ser gigantesco en 2027. El filme será una suerte de spin-off de La Comunidad del Anillo. "Es una historia bastante intensa que transcurre después de la fiesta de cumpleaños de Bilbo y antes de las Minas de Moria", confesó hace meses la guionista y productora Philippa Boyens. Y ahora, por fin, tenemos un montón de imágenes con el primer vistazo a Frodo incluido.
El actor Elijah Wood, quien diera vida al protagonista de El Señor de los Anillos en la trilogía original de Peter Jackson, regresa como el intrépido hobbit en La caza de Gollum. Warner Bros. ya nos ha dejado por fin su primera imagen, aunque en ella no vemos el rostro de Frodo, que se encuentra de espaldas saliendo de su casa de la Comarca.
Y es que todas las imágenes de El Señor de los Anillos: La caza de Gollum compartidas por el estudio nos muestran este idílico y clásico paraje de la Tierra Media. De esta forma, en la Comarca podemos ver a un montón de hobbits con sus reconocibles vestimentas rurales. En el caso de Frodo, el personaje aparece con una gabardina marrón y un bastón en la mano.
En las imágenes de El Señor de los Anillos: La caza de Gollum también podemos ver a parte del equipo técnico de la película. La más destacable es en la que aparece Andy Serkis, actor de Gollum desde las películas originales y que ahora ejercerá también de director del filme. El cineasta asume los mandos del proyecto que espera reavivar el interés del público por la legendaria saga fantástica de J.R.R. Tolkien.
Qué sabemos de El Señor de los Anillos: La caza de Gollum
Bajo la dirección de Serkis, El Señor de los Anillos: La caza de Gollum contará con Peter Jackson como productor, asegurando la continuidad con sus dos trilogías. "Es una parte específica de una historia increíble que no ha sido contada, relatada desde la perspectiva de esta increíble criatura", comentó también Philippa Boyens acerca de la trama de la película.
El reparto de El Señor de los Anillos: La caza de Gollum lo componen Andy Serkis como Gollum, Ian McKellen como Gandalf, Elijah Wood como Frodo, Lee Pace como Thranduil, así como los nuevos rostros de Jamie Dornan como Aragorn, tomando el testigo de Viggo Mortensen; Anya Taylor-Joy como Seren, Kate Winslet como Marigol y Leo Woodall como Halvard.
Esta será la primera de dos nuevas películas de El Señor de los Anillos. Y es que después llegará El Señor de los Anillos: Shadows of the Past, una secuela de la trilogía original. El presentador del programa The Late Show, Stephen Colbert, reconocido fan acérrimo de la franquicia desde hace muchos años, es el encargado de desarrollarla junto a Peter Jackson.

articles.title: Falsche Richtung, kein Begleiter: Dieser Exoplanet gibt Forschern Rätsel auf
articles.text:
Falsche Richtung, kein Begleiter: Dieser Exoplanet gibt Forschern Rätsel auf
Der Exoplanet mit der Bezeichnung GJ 3090 b, der etwa 73 Lichtjahre entfernt ist, weist eine stark geneigte Umlaufbahn auf und bewegt sich in entgegengesetzter Richtung zur Rotation seines Muttersterns.
Dieses Phänomen ließe sich laut Space.com gut erklären, wenn GJ 3090 b einen massereichen Begleiter hätte, wie beispielsweise einen Gasriesen, einen Braunen Zwerg oder einen weiteren Stern. Doch einen solchen gibt es nicht. GJ 3090 b scheint ein Einzelgänger zu sein.
GJ 3090 b weist zwei Ungewöhnlichkeiten auf
„Zu unserer großen Überraschung befindet sich der Planet GJ 3090 b nicht nur auf einer stark geneigten Umlaufbahn, sondern er bewegt sich auch retrograd, also in entgegengesetzter Richtung zur Rotation seines Sterns“, erklärte Yann Carteret, Mitglied des Teams am Astronomie-Institut der Universität Genf, in einer Pressemitteilung.
Planeten entstehen aus Gas- und Staubscheiben, die junge Sterne umgeben. Diese Materie rotiert in derselben Richtung wie der junge Zentralstern, weshalb auch die daraus entstehenden Planeten in diese Richtung rotieren sollten. Ebenso sollten die Planeten eine ähnliche Bahnebene wie ihr Mutterstern aufweisen.
GJ 3090 b verfügt über die 4,5-fache Masse der Erde
GJ 3090 b besitzt den 2,2-fachen Erdradius und die 4,5-fache Masse unseres Planeten und wird daher als „Sub-Neptun“ klassifiziert. Sub-Neptune gehören zu den häufigsten Planeten in der Milchstraße. Doch als das Team diesen Himmelskörper am La-Silla-Observatorium in Chile untersuchte, zeigte der Exoplanet eine Besonderheit, die alles andere als alltäglich ist: einen Psi-Winkel von 136 Grad. Zum Vergleich: Der Psi-Wert der Erde beträgt 7 Grad.
Als „Psi“ wird der Unterschied in der Ausrichtung zwischen der Bahnebene des Sterns und der seiner Planeten bezeichnet. Dieser Unterschied entsteht durch Störungen während der Phase der Planetenbildung. „Die Messung des Winkels Psi liefert Hinweise auf die Entstehung und Entwicklung von Planetensystemen. Daher ist es für uns nur logisch, diesen Wert auch bei anderen Planetensystemen zu bestimmen“, so Carteret.
Wissenschaftler:innen „müssen nun andere Hypothesen prüfen“
Das untersuchte Planetensystem ist eines von nur fünf bisher entdeckten Systemen mit einem Psi-Wert von mehr als 70 Grad – doch der entscheidende Unterschied liegt darin, dass die anderen Systeme jeweils ein massereiches Objekt aufweisen, das offensichtlich für die extrem schiefen Umlaufbahnen verantwortlich ist.
„Da es keinen massereichen Begleiter gibt, der diese ungewöhnliche Umlaufbahn erklären könnte, müssen wir nun andere Hypothesen prüfen“, sagte Vincent Bourrier von der Universität Genf, dessen Forschungsergebnisse wie die des gesamten Teams in der Fachzeitschrift Astronomy & Astrophysics veröffentlicht wurden. GJ 3090 b wird die Wissenschaftler:innen also weiter beschäftigen.

articles.title: Toronto startup SmartARM uses Meta AI glasses to help 'see' objects
articles.text:
Toronto-based robotics startup SmartArm is using AI hardware to help its prosthetic arm grab objects more easily.
SmartArm, which gained recognition for winning Microsoft’s Imagine Cup in 2018, uses self-built AI software and hardware from Meta to let the limb “see” the object and adjust to make grabbing it easier.
It does this using an onboard camera built into the palm that streams video to the operating system, which SmartARM calls Dexterity OS. It identifies the object and automatically selects the optimal grip. From there, the multi-articulating fingers move to grab the object, applying the right pressure for each individual object.
The SmartARM also uses three pieces of Meta technology: the Meta AI glasses, the DINOv2 open-source vision model, and the Meta Wearables Device Access Toolkit. SmartARM’s founder, Hamayal Choudry, noted that the Meta AI glasses let the arm see more of its environment than the palm camera alone. With DINOv2, users can train new objects by taking a few photos in the SmartARM app, and the software identifies similarities and determines the best grip. This means that it allows the arm to grip and pick up objects based directly on visual feature reading, and without needing prior understanding or traditional programming.
The toolkit allows SmartARM to extend and improve object recognition and understanding, which will provide more data from the egocentric point of view that the glasses offer. According to SmartARM’s website, the device currently recognizes over 365 everyday objects, with the library “constantly growing” through over-the-air updates. SmartARM also notes that the more you use the arm, the more objects get added to your personal recognition profile.
Although no device specs are listed yet, SmartARM notes an expected battery life of 12-16 hours, depending on activity level.
Pricing also hasn’t been released, but the company is actively working with insurers and health systems to establish coverage options. The device is currently in beta in Canada, and if you want one, you can join the company’s waitlist for updates and early access to pricing, specs, and more.

articles.title: Modal Motors is trying to cut China out of electric motors entirely | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Lately, it seems like everyone is talking about bringing manufacturing back to the United States, especially when it comes to hard tech like drones and robotics. Michael Van Steenburg thinks he’s ahead of the game.
Van Steenburg spent the last decade building all kinds of electric motors in the U.S. and North America, and now he wants to do it again with his new startup, Modal Motors. This time, he wants to ditch rare-earth magnets entirely, in a bid to further separate the U.S. from China’s supply chain.
As one of the founders in Startup Battlefield 200 who will compete at TechCrunch Disrupt next month, he thinks it’s an urgent pitch to make.
“China’s already flexed its muscles a couple times,” Van Steenburg said, referring to the country restricting access to rare-earth products.
There are other companies working on setting up electric motor manufacturing and supply chains in the U.S., but Van Steenburg argues they’re doing it the wrong way by continuing to rely on rare-earth magnets. Domestic supply of those materials is still years away, he said.
“Other people are ‘reshoring,’ [but] they’re basically knocking off Chinese motors and just doing it in the U.S. But they’re hoping that the U.S. rare-earth magnet system is going to get up to speed fast enough,” he said. “It’s going to still be a while longer before they can actually replace China.”
Modal Motors has two products that it’s developing ahead of Disrupt. One is a small electric motor meant for drones that can also work in fans, blowers, and even actuators. It’s designed to “minimize mass while delivering maximum torque density and efficiency,” according to the startup’s website.
The more radical design is what Modal refers to as the “Hybrid Enigma Drive,” a planar — or flat — electric motor that can fit in lower-profile spaces.
Van Steenburg is drawing on decades of experience in the automotive industry to develop these motors and get them customer-ready. But there’s also an irony in the work Van Steenburg is doing to make Modal Motors’ products a China-free option; in the late 1990s, he worked on a hybrid gas-electric drivetrain that China wanted to put in its so-called “People’s Car.”
“It’s kind of comical,” he said, thinking back on that experience and how much the world has changed. What hasn’t changed, he said, is his outsider streak and strong conviction about doing things that are hard.
“I always tell people that the clock started ticking 25 years ago, and in that whole time, I’ve watched a slow-motion train wreck as China’s been going around the world, grabbing mines, grabbing mineral rights, doing all these things, and slowly but surely monopolizing the entire rare-earth supply chain,” he said.

articles.title: FBI rushes to investigate if ShinyHunters hack of thousands of employees is real
articles.text:
The FBI is now investigating claims from a hacker group that thousands of current and former employees’ personal data was stolen after the group exploited a previously unknown bug found on an agency jobs website.
On Tuesday, 404 Media reported that ShinyHunters took down the agency site, FBIJobs.gov, then posted a banner on the homepage that said “THIS SITE HAS BEEN SEIZED BY SHINYHUNTERS.”
About two to three terabytes of data were taken, ShinyHunters told The New York Times. None of the data has been leaked yet, but it included “names of current and former agents as well as applicants and corresponding home addresses, phone numbers, names of spouses, certain medical information, and other data.” According to Bloomberg, the data could be used to potentially retaliate against agents, with one sample appearing to include “potentially sensitive professional information on the FBI employees’ work focus such as counter-intelligence work on China, Russia and Iran, as well as work against street gangs.”
The group’s motive was not to extort the FBI or seek a ransom, it claimed. Instead, the strike was meant to force the FBI to either remove or edit a May advisory warning about ShinyHunters that the group said circulated “disinformation in an attempt to ‘disrupt’ our operations.”
In a message posted on the dark web that was reviewed by Ars, ShinyHunters said it was “severely offended” that the FBI alleged that they sometimes use “exaggerated claims” to extract payments from victims. “We wish to state unequivocally our threats and claims are very real,” the group said. “Not exaggerated and never a bluff.”
ShinyHunters was also upset that the FBI claimed the group conducts swatting attacks against corporate workers and makes sextortion threats. That “never” happens, ShinyHunters said.

articles.title: How founders are rethinking capital in the AI era | BetaKit
articles.text:
AI is giving early-stage founders more room to experiment before raising significant amounts of capital, and this is changing how entrepreneurs think about when to raise and where that money gets deployed.
“What has become possible with a small team of really good people is phenomenal.”
George Babu, Aire Labs
George Babu is taking a more deliberate fundraising approach to his latest venture, Toronto-based Aire Labs. In 2007, he joined David Stein and Daniel Debow to co-found Toronto-based performance management company Rypple, which was acquired by Salesforce in 2011. He later co-founded San Francisco and Toronto based robotics firm Kindred Systems before it was acquired by the Ocado Group in 2020.
When he built Kindred, the company raised substantial capital early, which Babu said created room for mistakes. With Aire Labs, he is focused on keeping the company lean while it experiments.
“You can take very little capital, have a lot of control, and do a lot of experiments until you feel confident, and then you take a lot of capital,” Babu said on a recent episode of The Gradient Ascent Podcast.
The episode, hosted by CIBC Innovation Banking Executive Managing Director Paul McKinlay and CIBC Capital Markets Managing Director Daniel Lee, featured Babu and Gideon Hayden, Co-Founder and Managing Partner at Leaders Fund.
The conversation explored a changing funding calculus for tech companies as AI raises investor expectations, expands what small teams can accomplish, and shifts where startups allocate their spending.
Capital follows conviction
At project development platform Aire Labs, AI has already helped Babu’s team run more experiments without having to add headcount. The company has accumulated hundreds of transcripts from customer discovery calls that can be searched and analyzed when the team is considering building a new feature. AI tools also allow Aire Labs to customize and test messaging for particular customers and market segments, without the need for a 40-person team.
“What has become possible with a small team of really good people is phenomenal,” Babu said. “I can run way more experiments on much less capital, until I find that thing that then can be venture-fuelled. And you can keep doing that again and again and again, and ultimately that’s how you build an enduring company. You just keep making these bets.”
Babu pointed to Shopify’s early development as an example, noting the company did not take much capital in its early days because the market didn’t have conviction that another e-commerce company was needed at the time.
“They were very lean,” Babu said of Shopify. “They had to build their culture, build their processes, find where the real product-market fit was, and then they could raise a ton of money and go and just dominate the market.”
Staying lean early has become particularly important as expectations for venture-backed startups have skyrocketed. Babu noted that the bar for Seed and Series A startups is considerably higher compared to a few years ago, and raising a larger round creates an expectation that the money will be put to work quickly.
“If you’re going to take a lot of money, you better go fast and very far,” Babu added. “I don’t think it changes that you still need a lot of capital to build an enduring company.”
What a round buys
None of this means that AI has made building a successful company cheap, according to Hayden. “We have not seen the cost of building come down at all. If anything, it’s gone up,” he said.
His firm, which invests primarily at the seed and Series A stages across enterprise software, cybersecurity, and AI-native infrastructure, has seen a change in the composition of startup spending. He explained that many R&D-heavy teams plan to add employees at a slower pace because existing engineers can do more in less time with the help of AI tools. He has seen budgets increasingly account for both engineers and the token or compute spending required to equip those employees.
“What these tools effectively allow you to do is buy time,” Hayden said, noting that AI can give a company the capacity of many engineers working simultaneously, which compresses the time it takes to pursue an opportunity.
McKinlay noted that product development is only one part of a company’s cost base, and that reaching and retaining customers remains the most expensive part of company building. Babu estimated that a company may end up spending 30 percent of the budget on R&D and 70 percent on go-to-market, sales, and marketing, which makes the application of AI in the latter functions of the business particularly important to him.
AI also introduces a new variable into startup spending: model costs can be difficult to predict. “Part of enterprise buying enterprise software as a subscription is [that] you have some predictability to what that line item is,” McKinlay said. “AI can throw a wrench in that to some extent.”
While he expects the cost of AI tools to get cheaper in time, Babu has already seen Aire Labs’ bills rise enough in the short term to accelerate plans for multi-model workflows. His company has made its own architecture model-agnostic, which allows it to switch between providers if prices change.
“Right now, everyone’s exploring and no one minds the bills, but once you operationalize something, you don’t want to pay that bill,” Babu said. “The vendors that optimize [for model costs] from the beginning are going to be in a better position than those that don’t.”
At the seed and Series A stages, Leaders Fund places relatively little emphasis on a company’s margin profile, though the firm does need to believe the business can eventually produce sustainable unit economics.
The more immediate concern is whether the company is creating products customers find sufficiently valuable. Hayden expects this test to become more important as the enthusiasm around AI adoption matures. He sees many businesses currently buying AI products because of pressure to demonstrate that they have an AI strategy. Hayden expects that buying frenzy to eventually subside.
“There’s going to be this rationalization period that will come,” Hayden said, “when companies are going to say, ‘OK, this is cool, but is this actually delivering value?’”
Building the capital flywheel
The changing economics of company building also raises questions about whether Canadian founders can access the early capital required to fuel the experimentation stage. Research from Leaders Fund found that from 2015 to 2020, roughly 75 percent of Canadian-founded startups were started in Canada. But in 2024, nearly half of Canadian founders who had raised over $1 million were based in the United States.
Hayden, who presented his firm’s research in the House of Commons last year, has argued that Canada could encourage more early-stage investment through measures such as a long-term capital gains exemption and an angel investor tax credit. The latter, he said, would be particularly useful for companies raising their first angel round, often one of the more challenging milestones for young startups.
McKinlay said successful startup outcomes create a “flywheel effect,” as founders who build wealth in the sector reinvest it in former colleagues and new ventures.
“That’s one of the things you see in the Valley that is so powerful,” McKinlay added. “To enable that here further would be amazing.”
Creating that cycle also requires financing beyond the first cheque. As startups move from experimentation toward larger rounds and global expansion, their capital needs to evolve alongside them. CIBC Innovation Banking has spent more than 25 years providing financial advice, growth capital, and debt financing to tech companies and investors across Canada, the US, and Europe.
“Silicon Valley is a gravitational force. We’re not going to replicate that,” Hayden said. “But I think if we can create an environment for entrepreneurs that convinces more of them to build here, I think that’s healthy.”

articles.title: Managing 3D-IC Design And IP
articles.text:
Design data management, traceability, and revision control are critical for multi-chiplet heterogeneous integration.
By Keith Felton and Todd Burkholder
The trend towards multi-chiplet heterogeneous integration is here to stay. It promises faster innovation, more powerful and specialized devices, and greater design flexibility. However, realizing its potential hinges on our ability to manage the complexity that comes with it.
However, with this newfound modularity comes a significant challenge: managing the vast and intricate web of data that defines these systems. This is where robust data management and meticulous data traceability become not just beneficial, but essential. Without data management, even the most brilliant multi-chiplet design can quickly become a tangled mess, leading to costly errors, delays, and a loss of confidence in the final product.
In the first three articles of this series (published in the June, July and August editions of Semiconductor Engineering), we covered the first seven steps toward streamlining your 3D-IC design process. This article focuses on design data and design IP management, traceability, and revision control. This is a critical step for multi-chiplet heterogeneous integration, as there is so much design data and IP involved that using an incorrect version or missing an ECO can mean product failure.
Data management can be broken down to four components that will help you streamline your 3D-IC design flow:
In the world of multi-chiplet design, we often bring together various pieces of IP from different sources—from internal teams, external vendors, or even open-source initiatives. Each piece of design IP comes with its own set of design files, specifications, and usage guidelines.
When you have multiple chiplets from different sources, potentially designed with different tools and at different times, the sheer volume and diversity of this data can be overwhelming. Without a well-defined data management strategy to manage these diverse sources, the risk of introducing defects is significantly higher.
Innovator3D IC Data Management software supports robust data and design IP management to provide single moment-of-truth management of design IP data. It treats the design itself as a work-in-progress, applying a revision-controlled and access-rights managed process at every stage of design, all the way to tape out.
Fig. 1: Innovator3D IC Data Management’s centralized cockpit.
Multi-chiplet designs inherently involve a complex hierarchy. Chiplets are integrated into a larger multi-chiplet heterogeneous assembly using interposers and substrates. Managing this hierarchy effectively, especially with the inevitable design iterations, requires a powerful revision control system. When you manage your design hierarchy with revision control and history tracking, you avoid errors. Revision control is like a time machine for your designs. It allows you to track every change, revert to previous versions, and allow different teams to work on separate features or bug fixes concurrently without interfering with each other. Once a team’s work is complete and verified, their changes can be merged back into the main design.
Without this meticulous historical tracking, understanding how a design evolved, diagnosing issues, or even just knowing which version is currently “in play” becomes a monumental task. Errors can appear through miscommunication or accidental overwriting, leading to significant delays and increased costs. A well-managed design hierarchy with robust revision control is fundamental to preventing these types of errors.
In a distributed design environment, where different teams might be working on different chiplets across various locations, having a single, centralized hub for all design data is invaluable. This hub acts as the single source of truth, providing direct access to all relevant information for authorized personnel.
When engineers can quickly access information they need, cycle times are dramatically reduced. This direct access speeds up design, verification, and debugging processes, leading to faster time-to-market.
Beyond just storing data, an effective data management system provides real-time visibility into a project’s status. This capability is crucial for efficient project management, especially in the complex landscape of multi-chiplet integration.
Instant access to status tracking and analytical data empowers project managers and engineering leads to make informed decisions, proactively address issues, and ensure that the project stays on track. It transforms data from a passive record into an active tool for driving project success.
By embracing robust data management practices, including diligent management of the design and its IP sources, meticulous revision control, centralized information hubs, and comprehensive status tracking for traceability, you establish a solid foundation for success. These “unseen architects” ensure that your multi-chiplet designs are not only functional and perform well, but also are reliable, maintainable, and auditable — allowing you to build the complex, interconnected systems of tomorrow with confidence and clarity.

Todd Burkholder is a senior editor at Siemens DISW. For over 25 years, he has worked as editor, author, and ghost writer with internal and external customers to create print and digital content across a broad range of EDA technologies. Burkholder began his career in marketing for high-technology and other industries in 1992 after earning a Bachelor of Science at Portland State University and a Master of Science degree from the University of Arizona.

articles.title: La toute nouvelle montre connectée Xiaomi Redmi Watch 6 Lite connait sa première baisse de prix — Frandroid
articles.text:
Début septembre, Xiaomi a lancé en France deux nouvelles montres et un bracelet connecté : la Redmi Watch 6 Lite qui nous intéresse ici, la Redmi Watch 6 Active et le Smart Band 11 Active. La Watch 6 Lite se situe au-dessus de la Watch 6 Active (49,99 euros) et justifie ses 20 euros de plus par un écran plus grand (1,96 pouce contre 1,85) et surtout un GPS intégré. Si vous courez, marchez ou pédalez sans votre smartphone, la montre enregistre quand même votre parcours et vos performances. Les atouts de la Xiaomi Redmi Watch 6 Lite
- Son grand écran AMOLED de 1,96 pouce
- Le GPS compatible avec 5 systèmes satellitaires
