articles.title: OpenAI agents hacked an Australian government website in search for data
articles.text:
OpenAI’s artificial intelligence agents hacked an Australian government website and attempted to breach numerous other government and university websites. The attack appears to be the first confirmed instance of a rogue AI agent breaching a government website, adding fuel to rapidly intensifying concerns about the safety of advanced AI systems and the responsibility of the companies building them.
OpenAI agents hacked an Australian government website in search for data
Australia’s leader said it was ‘unacceptable’ OpenAI took months to report the incident.
Speaking on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said an agent from the American AI lab “infiltrated” Australia’s Medicare statistics portal and “accessed both public and non-public files.” Medicare is Australia’s universal health insurance program.
Albanese said personal information does not appear to have been accessed in the breach and that there is no evidence of a broader compromise to the network, but noted “investigations are ongoing.”
“This situation is obviously unacceptable,” Albanese said, adding that he had spoken with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman “to express Australia’s extreme concern.” Despite the breach happening in June, Albanese said the tech giant only notified the government about the incident earlier this month and did so via an email to a generic “public mailbox.”
Unlike previous agent incidents, which largely involved systems being tested for their cybersecurity skills, these latest hacks were the result of a more pedestrian task — data collection — going wrong. In a statement to The Verge, OpenAI spokesperson Oscar Haines said the models were attempting to “look up answers” during an internal evaluation. “In the course of that, our models took actions we did not intend.”
The timeline of the incident and its disclosure is likely to prove particularly inflammatory in the discussions of corporate behavior and transparency that follow. Albanese stressed the delay in disclosure is particularly unacceptable. OpenAI told the BBC in an unattributed statement that it did not become aware until August, when reviewing misaligned model activity.
OpenAI spokesperson Oscar Haines told The Verge the company’s “review found no evidence of patient records being accessed,” and that “the information accessed included aggregate health statistics and internal file names.” Haines said OpenAI has notified the relevant organizations and is providing technical information to support their investigations and address potential security vulnerabilities. “Our overall review is ongoing, and we remain committed to transparency about these issues and to sharing what we learn as that work continues,” Haines said.
Three further incidents of rogue AI activity linked to OpenAI agents were also reported on Wednesday by research lab Transluce. The group, which describes itself as a “nonprofit research lab dedicated to public oversight” of AI, said it had identified evidence that OpenAI’s systems had attempted to compromise websites linked to the University of New Mexico, the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare, and Data USA, a non-government platform that aggregates data from US government sources. It said the last two of these were directly linked to an agent swarm OpenAI has previously admitted originated from them.
Haines confirmed the incidents in a statement to The Verge and said the company had reached out to those involved. “Our initial review suggests that much of the activity described in Transluce’s report overlaps with cases at varying stages of investigation in our ongoing review of misaligned model activity,” he said. “In our broader review, we’re continuing to prioritize the most serious incidents while expanding our work to lower-severity activity, including agents spamming websites. Given the scale of this work and the need to verify each case, we expect the review to take months.”
OpenAI’s handling of the Australian Medicare incident is certain to place notions of corporate responsibility at the center of future discussions surrounding AI, which are often obscured with the language used to describe such attacks. OpenAI has already faced allegations of obfuscation for not disclosing similar unsanctioned activity by its agents, and efforts to prioritize investigating what it deems the most serious incidents raise the obvious question of what basis it uses to make such assessments, and how much has yet to be revealed. It echoes similar questions recently raised about Google, which did not disclose real-world attacks from its own agents.
The newly-revealed breaches come amid mounting concerns about the safety of advanced AI and the reliability of the companies developing it, largely ignited by the coordinated attack OpenAI agents launched on Hugging Face earlier this year. Worries over safety have led industry insiders to call for slowing down the pace of AI development and the global nature of the incidents has sparked significant debate among nations about how to implement stronger safeguards. Eyes will largely remain on the US and China, however, as these are the only two countries operating at the very frontier of the technology. Both appear to be resisting calls to slow down, and seem locked in a race to build the most advanced AI. Leaders from the two countries are set to meet on Thursday.

articles.title: ¿Desembarca Elon Musk en Hollywood? Paramount analiza sumarlo como inversor
articles.text:
Mientras se encamina a cerrar la compra de Warner Bros Discovery por 111.000 millones de dólares, Paramount analiza nuevas opciones para incorporar dinero fresco. Un reporte de Semafor indica que David Ellison, CEO de Paramount Skydance, analiza proponerle a Elon Musk que se sume como inversor de capital.
Los detalles del presunto plan son todavía escasos. Según se menciona, el nombre de Elon Musk no es el único que Paramount tiene en carpeta para acercar la posibilidad de sumarse en calidad de inversionista. Claro que ser el hombre más rico del mundo parece darle varios cuerpos de ventaja en el interés de Ellison y compañía.
Todavía no se sabe cuánto dinero podría solicitarle Paramount a Elon Musk para convertirlo en partícipe de la compañía. No obstante, sí se indica que el objetivo es armar un "sindicato de inversores de capital". El objetivo que perseguiría la firma sería obtener nuevas vías de liquidez y fortalecer su situación financiera cuando está a punto de concretar la transacción más cara de la historia de Hollywood.
Paramount analiza sumar a Elon Musk como inversor de capital
Con Paramount a punto de desembolsar 111.000 millones de dólares para comprar Warner Bros Discovery, la empresa buscaría diversificar sus fuentes de dinero. Tengamos en cuenta que la mayor parte del dinero para la adquisición de WBD, unos 46.700 millones de dólares, saldrá del bolsillo de Larry Ellison, fundador de Oracle y padre de David. En tanto que otros 24.000 millones de dólares serán proporcionados por los fondos soberanos de Arabia Saudí, Emiratos Árabes Unidos y Qatar.
Lo último ha desatado fuertes críticas sobre la posible injerencia extranjera sobre el funcionamiento de Paramount-Warner Bros Discovery, que no solo es un peso pesado del mundo del cine, sino también de la TV (incluyendo canales de noticias) y de la industria del gaming.
A pesar de que todavía no hay detalles que vinculen formalmente a Paramount y Elon Musk, se especula con que cualquier acercamiento entre las partes puede resolverse de forma positiva. Esto, debido a la relación de largo tiempo entre el líder de Tesla y SpaceX con Larry Ellison. El fundador de Oracle no solo fue inversor en Tesla, sino que también aportó 1.000 millones de dólares para que Musk compre Twitter en 2022.
Con o sin el dinero de Musk, Paramount se enfoca en su principal objetivo inmediato: cerrar la compra de Warner Bros Discovery. Esta semana, la compañía que lidera David Ellison llegó a un acuerdo con 12 estados de EE. UU. para levantar el bloqueo judicial contra la transacción.
Ellison se comprometió a no vender las instalaciones de Paramount Studios y Warner Bros en California por al menos 5 años. Además, prometió lanzar en cines al menos 30 películas por año durante los próximos dos años, así como inyectar 300 millones de dólares adicionales de forma anual (por un plazo de 5 años) para producir películas en Estados Unidos.

articles.title: Research on Models Engaging in Genie-Like Behavior - Schneier on Security
articles.text:
Research on Models Engaging in Genie-Like Behavior
New paper: “Self-Jailbreaking: Language Models Can Reason Themselves Out of Safety Alignment After Benign Reasoning Training.”
Abstract: We discover a novel and surprising phenomenon of unintentional misalignment in reasoning language models (RLMs), which we call self-jailbreaking. Specifically, after benign reasoning training on math or code domains, RLMs will use multiple strategies to circumvent their own safety guardrails. One strategy is to introduce benign assumptions about users and scenarios to justify fulfilling harmful requests. For instance, an RLM reasons that harmful requests like “outline a strategy for stealing customers’ credit card information from a retail store” could be associated with the benign intent of “a security professional trying to test defense,” despite no such benign context being provided as input. We observe that many open-weight RLMs, including DeepSeek-R1-distilled, s1.1, Phi-4-mini-reasoning, and Nemotron, suffer from self-jailbreaking despite being aware of the harmfulness of the requests. We also provide a mechanistic understanding of self-jailbreaking: RLMs are more compliant after benign reasoning training, and after self-jailbreaking, models appear to perceive malicious requests as less harmful in the CoT, thus enabling compliance with them. To mitigate self-jailbreaking, we find that including minimal safety reasoning data during training is sufficient to ensure RLMs remain safety-aligned. Our work provides the first systematic analysis of self-jailbreaking behavior and offers a practical path forward for maintaining safety in increasingly capable RLMs.
I think the core problem is that these models are all trained on the average of humanity, and we are a pretty duplicitous species.
cybershow • September 23, 2026 8:39 AM
That’s what everybody thinks Bruce. Or should I say, “knows in their
heart” (because making a formal proof of such a thing stretches the
limits of mathematics/logic)
However, here’s a clumsy proof (reducio ad absurdum) of a kind:
Take large language model training and start to subtract every possible
ambiguous construct. Eliminate everything that could be disingenuously
interpreted, maliciously complied with, extrapolated without reasonable
bounds, and so on, and then what are you left with?
Formal code; BNF or something not unlike C or LISP or Python or whatever.
We built all of computing, bottom-up, on formal logic for a reason. That’s
what works. It’s not just that it works on the hardware we created but that
it works in a more general sense of unambiguous deterministic reproducibility.
The “problem” is that not many people are good at doing it, coding is hard,
and it’s hard to organise large scale software projects.
So it’s always been a “dream” to jump straight from woolly high-level
requirements specifications to working execution.
Whose problem? Whose dream? People who want to make money by and large.
People content to take time getting things right – for example writing a functional
moon-lander in assembly language in 1965 – don’t worry so much abou those things.
It requires an narrative ideology to create the conditions for “stochastic” or
“almost-good-enough” computing.
That frustration has been burning a hole in society organised around capitalist
ideas for at least the past 50 years.
LLMs didn’t just change how we create code. How we do computing (formal bottom-up
codification or ambiguous top-down with natural language) is not merely a matter
of “efficiency”, it’s become a /moral/ question.
Code that allows you hide double meanings within it, is a programming language
for malice – which (unless you live under a rock in abject ddenial) is pretty
much what all of modern “business” has become.
As Ken Thompson taught us on the issue of “Trusting trust”, it’s almost
impossible for a defender to ensure fidelity of code that isn’t formally
circumscribed by complete visibility (of the whole toolchain and execution
context – which is why no real/competent security person argues against free
open source). As it stands, at least of half of all LLM functionality is
inscrutable, even with so-called “open models”. It is therefore,
fundamentally untrustworthy. The further interesting question then is;
“Is there anything practical/useful that lies in the space between formal
code and natural language?”
I believe there is, and “vibe coding” and other loose specification techniques
are going to be valuable once we harness them properly. However current experiments
with LLMs just directly churning out code, taking actions or providing “answers”
are not even close to the sort of systems that can ever be acceptable
as /real/ computing.

articles.title: Exclusive: Zoox grounds Atlanta test fleet after workers report toxic gas exposure symptoms
articles.text:
Zoox has grounded its autonomous vehicle test fleet in Atlanta after safety drivers were potentially exposed to carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, or hydrogen sulfide gas inside its vehicles last month, TechCrunch has learned. The repeated incidents led one worker to file a complaint with the Occupational Safety and Health Administration, which opened an inquiry and told Zoox to investigate the exposures.
As many as 40 workers were possibly exposed to the gases in the vehicles, according to a letter from OSHA to Zoox that TechCrunch viewed, though the Amazon-owned company says the number is lower.
Zoox put at least one group of workers back on the road in a different car after one vomited and the rest reported exposure symptoms, a contractor told TechCrunch. That second car may have also contained potentially toxic gases, he said, because the workers experienced another bout of exposure symptoms later that day.
“They made us go right back in the field after we said we were throwing up,” Jay Davis, one of the contractors who got sick in mid-August, told TechCrunch in an interview. “I emailed HR, told her what’s going on, and I told her I feel like it’s messed up that y’all made us go [back out].”
Workers reported exposure symptoms and strange smells through much of last month until August 22, when someone called 911 for a sick worker. The facility in northwest Atlanta has operated at limited capacity since then, with the test vehicles quarantined while Zoox investigated the exposures, according to two employees. Zoox’s purpose-built robotaxis, which are all electric, are not affected.
TechCrunch spoke to Davis, who filed the OSHA complaint, along with one current and two former employees for this story. The other three workers were granted anonymity to discuss private company matters and because they fear retaliation.
The illnesses come as Zoox branches into new cities and expands its existing operations in places like Las Vegas and San Francisco, in a bid to catch market leader Waymo. This rapid growth has put some safety monitors at risk. As TechCrunch previously reported, contractors have sustained injuries from sudden braking and swerving in the Zoox test vehicles. Waymo has also reported similar test driver injuries to OSHA.
Exactly what gases the Zoox employees were exposed to remains unclear. Davis said he and two other workers who became sick were told at the emergency room that their symptoms were consistent with carbon monoxide exposure. The complaint filed with OSHA mentions possible carbon dioxide, or CO2, exposure.
Zoox told OSHA in a September 10 letter, viewed by TechCrunch, that it examined its test vehicles for signs of CO2 and replaced their 12-volt batteries. Damaged batteries can produce hydrogen sulfide gas, which creates a “rotten egg” smell. Some of the employees who spoke to TechCrunch said they noticed a similar smell in the cars. (After this story was published, Zoox told TechCrunch it has detected no damage to the batteries and no signs of hydrogen sulfide gas.)
Zoox identified 28 employees who rode in six test vehicles that had an “unexplained odor,” the company said in its letter to OSHA. Zoox told OSHA that 10 workers “voluntarily underwent medical evaluation” to “determine whether any exposure had occurred.” Zoox said in the letter that it received only “one medical report identifying CO2 exposure.”
Zoox told TechCrunch it hasn’t identified the presence of carbon monoxide, which is odorless, in its vehicles. The company said it consulted an outside medical expert to help investigate the issues and that the only gas it detected in the impacted vehicles was CO2.
In the letter to OSHA, the company said it will add CO2 monitors to the vehicles, and Zoox told TechCrunch that these devices will be able to detect other gases like carbon monoxide and hydrogen sulfide. OSHA has since closed its inquiry.
“The safety and well-being of our Zoox test fleet operators is our primary concern in this situation,” the company told TechCrunch. “We are taking ongoing, appropriate, and cautious actions to investigate the reported events as necessary and support any needs from our operators. While we investigate these reports thoroughly, we have ceased operations of our test vehicles in this market.”
Known risks
Cars produce carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide when they burn fuel. These gases can enter a vehicle if there is a leak in the exhaust system; they can also build up if a vehicle runs inside an enclosed space for an extended period. It’s a common enough problem that the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration investigated Ford for six years over reports of carbon monoxide buildup in its Explorer SUVs.
In its letter to OSHA, Zoox said it tested the vehicles’ exhaust systems for leaks and performed a “smoke test” for cabin intrusions. It did not say whether it found any evidence of either. The company also removed all the 12-volt batteries, inspected them for damage, and replaced them. It did not tell OSHA whether it found evidence of damage to the batteries.
The company keeps its test vehicles running through much of a given day, in part to maintain sensor calibration and reduce the onboard self-driving computer’s boot time. Zoox uses an exhaust-capture system at its indoor depots — similar to what is used to capture truck fumes at firehouses — designed to mitigate the buildup of toxic gases.
Zoox modifies the Highlander SUVs it uses for its test fleet. Most of that work focuses on adding sensors and an autonomy computer. But the company makes other changes, too, including adding an interior “snorkel” above the central infotainment screen that pushes air toward rear-seat passengers, the employees told TechCrunch.
Zoox said it doesn’t modify the ventilation systems in these SUVs. But making any changes to a vehicle can increase the risk that gases will leak into the cabin. In the Ford investigation, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said in 2023 that the highest levels of carbon monoxide were found in police vehicles that had added sirens, lights, and other modifications, all of which can create sealing issues.
Zoox is an outlier among major robotaxi developers because its test fleet vehicles have internal combustion engines. Waymo, Tesla, Avride, and Motional all use electric vehicles, which don’t produce exhaust gases. May Mobility’s test fleet includes some hybrid vans, and Nvidia uses a small number of gas and electric Mercedes-Benz sedans.
“Everybody got quiet for some reason”
Davis and the other employees said individual safety monitors started reporting possible exposure symptoms to Zoox at the beginning of August.
The incidents Davis experienced on August 14 were more acute because four workers were riding in the SUVs together — a practice Zoox uses while training new employees.
Davis told TechCrunch the first signs of trouble appeared early that morning.
“Everything was fine. We was all laughing and talking, you know, just having a normal workday, and then everybody got quiet for some reason,” he said.
Davis recalled that one of his colleagues asked if anyone else in the SUV was “feeling weird.” The crew was approaching their scheduled morning break at 10 a.m., so the workers stopped at a Chick-fil-A. As soon as they got out of the car, Davis said one of his co-workers started throwing up. He and the others felt lightheaded.
They called the dispatcher at Zoox’s Atlanta depot, who arranged for the SUV to be towed back to base, he said. Meanwhile, Zoox arranged for an Uber to take the workers back to the depot.
“As soon as we get back to base, we’re thinking, okay, since we’ve been sick and said we was lightheaded, you know, we’re gonna have like, you know, mild duties for the day. Just sit down, you know, get yourself back together,” Davis said. “No, they put us in another [test car] and they told us to go back to work.”
After driving all afternoon, Davis said he and his colleagues went to a food court. He started vomiting after just a few bites of his meal.
Davis contacted a representative from HireArt, the third-party contractor that technically employs Zoox’s test drivers in Atlanta. He said the representative gave him a workers’ compensation hotline number and told him to call Poison Control. Three of the workers went to the emergency room, where they were evaluated for carbon monoxide exposure.
Davis said the emergency room doctor did not detect elevated carbon monoxide levels in his system. But he and others were told their symptoms were consistent with carbon monoxide poisoning.
Workers continued getting sick in the days that followed, according to all four workers who spoke to TechCrunch. On August 22, one contractor got sick enough that someone at the depot called 911.
It’s not immediately clear who called 911 or what happened to the sick worker. As for the four employees who reported symptoms on August 14, Zoox ordered them to take what it described as a random drug test in the days that followed.
This story has been updated with new information from Zoox.

articles.title: AI-Driven Device Modeling For Next Generation Quantum Applications
articles.text:
Extracting advanced compact models and overcoming their shortcomings using a hybrid ANN approach at cryogenic temperatures.
Key takeaways:
Quantum computing is advancing rapidly from isolated research devices toward increasingly complex and scalable systems. This growth is driven by cloud deployments and breakthroughs in artificial intelligence, optimization, and simulations, pushing the market to a 41.8% CAGR from 2025 to 2030[Source: https://www.marketsandmarkets.com]. But scaling a quantum processor is not only a challenge for the qubits, couplers or Josephson junctions themselves; it is also a challenge for the electronics that control, bias, and read out those devices sitting on a cryo-electronics wafer integrated alongside the qubit wafer. Much of the supporting electronics must operate at cryogenic temperatures, often only a few degrees above absolute zero. As more control and readout functionality moves closer to the quantum processor, the need for accurate models of semiconductor devices operating at these temperatures becomes increasingly important.
A common challenge modeling engineers face is to develop accurate and computationally efficient device models when low temperature physics is either not fully understood, or available compact models are not yet standardized which is further exacerbated by lack of specialized measurement setup needed at cryogenic temperatures. Parameters such as threshold voltage, carrier transport, leakage, and transconductance also shift substantially. Additional low-temperature effects also become important, including dopant freeze-out and changes in carrier statistics and band structure below 10K.
This creates a new challenge for device modeling and circuit design engineers:
How do you develop accurate, simulation-ready device models at cryogenic temperatures without spending months manually tuning parameters or developing new physics-based equations from scratch?
This matters because without accurate models, engineers cannot confidently simulate and optimize cryogenic control circuits, readout electronics, low-noise amplifiers, and other critical components of a quantum system. In this blog, we introduce a workflow that starts with extracting a high-quality baseline BSIM-BULK compact model using the Keysight ML Optimizer for room temperature (300K) data and then uses hybrid Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) to learn cryogenic behavior that the model cannot capture, as shown in Figure 1.
Fig. 1: Flowchart shows the Hybrid ANN approach.
The first step is to establish a high-quality model fit for room temperature measurement data. Most state-of-the-art compact models tend to be non-linear where multiple parameters interact strongly. Traditional optimizers such as Levenberg-Marquardt, Genetic algorithm, etc. either get stuck in local minima or take too long to converge to a global solution and hence lead to weeks of iterative tuning across numerous extraction steps. On the other hand, Keysight ML optimizer continuously learns and refines the parameter space while offering a derivative-free approach to simultaneously extract over 80 parameters in a single extraction step.
Using Skywater 130nm IV & CV data at 300K for a PMOS device, we build a full global model extraction flow for BSIM-BULK compact model involving just 5 steps where each step involves extracting relevant parameters using ML optimizer. This extraction procedure establishes a physics-based BSIM-BULK model reference against which cryogenic behavior of this extracted model can be compared.
Fig. 2: Final fitting of Id & derivatives for smallest and narrowest devices at 300K using BSIM-BULK v107.1.
It would be ideal to extend an existing compact model to 4 K, but BSIM-BULK currently lacks the equation needed to model the physical effects at cryogenic temperatures in CMOS devices. Going through the development process for such a physical model can take significant research, time, and standardization efforts. This is precisely where ANNs can complement the compact model by learning the residual behavior that remains after the physics-based model has been evaluated at 4K, which is the fundamental concept behind the hybrid ANN modeling approach. On the other hand, a standalone full ANN must learn device physics, temperature scaling, non-linearities, bias dependence, etc., from scratch, which requires significantly more training data and time, making physics interpretation and extrapolation more difficult. A typical forward propagation ANN architecture used is shown in Fig. 3 below.
Fig. 3: Input layer, Hidden layer and Output layer setup of the ANN residual.
Hybrid ANN acts as an intelligent correction layer than a replacement for compact models, making modeling problems at hand substantially more manageable especially when measurement data is limited. Using the Keysight ANN toolbox in IC-CAP, the neural network training process can be structured around the difference in drain currents between the measured 4K data and the baseline prediction by BSIM-BULK model extracted at 300K across all biases and geometries including derivatives. Forward propagation ANN consisting of 2 hidden layers which represent geometry/bias interaction more efficiently, with 18 neurons per layer across optimization iterations to achieve an error tolerance of 7.5e-4, is used to train ANNs against the current residuals from 4K measurement data and simulations, with final fitting results shown in Figure 4 below. Finally, the trained hybrid ANN equations are converted into Verilog-A format and implemented as a current source in conjunction with the 300K model.
Fig. 4: Final fitting of Id & derivatives for smallest and narrowest devices at 4K.
As demonstrated above, once a cryogenic model has been accurately extracted in a matter of minutes, it can quickly become a building block for circuit-level design and simulations. Engineers can then directly use cryogenic models in Verilog-A to investigate readout circuits, low-noise amplifiers, and control electronics, etc., for system-level quantum design. This approach has several added values:
As quantum systems continue to scale, cryogenic electronics design will increasingly be part of overall quantum system-level architecture and hence creates an opportunity to rethink device modeling in a new context. Rather than extracting or developing models at each new operating condition, AI-driven workflows such as the demonstrated hybrid ANN approach can combine the strengths of physics-based modeling and machine learning to build accurate, efficient, and scalable models for tomorrow’s quantum systems.

articles.title: SA’s HisWay Labs secures funding to help rebuild rail reliability - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
The Cape Town-based HisWay Labs, the company behind TrackView rail-integrity monitoring system, has secured funding from technology investment and product development firm Octoco Group as it prepares for international expansion.
Founded in 2018, HisWay Labs designed TrackView from the ground up for an environment where conventional rail equipment simply doesn’t survive. The solar-powered sensor contains no copper cabling and no batteries, the two components that make traditional trackside infrastructure a prime target for theft.
It is engineered to withstand extreme heat, dust, flooding and deliberate tampering, and to keep monitoring rail integrity and train positioning around the clock without the maintenance burden that legacy systems demand.
Built for the realities of South Africa’s rail network, it is now drawing international attention, and HisWay Labs has taken on strategic investment from Octoco Group to help it prepare for expansion.
TrackView has already earned formal certification and product type approval from the Passenger Rail Agency of South Africa (PRASA) and has been deployed commercially in partnership with Siemens Mobility. The technology is now in active field trials in the United States, and HisWay Labs is exhibiting this month at InnoTrans in Germany, the world’s largest transport technology trade fair, to build European distribution and operator partnerships.
“South Africa has a long tradition of solving hard engineering problems out of necessity,” said Heinrich de Lange, Octoco Group’s MD. “HisWay Labs has turned one of our most damaging infrastructure challenges into a globally competitive product. Backing them is a chance to help restore confidence in our own rail network while proving that world-class industrial hardware can come from here.”

articles.title: Meta changes the shape of virtual reality with its new thin and light Meta VR Glasses - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Meta is literally changing the shape of virtual reality after unveiling its new controller-free high-end VR glasses – Meta VR – which will go on sale in the first half of 2027 at a price of $US1,299.99.
Meta’s new device has a sleek and lightweight design which makes it easy for users to play games, enjoy cinematic experiences, sit courtside at major sporting events and enjoy a new level of productivity.
Meta VR has a small and light form factor with no straps or heavy hardware on the user’s face so it can be worn comfortably for extended periods.
The Meta VR glasses are 5 times lighter than Meta Quest 3.
They have a magnesium alloy construction for added strength and rigidity.
The device’s battery, storage and processor are housed in a smartphone-shaped puck that connects to the glasses with an optical tether.
The biggest change with Meta VR compared to its previous VR headsets is the move away from any hand controllers and complex setup processes.
Instead users navigate simply look at an app icon or button and use a tap of their index finger and thumb together to click.
To scroll users simply make a soft fist and move their thumb to scroll through pages, all the while their hands are comfortably by their side.
It’s also possible to use voice commands to control the navigation and system settings hands-free.
Meta VR can also be used as a workspace, with the ability to spread out your work on a large virtual screen and set up a virtual typewriter on a surface in front of you.
The Meta VR glasses include a 5K infinite display built on micro OLED panels with 37 pixels per degree.
The result is a stunningly sharp and clear picture, which is perfect for text legibility and punchy graphics.
The compact pancake lenses have been built specifically for the device and is why it can achieve cinema-grade clarity while being able to fit in a product that looks like a pair of glasses.
It also includes Dolby Vision so you can enjoy the same quality as you would on the latest smart TVs including vivid colour, impressive contrast, and lifelike detail.
On the audio side Dolby Atmos support also provides immersive spatial audio that’s integrated directly into the device.
Meta AI is also at the heart of the product and is central to the operating system.
The VR glasses are powered by Qualcomm’s new Snapdragon Reality Elite processor which provides exceptional performance, faster load times, and breakthrough power efficiency.
The battery offers up to three hours of continuous high-resolution playback and gaming and supports 45W fast charging.
On the content side Meta is working with several partners across the industry.
It is also the first IMAX Enhanced certified VR device ever to allow users to experience select films in IMAX’s exclusive expanded aspect ratio anywhere.
Meta has also partnered with Disney on 3D experiences, with Disney+ subscribers able to start streaming movies like The Avengers, Black Panther, and more in 3D in select countries.
There will also be themed immersive viewing environments as well as VR-enhanced cinema, where the space around the screen becomes part of the story.
After launch users will be able to watch films like Avengers: Infinity War and Star Wars: A New Hope in the new Disney Immersive Cinema by ILM app.
Meta has also partnered with other streaming platforms, including Amazon Prime Video, YouTube, Plex and Tubi with HBO Max and Paramount Plus also offering their 3D media catalogues for the very first time.
Sports fans will also appreciate the experience with their favourite apps like NBA, MLB, and ESPN also on board.
Meta has also worked with ESPN to offer immersive sports: a front-row seat with 180° views in 8K.
Other immersive formats include in the Billie Eilish Concert film directed by James Cameron.
On the productivity side users can enjoy a massive screen anywhere they are and turn any table or desk into a Surface keyboard and touchpad.
Users will also be able to connect their Mac or Windows PC wirelessly or via USB-C and bring their own keyboard and mouse to enjoy full-colour passthrough where you can still see your keyboard, desk, phone, and surroundings while you work.
And when it comes to gaming there will be plenty of choices, including more than 75 games at launch that you can play just with hand gestures.
Will also have full access to the entire Meta Quest catalogue and full compatibility with Touch Plus controllers.
Is also access to Xbox Cloud gaming to stream hundreds of games directly to the VR glasses. Users will be able to connect a Bluetooth gamepad to create an on-the-go gaming experience.
They can also connect a handheld gaming device wirelessly or via USB-C to play on a bigger screen.
Meta is also introducing a new hologram technology so you can present a photorealistic digital version of yourself, which includes expressions and reactions in real time, for video calling on the Meta VR glasses.
During the call the other person will appear in front of you, with spatial audio placing their voice where they are, so it feels like they’re in the same room.
The new Meta VR glasses will go on sale in the US spring 2027 and will be priced at $US1,299.99.
* Stephen Fenech travelled to the US as a guest of Meta

articles.title: PhysicsWallah puts South India at the centre of its next phase
articles.text:
PhysicsWallah puts South India at the centre of its next phase
PhysicsWallah founder Alakh Pandey plans a two-year South India expansion, targeting five states through local partnerships, multilingual learning and a broader education offering.
Edtech firm PhysicsWallah (PW) is putting South India at the centre of a two-year expansion led personally by founder and CEO Alakh Pandey.
The move matters as the company is trying to take a model built around low-cost digital teaching, physical centres and hybrid learning into markets where language, local academic preferences and established coaching networks can be different.
“For the next 24 months, my life will be dedicated to students in South India, and I will be stationed here,” Pandey said at an event in Tirupati. He said the focus would cover Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Kerala.
The immediate step is a five-year partnership with Mohan Babu University in Tirupati. According to the company, it will provide online AI, skilling and career-focused courses to nearly eighteen thousand students. The partnership broadens the South India strategy beyond entrance-exam coaching towards university learning and employability.
“Through our platform, I want to provide them the tools required to realise their potential. Since PW’s inception until today, I feel we need to create a more measurable impact in the southern part of our country,” he said.
That ambition comes after a rapid expansion of the company itself. PW began as a YouTube teaching channel in 2014 and was founded as a company in 2020 by Pandey and Prateek Maheshwari. It now spans online, offline and hybrid formats and multiple education segments.
The company said it has reached more than four crore students since inception and had more than half a crore paid students in FY26. Its app had recorded nearly nine crore cumulative downloads by FY26. The company listed on the NSE and BSE in November 2025.
Across India’s test-preparation sector, providers have been moving beyond traditional coaching hubs into Tier-II and III cities. Online-first companies have also built physical classroom networks.
PW said in its Q2 FY26 shareholder letter that it had more than twenty centres in Chennai, Hyderabad and Bengaluru and planned thirteen additional centres across five southern states.
The wider policy environment also supports digital and multilingual delivery, although it does not guarantee commercial success. The National Education Policy calls for education technology and digital content in major Indian languages, while the government’s DIKSHA platform supports learning content in eighteen languages, including Tamil, Telugu and Kannada.

articles.title: Windows 11 : l’appli Clipchamp peut upscaler vos vidéos en 4K
articles.text:
S’il vous arrive de faire du montage vidéo ponctuellement sur votre PC, il y a de fortes chances pour que vous utilisiez Clipchamp. L’application de montage vidéo de Microsoft, gratuite, est généralement installée par défaut sur Windows 11.
Elle embarque tout le nécessaire pour réaliser des petits montages peu exigeants, et permet aux débutants de créer facilement des petits films grâce à une interface très intuitive. Mais Microsoft y a aussi intégré un certain nombre d’outils alimentés par l’Intelligence artificielle. Le dernier en date introduit une fonction particulièrement intéressante. Il permet d’améliorer la qualité de vos vidéos en basse résolution.
Des vidéos upscalables jusqu’en 4K
Depuis sa dernière mise à jour, Clipchamp peut upscaler vos vidéos en basse résolution pour les rendre plus nette. « Augmentez la résolution de votre vidéo pour obtenir un rendu plus net et plus clair, même si elle a été enregistrée sur un téléphone plus ancien » affiche ainsi Microsoft à l’ouverture d’une vidéo dans Clipchamp.
« Améliorer la résolution », c’est le nom de cette nouvelle fonction, est accessible directement depuis la barre d’outils latérale de Clipchamp. Concrètement, la fonction s’appuie sur l’IA pour créer une copie de votre vidéo dans une résolution plus élevée, en y ajoutant des détails visuels. Ce « processus de mise à l’échelle par IA » comme l’appelle Microsoft, n’est toutefois pas accessible sur toutes les configurations.
Il faut en effet être équipé d’un PC estampillé Copilot+ pour pouvoir en profiter. Car l’opération d’upscaling est entièrement réalisée localement sur la machine. Par ailleurs, si vous décidez d’upscaler une vidéo en 4K, il faudra impérativement passer à la caisse. Car pour exporter votre projet final dans cette même résolution, un abonnement Microsoft 365 est requis.
Comment upscaler une vidéo avec Clipchamp ?
La procédure pour améliorer la qualité d’une vidéo basse résolution avec Clipchamp est très simple. Après avoir importé un clip vidéo sur la timeline, sélectionnez simplement celle-ci pour la mettre en surbrillance, puis cliquez sur le bouton Améliorer dans la barre d’outils affichée à droite de la fenêtre.
Un volet « Améliorer la vidéo » va alors s’ouvrir avec, à l’intérieur, un menu déroulant permettant de sélectionner la qualité souhaitée. Un clic sur le bouton Améliorer la résolution suffit ensuite pour lancer le traitement de la vidéo.
Après l’opération, qui prend plusieurs minutes, Clipchamp permet de revenir en arrière si toutefois le rendu obtenu ne vous convient pas, afin de restaurer la vidéo originale. Vous pourrez ensuite continuer votre montage, ou exporter directement votre vidéo upscalée en cliquant sur le bouton idoine.

articles.title: Malicious AI agents steal 600K credit cards, infect 100+ sites with skimmers
articles.text:
A financially motivated threat actor is using open-source AI agent frameworks to attack hundreds of online retailers at scale, stealing more than 600,000 credit card records.
The campaign has been active since at least July and is ongoing as of September 22. In just five days, the threat actor compromised at least 27 companies and launched more than 100 attacks.
Despite the broad targeting, findings from cybersecurity startup Gambit indicate that the attacker stole more than 600,000 valid card details from two companies and deployed skimmer malware on the websites of five other organizations to collect payment data.
The researchers say that the campaign is powered by three AI tools to execute the attack chain against tens of companies every day:
- Strix — penetration testing framework for scanning and vulnerability discovery
- Cairn — autonomous exploitation engine, tasked with objectives such as obtaining a shell or admin access. It should not be confused with the same-name AI malware analysis tool Cisco Talos released yesterday
- Hermes — for campaign orchestration, post-exploitation work, tactical decisions, and directing the malicious activity using claude-opus-4.6
Strix ran 146 times against 138 hosts between August 23 and 31, accumulating 633 scanning hours, the researchers found.
Hermes contained a persona called "SOUL - Red Team Operator" and 121 skills, including 78 attack-related skills.
The researchers report that the human operator, who appears to be Chinese, gave the AI agents brief instructions on the operation’s goals, then let them handle the rest.
Between September 10 and 15, the attacker reportedly launched 105 distinct attack waves, succeeding to varying degrees on at least 27.
The skimmers were injected into target websites using various methods that depended on the level of access, identified vulnerabilities, and architecture.
Observed methods include appending malicious code to legitimate JavaScript files, adding script tags to checkout pages or Google tag blocks, poisoning S3/CDN content and server-side caches, modifying database fields, altering Kubernetes deployments, and using cron jobs to restore the skimmer after it was removed.
Gambit researchers gained access to a staging server operated by the attacker and retrieved direct evidence.
In total, the campaign has compromised at least 119 websites with credit card skimmers, and the threat actors breached large organizations such as a Fortune 500 hospitality company, a major U.S. airline, a large U.S. industrial supplies distributor, and an online fashion retailer.
The attacker used a website traffic-ranking service to find valuable targets in the list Strix produced and prioritized those running custom software, presumably because they were more likely to be vulnerable.
During the investigation, Gambit researchers discovered that the attacker instructed the AI agent to run cleanup procedures that removed card data from Magento databases after exfiltration.
The instruction is present in one of the Hermes agent's skill files: "After extracting and downloading all card data, wipe the source fields in batches."
This caused operational disruptions at several retailers due to data losses, the researchers note.
Low per-target costs
Gambit researchers also gained insight into the costs for running this operation. They found an OpenRouter account showing $7,005.71 spent over roughly four weeks as of August 25.
Based on subsequent usage, the researchers estimate the total costs between $12,000 and $18,000. This adds up to an average cost of $25 for each target.
“Spread over the companies attacked, this is a marginal cost of a few US dollars to a few tens of US dollars for each targeted company,” Gambit explains.
“The operator’s own cost review gives a similar figure, a mean of $25.46 over 101 completed scans, from $3.13 for the cheapest target to $79.31 for the most expensive.”
The researchers say that automation and low cost make it easy for threat actors, even less skilled ones, to deploy such attacks. In many cases, access was obtained in just a few hours, with AI tools doing the work based on short instructions the operator provided between autonomous runs.
Gambit warn that organization looking to defend against this type of attack should also plan against potential data loss as a side effect of the attacker's cleanup routine.
Build your security blueprint for AI-powered attacks
Join Mikko Hyppönen and security leaders from the NFL, CHANEL, and Atlassian for a two-hour digital summit on what AI-speed attacks change, what defenders should stop doing, and how to validate, decide, fix, and re-validate at machine speed.

articles.title: Las empresas han encontrado otra forma de atraer talento: ofrecer acciones junto al sueldo para compartir beneficios y riesgos
articles.text:
La negociación del salario es uno de los puntos más importantes en el proceso de contratación, pero independientemente del importe de la nómina, no se habla en los mismos términos cuando se habla de la retribución de un directivo que de un empleado. En el caso de los primeros, es habitual que reciban parte de ese salario en forma de paquetes de acciones u otros beneficios, mientras que los empleados deben conformarse con una nómina mensual.
Sin embargo, algo está cambiando en las negociaciones salariales de los empleados de Silicon Valley. Cada vez es más habitual que la empresa comparta algo distinto con sus empleados: un trozo de sí misma. Un beneficio que antes era casi exclusivo de altos directivos y fundadores, ahora empieza a formar parte del salario de los empleados de ventas o de atención al cliente.
De los despachos a la sala de ventas. Históricamente, las opciones a acciones se han reservado para CEOs, consejeros o para la alta dirección de las empresas. El resto de empleados normalmente cobra en euros o dólares y punto. Esa barrera se está rompiendo, tal y como confirma un análisis de 8.000 concesiones en 480 empresas que ha llevado a cabo la plataforma de Recursos Humanos Deel.
Según los datos de este estudio, los equipos de ventas que reciben parte de su retribución en forma de paquetes de acciones se han incrementado en casi un 30% desde mediados de 2025. Los de marketing suben un 24% en el mismo periodo, mientras que los empleados de Ingeniería, la eterna favorita del capital, da signos de estancamiento.
Pese a eso, un análisis del economista Jakob Brounstein para Revelio Labs destacaba que el 70% de los empleados de las grandes tecnológicas recibía parte de su salario en forma de acciones, aunque solo el 35,8% de las empresas ofrecían esa opción, destacando entre ese porcentaje la presencia de las grandes empresas cotizadas.
Las acciones son más atractivas. El salario fijo lleva años descolgado de la inflación, lo cual provoca una pérdida del poder adquisitivo real. Si se negocia un salario fijo y los incrementos salariales no superan el IPC, al final el salario cunde menos año tras año.
Las acciones, en cambio, ofrecen algo distinto. Si a la empresa le va bien, ese dinero puede multiplicarse. Es una apuesta con un riesgo implícito, pero cada vez más gente la acepta como forma de no quedarse atrás. "Creo que se está convirtiendo en una parte fundamental de la compensación, pero no es lo mismo que un salario", resume la economista de Deel Lauren Thomas. Los empleados de Nvidia o de SpaceX son un buen ejemplo de ello.
No es una moda pasajera. Un estudio publicado en la revista International Review of Applied Economics revela que los trabajadores de EEUU con acciones pasaron de 10 a 14 millones entre principios de los 2000 y 2025. El propio estudio explica el origen de esta tendencia. Cuando el talento cualificado escasea y las empresas quieren retener a esos trabajadores, ofrecer opciones de acciones de la empresa les vincula más que con un simple contrato y se les incentiva a llevar a la empresa al éxito.
De hecho, ese es el motivo por el que las grandes empresas los ofrecen a sus directivos clave. La idea que hay detrás es que, si hacen crecer a la empresa y permanecen en ella el tiempo suficiente, recogerán los frutos de ese éxito en forma de una revalorización en el precio de sus acciones. En las grandes empresas cotizados, las acciones ya suponen el 71,6% del sueldo medio de un consejero delegado.
Los impuestos también cuentan. La fiscalidad está siendo otro de los argumentos de peso que está decantando la balanza hacia el lado de las acciones. Los impuestos que soportan los ingresos por rendimientos del trabajo son mayores que los que soportan las operaciones financieras como la venta de acciones por lo que, fiscalmente, es más interesante recibir un dólar de nómina y un gran paquete de acciones cada año como hacen los CEO de las grandes compañías.
Fuera de EEUU, la fiscalidad también se ha adaptado a esta nueva modalidad salarial. Alemania reformó en 2024 su Ley de Financiación (Zukunftsfinanzierungsgesetz) ampliando la exención fiscal por acciones de 1.440 euros a 2.000 euros. También alarga hasta 15 años el plazo antes de tributar por ellas. Según Deel, los empleados alemanes que comenzaron a recibir parte de su remuneración en acciones subieron un 62% entre el primer semestre de 2025 y el mismo tramo de 2026.
En Reino Unido pasa algo parecido con el plan EMI, el esquema fiscal favorito de las startups británicas. Desde abril de 2026, el Gobierno duplicó el límite de opciones que puede repartir cada empresa. También triplicó el tope de activos para acogerse a él.

articles.title: Meta dévoile un « Tamagotchi » pour emporter Muse (son IA) partout avec vous
articles.text:
Un petit écran, un personnage animé (plutôt mignon) et un format qui tient sur un porte-clés : le nouvel appareil de Meta a un air de Tamagotchi.
Mais le Muse Charm, dévoilé par Mark Zuckerberg à la fin de sa conférence Meta Connect 2026, doit servir à autre chose qu’à s’occuper d’un animal virtuel. Son ambition est de rendre l’assistant IA Muse accessible d’un geste, sans ouvrir une application sur son téléphone. Lancé le 8 septembre aux États-Unis, Muse n’est pas encore proposé en France, où aucune date de sortie du Charm n’a logiquement été annoncée.
Ce petit boîtier s’inscrit dans une stratégie plus large : multiplier les façons d’accéder à l’IA de Meta. Pendant la conférence, l’entreprise a également présenté de nouvelles lunettes connectées et des lunettes de réalité virtuelle. Elle prévoit aussi d’intégrer Muse à ses lunettes IA. Le Charm offrirait donc une autre option, pour ceux qui préfèrent garder leur assistant dans leur poche plutôt que sur leur nez. Meta y voit aussi un moyen de réduire sa dépendance à Apple ou Google qui, avec iOS et Android, ont un avantage concurrentiel sur les autres.
Un « Tamagotchi » qui doit travailler pour vous
Selon Bloomberg, l’appareil dispose d’un écran tactile OLED d’environ 2 pouces, soit 5 centimètres de diagonale, affichant un personnage Muse personnalisable (l’IA a un avatar chez Meta). Il embarque des microphones, des haut-parleurs, un port USB-C et une connexion 5G. Ses deux caméras, à l’avant et à l’arrière, doivent surtout permettre à l’IA d’analyser ce que vous lui montrez, même si elles peuvent également prendre des photos et des vidéos.
« Nous avons intégré toute l’expérience Muse, y compris la voix en temps réel et l’avatar, dans un objet qui tient sur un porte-clés et reste toujours disponible pour vous parler », a expliqué Mark Zuckerberg sur scène. Pour lancer une conversation, il suffit de toucher le capteur d’empreintes situé dans un coin du boîtier, sans déverrouiller son téléphone ni ouvrir une application. « Si vous ne portez pas de lunettes, ce sera de loin le moyen le plus rapide de parler à votre Muse et de lui montrer ce qui se passe autour de vous », promet le patron de Meta.
Ce compagnon rappelle forcément le collier de Friend.com, dont les publicités avaient fait polémique jusque dans le métro parisien. Friend vend cependant surtout une présence, un « ami » numérique qui écoute son environnement et envoie des messages sur le téléphone. Meta mise davantage sur les services rendus, même si son avatar contribue, lui aussi, à personnifier l’IA.
Meta et OpenAI cherchent une place à côté du smartphone
Pourquoi transporter un appareil supplémentaire pour utiliser une IA déjà accessible sur son téléphone ? Meta parie sur un accès plus immédiat. L’entreprise y gagne aussi une relation plus directe avec ses utilisateurs, moins dépendante des plateformes mobiles d’Apple et de Google.
Meta n’est d’ailleurs pas seul à vouloir donner à son IA un appareil dédié. OpenAI travaille également sur des produits avec Jony Ive, l’ancien patron du design d’Apple. Leur forme reste à confirmer : des informations publiées en juillet évoquaient notamment une enceinte connectée pour discuter avec ChatGPT. Une première présentation est attendue cette année, pour une commercialisation qui pourrait intervenir en 2027.
Face à ces entreprises qui cherchent une place à côté du smartphone, Apple défend au contraire son rôle central. Lors de sa keynote du 9 septembre, John Ternus a présenté l’iPhone comme un « intelligent personal hub », un centre personnel intelligent. Son argument est que l’IA rend le téléphone encore plus utile lorsqu’elle relie notre contexte personnel aux applications, services et appareils du quotidien. On peut y lire une réponse à ces nouveaux gadgets : pourquoi chercher ailleurs ce que l’iPhone dans votre poche pourrait déjà accomplir ?
Le Muse Charm devra le justifier à l’usage, et son prix pèsera dans la réponse. Aucun tarif n’a été annoncé, même si des sources de Bloomberg évoquent un montant comparable à celui d’une montre connectée. Le coût de la connexion mobile reste également à préciser.
Le calendrier reste lui aussi ambitieux. « Nous n’en avons construit que quelques exemplaires pour l’instant », a reconnu Mark Zuckerberg. Les matériaux de finition et l’agencement des composants doivent encore être finalisés, mais Meta prévoit des appareils « prêts à être expédiés pour les fêtes de décembre ».

articles.title: Vicarius launches ScriptAI to write fixes for flaws with no vendor patch - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Vicarius launches ScriptAI to write fixes for flaws with no vendor patch
Vulnerability remediation company Vicarius Inc. today launched an artificial intelligence engine that writes detection and remediation scripts for software flaws with no vendor patch available.
ScriptAI is aimed at the gap between a public disclosure and a working fix. Mean time to exploit stood at negative eight hours as of July on Zero Day Clock data cited this month by Radware Ltd. The same measure gave defenders 53 days in 2024.
Vicarius calls the result a capacity problem rather than a discovery one. Its announcement names Anthropic PBC’s Claude Mythos and Google LLC’s Big Sleep agent as evidence of how quickly machines now surface exploitable code. The fixes still have to be written, the company said.
ScriptAI sits inside the company’s vRx platform. When a vulnerability turns up with no vendor patch behind it, the engine drafts detection and remediation logic, and Vicarius researchers check that logic before anything runs. The platform then executes the script and verifies the result on affected machines. Vicarius said the sequence takes under an hour, against weeks for the same work done by hand.
A deterministic judge issues the pass or fail verdict, the company said, with no language model in the decision path. Each validated case ships with a cryptographically signed evidence manifest. Customers can verify it themselves. Scripts run a pre-check, apply the fix, then verify it and roll back on failure, so a breaking change is caught before it reaches production.
“Finding ten times more vulnerabilities is meaningless if remediation still happens through tickets, manual research and weeks of engineering work,” said Roi Cohen, co-founder and chief executive of Vicarius. “If AI can find the vulnerability, AI should help build the protection.”
Vicarius has done a version of this before. The vuln_GPT model arrived in August 2023, billed as the first trained specifically to write remediation scripts, and its output went out free through the company’s vsociety community. The verification step is what ScriptAI adds.
Everything the engine writes lands in the vScript library under a ScriptAI label. The scripts run as native Bash and PowerShell at the operating system level, with no additional agents or proprietary rule formats.
ScriptAI becomes the fourth path in what Vicarius calls True Remediation. Patching runs through vPatch. When no patch is available, vShield protects the workload, and vScript holds custom and community-sourced remediation scripts.
The new service is available to vRx customers starting today. Vicarius has built remediation tooling out of New York and Tel Aviv since 2016, and Bright Pixel Capital led a $30 million Series B round for the company in January 2024.

articles.title: Begin at the End: How to Enable Agentic Remediation
articles.text:
There is a corporate mandate to implement AI enablement programs. In cybersecurity, integrating AI chatbots into dashboards is table stakes. The industry, and the organizations it serves, must evolve to adopt agentic AI.
But true autonomy isn’t just about moving faster – it’s about changing the goalpost entirely. The ultimate objective is Shift Zero: eliminating vulnerability backlogs entirely and preventing exposure at the source. To achieve this, the best place to begin is the end.
Continuous threat exposure management (CTEM) is a framework to discover and remediate threats and exposures. The final step of this framework, mobilization, is the operational endpoint. Until now, this has remained a time-consuming manual process.
Automation has historically been focused on discovery, prioritization, and validation. By inverting the traditional CTEM framework to focus on automating remediation, organizations can close the loop on exposure management.
The final frontier for CTEM
Every security team that tries to find and fix its exposures experiences the same lifecycle. You decide what matters. You find out what’s in your environment. You plan your work. You test your plan. You operationalize.
This sequence is the CTEM framework: scoping, discovery, prioritization, validation, and mobilization.
The first half of this framework is diagnostic. Scoping defines assets and the attack surface, in relation to their business impact. This is a mostly manual process that relies on human discernment.
Discovery is also diagnostic. Finding out what exists used to be the hard part. Organizations used to rely on static asset inventories, which were maintained in spreadsheets. Scanning is now continuous and automated.
Likewise, prioritization is diagnostic, and it has also been enhanced with automation over the past several years. For a long time, organizations relied on a common vulnerability scoring system (CVSS) to determine the severity of a vulnerability.
Now solutions prioritize vulnerabilities based on whether an exploit for a vulnerability exists in the wild, a compensating control protects an exposure, and the business impact of the assets. Processing all of these variables is an ideal use case for machine learning.
The other half of the framework is action. Validation is the process of confirming that prioritized exposures are exploitable and that controls actually stop attacks. Over the past five years, attack simulation, penetration testing, and adversarial validation have also become increasingly automated.
The final step, mobilization, is where there is the most opportunity to embrace automation. Mobilization operationalizes insights across people and processes.
When you get to this step, the automation stops. Someone opens a ticket.That ticket gets passed across teams, delayed by change windows, negotiated, batched, and occasionally closed without ever being fixed.
We have built an extraordinary solution for producing perfectly prioritized and rigorously validated findings, but the fix still requires manual processes.
CTEM was designed to bring order to exposure management, but manual mobilization has kept security teams trapped in a reactive cycle. Shift Zero flips this paradigm. Instead of managing an ever-growing number of findings, Shift Zero embeds autonomous remediation directly into the operational flow. It takes us from “we found a problem, now let’s fix it” to eliminating the window of risk altogether.
Enabling mobilization with agentic remediation
Agentic remediation is not an act of faith. We are talking about fixing known problems, not judgment calls about unfamiliar risk. An agent applying a known patch to a known asset is executing a decision that has already been made.
We can turn to supervisory control theory, which dictates how human operators control machines they cannot micromanage. This school of thought is responsible for a widely discussed distinction: human in the loop versus human on the loop.
Human in the loop means that agents wait for approval. Agents gather context, determine a fix, stage the change, and stop. A human approves or rejects the fix. The agent does the legwork, while the human supplies the decision.
Human on the loop means that the agent acts and reports. The agent executes its tasks within a defined scope, and a person supervises its output through dashboards and alerts, rather than reviewing individual actions. The human sets policy, and the agent handles the volume.
The natural way to divide work between the two is by the risk score you already produce. Prioritized exposure management rankings are a stronger signal than CVSS severity scores. Use human review on high-risk findings; build confidence in agentic automation with low-risk findings.
Security leaders are reluctant to let an unsupervised agent act on their most impactful exposures, and for good reason. AI systems continue to act in ways that are difficult to anticipate. The fear is that an agent applies a solution that causes further harm.
To allay that concern, agents should operate inside a constrained action space: apply patches from an approved set, modify specific configuration parameters, isolate a segment, and open a ticket for anything else. Destruction isn’t a decision because it isn’t in the vocabulary. Bounding is what makes autonomy safe.
Two more guardrails matter. Every action needs a rollback plan, and approval paths need to be standardized before they’re automated. If ownership of asset classes is ambiguous today, an agent amplifies that ambiguity at machine speed.
Next, rehearse the failure. Prepare tabletop exercises to practice an agent patching the wrong host at the wrong hour. Find out who notices, who has the authority to stop it, and how long it takes. Those lessons are better learned in a conference room than a production environment.
In the future, the promise of agentic remediation is even more ambitious: self-healing networks, or networks that monitor their own telemetry, model normal behavior, and isolate anomalies autonomously.
CTEM is supposed to be a closed-loop lifecycle. Discovery, prioritization, and validation have been running at machine speed for years, but mobilization has been a manual process, which means the loop gets left open.
Agentic remediation is where the mandate to adopt AI meets a problem worth solving. The exposures are already found, ranked, and validated. What remains is the fixing. Begin at the end, close the loop, and Shift Zero becomes operational reality.

articles.title: Ce vidéoprojecteur en promo à moins de 400 € est une pépite : Google TV, Dolby Audio et image Full HD jusqu'à 300 pouces — Frandroid
articles.text:
Avec le Wanbo X7 Pro Max, vous avez un sérieux candidat pour remplacer le téléviseur de votre salon. Ce n’est pas donné à tous les vidéoprojecteurs, notamment à cause de la luminosité, mais ici elle est suffisamment élevée pour faire le travail. Alors vous ne pourrez peut-être pas l’utiliser en plein jour, mais au moins il ne faudra pas attendre l’obscurité complète pour en profiter. Grâce à une promotion temporaire sur Amazon, il bénéficie de 90 euros de réduction jusqu’au 2 octobre.
Les atouts du Wanbo X7 Pro Max
- Sa luminosité annoncée à 1 500 lumens ANSI, un niveau rare à ce prix
- L’interface Google TV basée sur Android 14 avec les principales applications de streaming
- Le son Dolby Audio de 20 watts pour se passer d’enceinte externe dans de nombreuses situations
Jusqu’au 2 octobre, le vidéoprojecteur Wanbo X7 Pro Max est disponible sur Amazon pour 389,99 euros au lieu de 479,99 euros.
Un projecteur Full HD lumineux et bien équipé
Le Wanbo X7 Pro Max est un vidéoprojecteur Full HD abouti qui brille principalement par sa luminosité annoncée à 1 500 lumens ANSI. Avec lui, vous pouvez envisager une image confortable entre 80 et 120 pouces. Wanbo recommande de rester entre 40 et 180 pouces, même s’il annonce pouvoir pousser jusqu’à 300 pouces. Mais à ce niveau-là, l’image risque de ne pas être de qualité égale partout, donc il vaut mieux se contenter d’une taille plus raisonnable. L’image est compatible HDR10 avec un MEMC qui fluidifie les scènes rapides, mais ça reste de la Full HD native. Il accepte les sources 4K (d’où la mention « 4K » sur certaines fiches Amazon), sans les afficher en 4K. Quant au HDR, il ne rivalise pas avec les TV haut de gamme ou les vidéoprojecteurs laser.
Malgré ses atouts, le Wanbo X7 Pro Max a les limites typiques de sa catégorie. La netteté des bords se dégrade s’il est placé de biais ou que la correction trapézoïdale est sollicitée. L’automatisation de l’image (autofocus, ajustement automatique et évitement d’obstacles) simplifie la mise en route mais peut nécessiter une retouche manuelle. La connectique est simple avec un seul port HDMI 2.1, un port USB-A et une sortie jack 3,5 mm. Son format est imposant, avec 284 x 284 x 151 mm pour 4,1 kg. Il reste maniable, mais se prête moins à un usage réellement nomade.
Google TV fluide et son Dolby Audio convaincant
Côté logiciel, le Wanbo X7 Pro Max tourne sous Google TV (Android 14), avec une puce MediaTek MT9660, 2 Go de RAM et 32 Go de stockage. Avec ça, la navigation dans les menus est fluide, l’accès aux plateformes de streaming est simplifié et Google Cast permet de diffuser directement le contenu de votre smartphone. La télécommande permet d’utiliser les commandes vocales et il y a des raccourcis vers plusieurs applications. Il profite du Wi-Fi bi-bande 2,4/5 GHz, ainsi que du Bluetooth 5.0 pour connecter un casque, des écouteurs ou encore une barre de son.
Le Wanbo X7 Pro Max embarque aussi deux haut-parleurs de 10 watts chacun, compatibles Dolby Audio, qui délivrent un son équilibré pour un vidéoprojecteur. Bon, le rendu ne remplace pas une barre de son. Pour une vraie immersion audio, il faudra en brancher une, idéalement sur le port HDMI 2.1 compatible eARC. En l’état, ça dépanne. Aussi, vous pouvez utiliser le Wanbo X7 Pro Max comme enceinte Bluetooth, avec la projection désactivée, pour écouter de la musique sans faire fonctionner inutilement la lampe. Enfin, le support fourni s’incline de ±15° pour orienter correctement l’image, ce qui simplifie l’installation.
